I found two not very bright brothers in a cellar of their house. They seemed to be talking about some sinister plan.
They were planning to destroy the great dam of Brimhaven. They just could not agree how they would do it.
They asked me to help them.
I have agreed to destroy the dam for them.
The brothers gave me a hand axe that could weaken the dam in a vulnerable place.
I took another hand axe. This time I shouldn't lose it.
I found the weak spot in the dam and started hacking at the wood.
Water came pouring through the hole in the dam. A lot of water!
I refused to destroy the dam for the brothers.
Given what I overheard, I was not allowed to leave. The two brothers attacked me.
Someone else destroyed the dam and water came pouring through a hole in the dam. A lot of water!
The Brimhaven guards have informed me that I may not leave the town until they have investigated who destroyed the dam.
I have promised to track down the real perpetrators. However, I still cannot leave the town.
The two brothers did not know their boss's name, but he seemed to have a lot of gold.
The rich man living up on the hill of Brimhaven seemed to know more than he admitted.
The rich man boasted that he had been bribed by an important man in Loneford to sabotage the dam.
I gave the letters as a piece of evidence to the captain of the guard. Now it is up to them to deal with the rich man.
The dam is very important to Brimhaven. It should be repaired.

Stebbarik was ill at home in bed. He could not work and feared that he would lose his job. Because of his high debts, he feared that Gnossath would then take his house away.
I have offered to do the work for Stebbarik.
Gnossath has asked me to carry 25 heavy boulders from the stock to the dam.
I have carried the first boulder to the dam.
I have carried 5 boulders to the dam.
I have moved 10 boulders.
I have moved 15 boulders. This work is exhausting!
Only a few to go...
Finally - that was the last boulder! Gnossath was very pleased with my work.

If I can find the gem he can remount it in the dagger, and the dagger will have special properties. Apparently it used to belong to someone named Lawellyn.

If I can find the dagger he can remount the gem, and the dagger will have special properties. Apparently it used to belong to someone named Lawellyn.

I found Hettar, a tough boy about my age, on top of Blackwater mountain. He kept calling for a certain Norry.
Hettar's little dog Norry has run away. He was very anxious to find him. I promised to get Norry back.
Hettar has given me a piece of Norry's favorite food.
I have offered Hettar's piece of Wyrm meat to Norry, who took it eagerly.
Norry ran off to reunite with Hettar.
Hettar thanked me a thousand times for my help in finding Norry.
I explained to Hettar that I killed Norry. Hettar broke down on the floor in agony.
I met old man Bogsten in his cabin. He was sick after encountering a giant mushroom and wanted me to go see the potion merchant in Fallhaven to get a cure.
The potion merchant needed four spore samples to prepare the cure. I should go back to see Bogsten.
Bogsten gave me the key to his backyard. I should go to the mushroom cave from there and collect the spore samples.
I opened Bogsten's backyard door.
I showed Bogsten the spores. Now I should go back to see the potion merchant.
The potion merchant gave me the cure. I should give it to Bogsten now.
Bogsten was cured.
Bogsten said evil forces in his cave were preventing him from working. He asked me to check his cave and gave me his necklace.
I met an old sorcerer named Zuul'khan in the cave. He told me Bogsten's family imprisoned him using an ancient petrifying spell, but thanks to Bogsten's laxity, he was now free.
He wanted me to kill Bogsten and bring him Bogsten's staff.
I decided to slay Zuul'khan.
I defeated Zuul'khan, but he was not dead. He disappeared into the ground.
I told Bogsten about what happened.
Bogsten remembered the petrifying spell. This time he would make sure that Zuul'khan cannot come back. He gave me a bag of mushrooms and told me I should take them to the potion merchant.
Zuul'khan seems to have moved away from Bogsten's caves to another hiding place.
The potion merchant said that these were very rare mushrooms. He prepared two "Underground Fighter" potions for me. He would sell me some more if I came back.
Zuul'khan's offer seemed interesting. I have to go kill Bogsten.
I decided to keep Bogsten's staff for myself, so I had to kill Zuul'khan.
I defeated Zuul'khan, but he was not dead. He disappeared into the ground.
I gave Bogsten's staff to Zuul'khan.
He rewarded me with permanent immunity to Spore Infection.
I got through the black fog.
I got through the black fog again after a fight with Zuul'khan.
And a third time.
After another fight with Zuul'khan I got through the black fog again.
I overpowered Zuul'khan one more time, but this time the black fog wouldn't go away. Obviously I can't get past the fog that way.
I defeated Zuul'khan one last time and the black fog was gone for good. I must find and destroy the fungi leader.
I defeated the giant mushroom, Zuul'khan's fungi leader.

A young girl named Lediofa emerged after my battle with the mushroom. She told me how Zuul'khan captured her as food for the mushroom. She seemed to have been poisoned just like Bogsten, so I directed her to see the Fallhaven potioner.

I met Lediofa at the potions shop in Fallhaven. She couldn't afford to pay the potioner for a mushroom poison cure, so I gave her the gold she needed. In return, she offered her family's hospitality if I ever come to visit in Nor City.

Down in a hole, in the mountain side near Prim, I found signs of a heinous torture. At least three corpses were there. I felt the urge to get out of there as fast as I could and immediately report what I found to someone in the village.
A mysterious looking guy suddenly appeared in my way when I was headed to report to the guards. He has recommended that I should not tell them anything.
I ignored the advice of the strange guy that I almost stumbled over. I must see some guards.
Somehow, a Feygard general and his men reached Prim. They are kind of extorting the people in charge to get full control of Elm mine.
The man in charge is not willing to listen to me. He says he has more important things to deal with. Maybe the guy I met earlier was right.
A Feygard general and two of his henchmen appeared. What are they up to?
Ehrenfest is uneasy. He said we must meet in Elm mine, west of prim. We should talk no more about this inside the village.
Ehrenfest told me his story, and why he knew about what I saw on the mountain side, but he didn't dare to go down the hole.
I explained to Ehrenfest the horrible scene, and showed him proof of the torture. Poor guys...
I must ask the villagers about Lorn and his partners, maybe I can gather some useful information from the common gossip.
It seems Lorn was a regular client of the tavern. I should ask there.

One of the tavern regulars, possibly Lorn's old partner Jern, does not believe that Lorn's death was an accident, maintaining Lorn had been climbing the mountains for longer than he could remember. However, he does not feel comfortable to continue the conversation.
Lorn's old partner asked me to bring a large bottle of cool water from the streams that are down the hole east of Prim. I bet it is the same hole I've been down earlier.
I've collected enough water. Time to leave this dark place.
I brought the cold water to Lorn's old partner. He seems to be better, and is less intoxicated.
Jern doesn't know anything about a missing couple. How can a member of Lorn's crew ignore the mission of his group? Again, something does not fit. I should visit Ehrenfest again.
I decided to solve this situation myself, as Ehrenfest proved not to be trustworthy enough.
Despite Ehrenfest's ostensible lies, I decided to give him a second chance.
It's settled. Ehrenfest and I will reach Blackwater Settlement and stop General Ortholion's evil plan.

I've found a severely wounded woman inside a mountain cabin. She claims to have been suddenly attacked by a group of wyrms. Ortholion and the other scout left her resting and departed to Blackwater Settlement.
I killed the mountain scout that was taking refuge in the old cabin up in the mountain.
I talked again with Jern. Maybe the guards will be more reasonable if he leads the conversation instead of me.
It seems Ehrenfest lied to me more than once. He's probably connected with the missing people and Lorn's death. I must find General Ortholion and warn him about Ehrenfest.
One of the general's henchmen attacked me without provocation. There was something wrong with her. Better hurry up and meet with the Feygard general.
Ehrenfest revealed his true intentions, but fled before getting surrounded. He told me he will be waiting for General Ortholion in the Elm mine.

After a brief conversation with the general, he left Blackwater settlement in a rush to reach Elm mine. He seemed really worried about the mine, so he asked me to warn his soldiers, settled south of Prim.
I reported to the general's henchmen about his plans. Now, I should hurry to the Elm mine.

Once in the mine I saw corpses and collapsed tunnels. I tried to go another way and reached some more tunnels. Fortunately, they were not collapsed, but there was something strange there that scared even the venomfangs. Something evil.

One of the unexploited areas of the mine had a walled up passage and lots of those strange glowing gems. They seem to consume living beings to grow and bring life to inanimated things or corpses. I must be very careful.

It was true! That strange glowing material is alive. I should be extremely cautious; it seems to be able to engulf living beings. I found the last of Ortholion's henchman alive. He has gone back to search for reinforcements. I hope they are better than those who dared to enter here.
I ended up trapped on a one-way path deep in a cavern below the Elm mine. General Ortholion is blocking the only way to escape for Ehrenfest. This is his end.
Ehrenfest reversed the situation using some kind of magic, seemingly unknown even to himself.
Ehrenfest escaped again! General Ortholion is unconscious and the reinforcements haven't shown up yet...
Kamelio, who was no longer a human being, tried to kill both the general and me, but we survived. Better get out of this cavern as soon as possible.
I got back to the Elm mine dining room. Despite saving the general's life he's not eager to reward me. Maybe I should try again later when we are both more settled.
After arriving back at a safer place, General Ortholion asked me a question. "What is most important to you?" I need to think about it before giving him my reply.
For my bravery, General Ortholion rewarded me with a lot of gold and told me to meet him in a couple of days.
For my bravery (and my greediness), General Ortholion rewarded me with a lot of...junk. He might pay me better next time if I meet him in some days.
For my bravery (and my lack of honor), General Ortholion rewarded me with a small bag of gold. He may have some news for me in a couple of days.

For my bravery and sense of honor, General Ortholion gave me a beautiful necklace, a symbol of his gratitude towards me. He also told me to come back in a few days, when I should ask him about all the events that have happened.
For my bravery and... ignorance?, General Ortholion gave me a few days to rest and urged me to come back soon after that.

I have found a jeweled key that looks like it might be for the diary. Time to try it.
The key unlocked the diary. The final entry did not really give an answer, except that he intended to go to either Nor City or Feygard, but had yet to decide which. Perhaps I will meet him some day.

I accepted his offer to apprentice with him.

In order to imprison the released prisoners again, I should call the demon guard by throwing an Oegyth crystal into the abyss.

I declined the offer to become his apprentice.
Kotheses attacked me.
I told the prisoners that I had killed their torturer. Now they could get peace.

I ordered the demons to watch over the prisoners.

The island west of Remgard was inhabited by centaurs who were very angry about your visit. They told me to seek out their leader, Thalos. He should be in the northeast of the island.
I have met Thalos.
He ordered me to slay a foul creature that hides in a cave on the hills of Laeroth Island, because the centaurs can't enter it.
In the cave entrance I have met Algangror, who asked for help.
In a cave entrance I have met Jhaeld of Remgard, who asked for help.
A common friend would be trapped deeper in the cave and I should free him.
Down in the cave I have found my brother Andor, locked in a room with no doors or other entrances.

To open an entrance I had to find the four scrolls of elements and the three color globes. These were hidden all over the island.
The scrolls and globes would need to be properly placed around Andor's golden prison.
The wall opened and gave access to the interior of the room.
With an intense sound, the wall built up again. I've been locked up!
The only way out was down a staircase, which, however, seemed to be magically secured.
The only way out was down a staircase, which, however, seemed to be magically secured.
It was no problem going downstairs, but something was wrong there.
The whole thing was just a big scam to lure me into this cave to serve Dorhantarh as dinner.
The moment I placed the Scroll of Fire on the table, it exploded. At the same time the wall opened again.
I brought the monster's heart to Thalos and told him that the danger has been averted. He was impressed and relieved at the same time.
Since then I have been a welcome guest of the centaurs.

On the road to Feygard I have met a boy named Tobby. He is looking for his brother Sobby.
I have promised to help Tobby get past the kobolds to the south.
I have killed the rat in Tobby's garden.
I gave Tobby a loaf of bread for his father.
Tobby has followed me to the beginning of the ravine with the kobolds.
Tobby has made it through the ravine.
Tobby followed me further to the south.
I have attacked poor Tobby, but he ran away. Now he will never find his brother.
We have parted. Tobby was sure now to find his brother.
I have met Tobby again, together with Sobby in the little village in the woods.
At the Wexlow well, I angered something evil and powerful (named Gamjee, I think) to the point that it pulled me down into the well. I've landed at the well's bottom severely injured, but alive.
After I landed with a thud at the bottom of the well and being concussed, I began to hear sounds off in the distance. Were they voices? Were they even real? Maybe a symptom of the concussion perhaps?

After I landed with a thud at the bottom of the well and being concussed, I began to hear sounds off in the distance. Were they voices? Were they even real? Are they the voices of something more sinister?
The voices I thought I heard earlier seem to be persistent and seemed to be getting louder. It was hard to tell if they're real or just a figment of my imagination.
Deep inside the well's tunnels, I found eight people being held captive inside a very deep pit.
I learned that these people are held captive by a troll and they need me to find a way to free them.
I met the troll named Gamjee and listened to what he had to say.
In an attempt to help Gamjee and the villagers, I have facilitated a conversation between Gamjee and one of the villagers.
I killed Gamjee and in doing so, I found a rope that I think might be helpful in freeing those people in that pit.
I killed Gamjee and in doing so, I realized that I really should go investigate the voices I heard earlier.
The villagers have been freed. I should visit them back in their village of Wexlow.
The villagers and Gamjee agreed to a schedule for using the well, ensuring everyone has access to water without conflict. But the villagers are still in the pit.
After the villagers and Gamjee agreed to a compromise, Gamjee gave me a rope and instructed me to use it to free the remaining villagers in the pit.
I've visited the people of Wexlow Village after they made it home. They are happy to sleep in their own beds now.
Philippa, one of the lovely Feygard loyalist ladies from Wexlow that I rescued from Gamjee the troll has informed me that she is a master baker.
Philippa has educated me about what a "Feydelight" is.
In return for my helping to rescue Philippa, she's stated that she could make a "Feydelight" for me if I provide her with all of the ingredients necessary to bake one.
I need to find dough, two eggs, wine, butter, honey and five Feygard fig fruits. I can find the figs in Feygard, but maybe I could find some along the Duleian Road too?
She told me that I can find the dough in Brightport or Feygard, but I could find a baker in just about any town.
Philippa told me that I can get honey from a beekeeper. But where to find one?
I gave Philippa all the ingredients needed to bake the Feydelight. Now I just need to come back later.
I have received my Feydelight from Philippa.

I met Arensia in Fallhaven. She is being taunted by lytwings while she slumbers. I agreed to help get rid of the mischevious creatures. I should talk to Rigmor to find out more, she lives north of the tavern.
Rigmor told me that lytwings live near large rings of mushroom growth, I should look for these in the forest surrounding Fallhaven.
I have to take a gift of two red apples and two strawberries before I can talk to the lytwings. They cast some kind of spell on me for not bringing them these fruit, it made me feel very tired.
The lytwings accepted my gift, and I can now talk with them.
I offered my help to the lytwings in exchange for leaving Arensia alone. They are considering my request. I should check in with them shortly, to hear their decision.
The lytwings asked that I chop down a gnarly old tree that is inside their mushroom ring. They insisted that I use an iron axe because the cursed bark of the tree cannot be cut by other tools.
I was about to swing my axe, when the lytwings stopped me. They have changed their minds about chopping down the tree. I am beginning to think they are indecisive on purpose.
The lytwings want four bottles of mead. I can probably find some at the Fallhaven tavern.

They took the mead, and turned around saying they want something else. I can now see why Rigmor said they are full of mischief! But I have no other choice but to continue this fool's errand if I want to help Arensia.
I have to find twelve wild flowers for the lytwings. I wonder where I could find those. Perhaps Arensia will know.
They accepted the flowers, and as expected, said they want something else! How many more times will they make me run around?
The lytwings want a token of Arensia's promise that she will not to pick their mushrooms again. I sense they are not playing another prank this time, they seemed intent about this task.
Arensia made a promise to her mother's ring, and then she gave it to me. I should take it to the lytwings at once.
I gave Arensia's ring to the lytwings. Just when I thought it was done, they said they need something else! I am waiting on their decision.
The lytwings have agreed to stop taunting Arensia. I should go tell her.
Arensia was elated to hear that the lytwings will no longer taunt her.
I could not take the absurd errands any more. I am no longer helping Arensia with her lytwing problem.
I lied to Arensia's and kept her mother's ring for myself.
Arensia gave me her magical promise ring as reward for helping her.
I went to the Thieves' Guild in Fallhaven looking for things to do.
Since I had helped Defy, Umar and Nanath threw me out. I cannot enter the basement again.
Since I had looted the Thieves' Guild vault after killing Defy, Umar and Nanath threw me out. I cannot enter the basement again.
I met Nanath, who's scared and upset, because someone put a spell on all members of the Thieves' Guild. This spell made all thieves noticeable. He asked me if I could help dispel the spell.
Nanath told me to find the Shadow priest who had cast the spell on the Guild.
I set out interviewing Shadow priests to find who had cast the spell.
Talion, Shadow priest of Loneford, had cast the Striking Spectacle Shadow spell on the Guild, on payment from Dameni, a mysterious lady leading a band of toughs
Talion could dispel the spell, using a few items - Villain's ring, Troublemaker's ring, ring of backstabbing, Tears of the Shadow potion, Luthor's ring.  He also wanted 50000 gold.
I have informed Nanath about the Striking Spectacle Shadow spell and Talion's demands.
Nanath told me Thieves' Guild would give me the 50000 gold back when I have got the spell dispelled.
Nanath asked if I had already found Luthor's ring.
I went back to Nanath as I couldn't find Luthor's ring anywhere.
He told me to seek out Fanamor's friend Sly Seraphina near the Sutdover bridge.
Seraphina didn't believe me. She told me to go away.
Nanath sent me to Umar. He should make sure Sly carries out the order.
Umar told me one of his secret passwords to convince Seraphina.

Sly Seraphina said that Luthor's ring was to be found in the cave which Crackshot tried to open. The door was sealed by Umar and Seraphina to prevent monsters in that cave from devastating Dhayavar. The sealing was done by using Luthor's items. She and Umar decided to separate them, and keep them separate.
Seraphina felt that the danger was too high to open that door. So she disappeared.
I had to find Sly Seraphina again.
Nanath told me to look for her in her usual hiding places: Near one of the towns Sullengard, Stoutford, Vilegard, Prim, Loneford, or Brimhaven.
Talion said that without the items he asked for he couldn't help. I had to find Seraphina.
After beating the tough guys protecting Seraphina, she was convinced that I was strong enough to help her beat the monsters in the cave.
Seraphina gave me back the money she had stolen from me earlier.
I have to ask Umar for Luthor's key.
I have got the key.
Seraphina agreed to help me and told me to meet her at the locked door in the cave where Crackshot was defeated.
I met Seraphina at the cave door where Crackshot was defeated.
Seraphina could open the door with Luthor's key wearing also his gloves. She entered the cave behind the door.
I followed her.
Seraphina got injured attacking one of the monsters.
I have killed the monsters blocking the entrance.
I healed Seraphina using potions.
I tried to poison Seraphina, but she noticed in time. At least she didn't notice that I did it on purpose.
Seraphina already started the search for the ring.
I searched the cave for Luthor's ring. I couldn't find it.
Sly Seraphina had found the ring. She gave it to me and told me to keep it safe. She disappeared again, probably back to Sutdover bridge. I had to go to Talion.
I gave 50000 gold, Villain's ring, Troublemaker's ring, ring of backstabbing, Tears of the Shadow potion, and Luthor's ring to Talion.
Talion used them to undo the spell.
Talion returned Luthor's ring. The other rings were broken in the process though and the Tears of the Shadow potion was used up of course.
The room with the dangerous creatures has been locked and sealed again.
Nanath gave me 75000 gold as a reward for a job well done.
Sly Seraphina was friendly to me - for now.

I met Miri in the Crossroads Guardhouse.
Since I had helped Ailshara, she wouldn't tell me about Andor.
Since I had hidden the truth about the bootlegging of beer from Sullengard, she wouldn't tell me about Andor.
Since I had aided Feygard once or twice earlier, she would tell me about Andor, after I had completed an investigation for her.
Since Miri was poisoned by slitherers near Sullengard, and healing is taking time, she wanted me to investigate something bad in the Purple Hills in the strange areas to the south of Stoutford.
I went to the area to the south of Stoutford and encountered an impassable force there.
There was a piece of Kazaul ritual there, which I had encountered before. I should inform Miri.
Miri asked me where I had seen this before. I told her about a task I had carried out on behalf of Throdna of the Blackwater settlement.
Miri told me to meet him and enquire further. And gave me a phrase to use whenever he started rambling.
Throdna told me it was part of a ritual to break the barrier which forms when one does a ritual to call strong Kazaul monsters.
The ritual consisted of two parts which I had found earlier, and a chant in a book called Calomyran Secrets. I need to report this to Miri.
I told Miri about finding the book for an Old Man in Fallhaven.  She told me to talk to him.
The Old Man would not let me borrow the book, so I started noting the chant in front of him.
The book contained half the chant. The rest was to be found in another book Azimyran Secrets.
Miri told me she'd trace the book. She told me to wait for her return.
Miri came back and told me that the book Azimyran Secrets was with an old hermit near Arulir mountain.
I met the old hermit and asked him about the book, Azimyran Secrets.
He refused to give it to me, so I copied the chant sitting with him. I needed to tell Miri.
Miri told me to hurry, and pass the barrier.
After destroying the ritual statue of Kazaul, beyond the barrier I found a crying woman.
She was performing a ritual that should bring her husband back to life.
Miri, who followed me, convinced the woman that it was actually an evil ritual to overrun Dhayavar with Kazaul's monsters.
The mourning woman told us that the ritual was given to her by a priest who walks on lava east of the Purple Hills.
We let the mourning woman go.
The mourning woman cried that she would never be happy again.
I had to travel to the lava wastelands.
There, after fighting monsters, I met a priest in red.
He accused me of interfering. Miri, who again followed me, revealed the red priest to be a monster.
I defeated the monster.
Miri fulfilled her promise and told me that Andor would be refilling his food supplies at Rosmara's food stand.
Indeed, I have found Andor there.
He told me he couldn't come home now, and vanished.
I met Borvis on the great road near Alynndir's hut.
Since I had told Gandoren about the switch of the weapons, and also the truth about the bootlegging of beer from Sullengard, he told me to leave.
Since I aided the Shadow once or twice earlier, he requested my further help for an urgent task.
He wanted me to investigate something bad in the Purple Hills in the weird areas to the south of Stoutford.
I went to the area to the south of Stoutford, and encountered an impassable force there.
There were strange glowing, immovable pebbles there. I had to inform Borvis.
Borvis told me that was the basic, but effective, Shadow shield, to protect Shadow incantations from outside interference.

For that, he would give me a chant. But I had to get him energies in the form of four 'blessings' - Shadow's Strength, Shadow Awareness, Fatigue, and Life Drain - within myself. He told me to go to Talion in Loneford for the first blessing, and for information about the others.
Talion bestowed me with Shadow's Strength.
Talion told me to seek out Jolnor in Vilegard for the rest of the 'blessings'.
Jolnor bestowed me with Shadow Awareness.
Jolnor told me to seek Favlon to the west of Sullengard for the remaining two.
I reached Favlon who asked me for 10 Cooked Meat.
I gave Favlon 10 Cooked Meat. He bestowed me with 'blessings' of Fatigue and Life Drain.
After a grueling travel back, I returned to Borvis.
Borvis removed the 'blessings' from me, and made a chant.
Borvis told me to hurry back to the barrier.
I passed the barrier.
After destroying the ritual statue of Kazaul, beyond the barrier I found a crying woman.
She was performing a ritual that should bring her husband back to life.
Borvis, who followed me, convinced the woman that it was actually an evil ritual to overrun Dhayar with Kazaul's monsters.
The mourning woman told us that the ritual was given to her by a priest in the lava wastelands.
We let the mourning woman go.
The mourning woman cried that she would never be happy again.
I had to travel to the lava wastelands.
There, after fighting monsters, I met a priest in red.
He accused me of interfering again and again. Borvis, who again followed me, revealed the red priest to be a monster.
I defeated the monster.
Borvis fulfilled his promise and told me that Andor would be refilling his supplies from Alynndir.
I ran to Alynndir's hut.
I found Andor there.
He told me he couldn't come home now, and vanished.

In the devastated lands south of Stoutford, I found an ominous stone etched with strange symbols.
As I touched its glowing mark, an unnatural chill ran through me, and I heard a voice in my mind, calling out for help. It spoke of torment and told me to return to Crossglen to find answers.
The presence of the mark grows unbearable. I feel an overwhelming pull to return to Crossglen. There is something wrong, and I sense it's tied to my father. I must hurry to see what's happening.
I spoke to father. He assured me he's fine, but mentioned Leta hasn't been herself lately. She's been pacing her home and muttering to herself. I should check on her and see what's going on.
When I confronted Leta, she seemed different--angrier, more agitated. As I pressed her, a dark spirit suddenly manifested before me and attacked.

I defeated the Dark spirit, but it didn't feel like the end. The Dark spirit trapped inside Leta has fled back to the devastated lands south of Stoutford, where its power can grow stronger. I need to return there and finish what I started.

In the depths of the devastated lands south of Stoutford, I found the dark spirit waiting for me. It was stronger this time, but I defeated it once and for all. Whatever bond it had with me and Leta is broken. I should check-up on Leta again.

I returned to Crossglen to find everything changed. Leta has aged decades in an instant. Her child is now fully grown, and her timid husband, Oromir, seems like a different man entirely. They remember nothing of what happened. The spirit may be gone, but its curse has left a permanent mark on the lives it touched.

I changed my mind and would keep these glittery things. They're too pretty to be destroyed.

I encountered Vaelric, a reclusive healer living in the swamp between Mt. Galmore and Stoutford. He refused to help me unless I dealt with a dangerous creature corrupting his medicinal pools.
I defeated the monstrous creature that I found on Vaelric's land. This creature was enormous and venomous, feeding on the lifeblood of the swamp.
Vaelric rewarded me for my efforts by teaching me how to use leeches to heal bleeding wounds. He warned me to save them for dire situations and respect their power.
I noticed that one of the Galmore grave plots looked to have been dug-up in the not-so-distant past. I should ask Vaelric about this.
I noticed that one of the Galmore grave plots looked to have been dug-up in the not-so-distant past.
After I mentioned to Vaelric that the graveyard near the Galmore encampment has a dug-up grave plot, he asked me to investigate it. I agreed to look for clues.
Just outside of the graveyard, I found a bell attached to a broken rope. It was partially buried and covered by grass, but I retrieved it.
I discovered a music box in the graveyard. It was partially buried and obscured by overgrown grass.
I discovered the skeletal remains of a human beneath a covering of grass and weeds. I wonder if it's related to why that grave plot is dug up?
I brought the bell and music box to the Galmore encampment and encountered a ghost named Eryndor that told me the items were his. I gave them to him in exchange for being "friends".
Eryndor told me his story and said he would leave Vaelric alone if I returned his ring. I should return to Vaelric.

Vaelric has told me his side of the story. He claimed that Eryndor came to him desperate, in a severe condition and Vaeltic said he did everything he could to save Eryndor's life. Thinking that Eryndor was dead, Vaelric buried him.
After hearing Eryndor's story, I decided that he has been wronged. I also agreed to get his ring back from Vaelric.
I informed Vaelric of the ghost's terms, and he agreed. He also gave me Eryndor's ring and now I should return it to Eryndor.
I've stolen the ring from Vaelric's attic.
I lied to Vaelric as I informed him that I was not able to find any clues surrounding the grave site or anywhere else.
I brought the ring back to Eryndor. Vaelric received no relief from the haunting.
I brought the ring back to Eryndor and he agreed to stop haunting Vaelric.
Vaelric rewarded me by offering to make Insectbane Tonics if I bring him the right ingredients.

I need to bring Vaelric the following ingredients in order for him to make his "Insectbane Tonic": five Duskbloom flowers, five Mosquito proboscises, ten bottles of swamp water and one sample of Mudfiend goo.
I brought the ring back to Eryndor just to tell him that I've decided to keep it.
When I refused to return the ring, Eryndor attacked me.
I defeated Eryndor and prevented the hauntings of Vaelric...for now, but I feel that they will resume someday.
Vaelric is now able to mix up some Insectbane tonic for me.

I've informed Vaelric that I defeated Eryndor but was not able to promise an end to the hauntings, Vaelric was dissatisfied with me and the outcome even going as far as saying that Andor is a better person than I am.

Eryndor has asked me to find Celdar, a woman from Sullengard and give her the mysterious music box because he has no need for it and it's the right thing to do. I think I remember hearing that name, "Celdar" somewhere. Eryndor stated that Celdar is intolerant of fools and petty trades and wears a garish purple dress.
In Sullengard, Maddalena informed me that Celdar was headed for Brimhaven, but may have stopped to rest along the way as it is a long trip to Brimhaven.
I gave Celdar the 'Mysterious music box' just as Eryndor had instructed and she gave me her longsword.
Inside a house in Brightport, I met two people named Dynes and Barthold. It turned out that they are the friends Benbyr told me to visit. Rather lacking in hospitality, they offered me work.
Barthold was hesitant because any job I could do for them would put me at odds with Gunfryk the guard commander. Taking that into account I offered to rid them of him.
I was told not to kill him, but surely it won't be a problem if I do. Either way I'll resolve things for them.
I received some records from silvear that could be useful as blackmail against Gunfryk.
I used the records to blackmail Gunfryk. To save his reputation he begrudgingly agreed to give Barthold and Dynes some leeway.
I lied to the commander that there are some lizardmen in the derelict house east of town, I should go there and prepare an ambush.
I ambushed and killed Gunfryk in the house to the east, along with the two guards he brought.
I informed the commander about Barthold and Dynes' scheme. He requested that I find some incriminating evidence of their role.
I found some of the duo's merchandise in the smuggling cave east of brightport.
I opted to blackmail the duo instead for some quick gold. Should've had the Guild's protection, suckers!
I told the commander I couldn't find anything
Barthold was disappointed in me for having done nothing about Gunfryk. Little did he know I lined my pockets with his merchandise.
Barthold was happy with my work and gave me a reward, he said I could find more work like this in Nor City.
Barthold was a little disappointed about me killing Gunfryk. It's possible that now Feygard might take more severe action with Brightport.
Gunfryk was happy with my work, the duo will soon be jailed. He said Feygard needs more brave youngsters like me and that I should give the military academy a try.
I gave the commander the blade, even though I already got paid not to. If there's any honor among Nor City's thieves, they will surely have none to spare for me.
I told the commander I couldn't find anything, even though I had the blade I blackmailed Barthold and Dynes with.
I arrived at Brightport's school, only to be told that Stanwick is not allowed visitors.
Janwick, Stanwick's grandfather, mistook me for Andor and asked me to deliver some fresh fruit to Stanwick.
I was allowed to visit Stanwick.
I learned that Stanwick is under investigation as the main suspect in the disappearance of an important scroll from the school library.
Stanwick has something important to tell me about Andor, but I must help him first.
I agreed to help Stanwick find the culprit responsible for the theft. I should look for clues around the school.
Milena, the school cook, told me that last year she noticed a dark figure sneaking off from the living quarters.
Dibella, the lady at the desk at the entrance, told me that Stanwick has a respectable reputation, but as the library supervisor he must be considered a suspect.
Oswald, the Headmaster, expressed his disbelief that Stanwick is guilty of the theft and accepted my help in finding the document, whilst insisting that it be returned to him.
Frederich, the history teacher who moved in from Feygard, believes Stanwick is associated with "Those Nor City savages" and was told by them to steal the document.
Franz, the math teacher, told me that the most logical thing to do is to investigate the library, which is sealed. I must find a way to access it.
I asked the Headmaster for access to the library, but he denied my request.
I stole the library key from the Headmaster's desk while he was distracted. Hopefully there will be no consequences.
Counterfeit, a thieves guild member in the basement of the Brightport warehouse, gave me a copy of the library key.
In the library's basement archive, I found a record of a baker named Bryma requesting to read the secret scroll, but she was denied. I should seek out her whereabouts.

Richimor, the old man sitting by the lake shore in Brightport, was an acquaintance of Bryma. He said she left Brightport many years ago and did not tell him where she went, but she left a large part of her research material at his house. I should check it.
Inside Richimor's house, I found a bundle of papers left by Bryma. In there, amongst the trivial writings, one paper stood out as it talked about four strange statues in the vicinity of Brightport.
I discovered a strange statue in the forest south of Brightport, with several indecipherable symbols. Perhaps this is one of the statues mentioned in the writings of Bryma.
I examined a statue north of Brightport. Carved into the statue were the symbols for the letters L and H.
I examined a statue southeast of Brightport. Carved into the statue were the symbols for the letters T and E.
I examined a statue far west of Brightport. Carved into the statue were the symbols for the letters A, G, and R.
The puzzle is proving itself to be very difficult. I should return to the library in Brightport to search for clues
I spoke the activation word to the statue in the forest, and can now move further.
Inside the forest was a cabin, in which I found Bryma and some strange creature made of bread.
I received the secret scroll from Bryma. I should return it to the headmaster now.
I threatened Bryma to make her hand over the scroll. She gave it to me as she did not intend to keep it anyway.
I returned the secret scroll to the Headmaster and Stanwick was cleared of all suspicion. I should inform him.
I did not receive any reward.
I received a reward from the Headmaster for having returned the scroll.
I informed Stanwick and he was relieved to hear the news.

I've started some work for Allares at the bakery in Brightport. He asked me to help Delon down in the storage area.
I spoke with Delon and he's a real slacker. He wants me to do all sorts of work, all by myself.
He told me to start by sweeping the floor, and to do that I must find a broom.
The floor's all swept. I did it all by myself. Delon's "help" was more of a nuisance.
No wonder it got so quiet. Delon disappeared to sleep on some sacks. And now I have a new task, to sift through some flour.
I've sifted through all of the flour.
One last errand. An apple delivery hasn't arrived. I should ask Allares about it.
Allares refuses to accept my help until I prove my capabilities by bringing him one piece of deer meat.
After bringing the deer meat to Allares, he accepted my help, I should speak to Eatloni outside.
According to Eatloni, the order of 30 apples never arrived. I should visit Deebo's Orchard to check if the order had been picked up.
I went to see Deebo at the orchard. Apparently the merchant sent by Eatloni already picked up the apples.
I found some half-eaten apples in the woods north of the Duleian road.
I found two crates of apples. One was intact, but the other was empty. Did the mountain cats attack the merchant for food to feed their cubs?
I paid for a new shipment out of my own pocket. Deebo promised to hurry his workers and get them picked quickly. I should receive them from the orchard supervisor.
I received the apples from Alduan.
I brought the apples back to Eatloni. He reimbursed me for half the cost. Time to let Allares know I'm done with everything.
I brought the apples back to Eatloni. Time to let Allares know I'm done with everything.
I completed all the tasks at the bakery.
Fiamma, the swordsmith of Brightport. Is willing to forge me a sword if I can bring him the materials.
In the mountains near the road to Remgard lies a dangerous area overrun by Arulirs, beasts with skin as tough as steel.
Fiamma has asked for a strip of Arulir skin, coveted for its durability and flexibility. He also requires 15 cold lava rocks from the mountain cave, which burn hotter than any ordinary coal.
The final material is a red crystal from a Gornaud, a ferocious beast that sometimes forms these rare crystals in its body.
I brought Fiamma the arulir skin and lava rocks.
I brought Fiamma the red crystal.
I gave all the materials to Fiamma. He thanked me and told me to come back later when it's finished.
To my surprise, the sword he forged heats up on contact with air and requires special gloves to handle. They are made of the Arulir skin I brought.
I asked Fiamma to give me something else, and he gave me a very sharp glaive.
I thanked Fiamma and went on my merry way.

The Thieves Guild was due to receive a package, but the guards in Brightport have been impeding their activities. They need a new face like me to pick the package up discretly. I was told to head east of the town.
I met the courier from Nor City inside the house.
Before we could conclude the meeting we heard the town guard making noise outside.
I received the package.
Thanks to some previous interactions I've had with the commander, I convinced the guards to let me go.
I couldn't fool the guards and got caught.
I managed to hide inside a crate and waited. Eventually, the guards left.
I delivered the package to Elysa, She was pleased with my work and said the Thieves Guild may have further opportunities for me in the future.
I lied to Gunfryk in a plot to kill him, and in the process the courier I was supposed to meet got arrested.
I failed to deliver the package to Elysa. She was not happy.
In the rundown mysterious basement behind Bryma's house, I encountered a humanoid green creature that fled beyond a pile of cave rubble.
When I questioned Bryma about the creature, she explained that lizardmen live in the caves beneath her house and have been bothering her for some time.
I agreed to help Bryma with her problem. She shared the activation phrase for another statue leading deeper into the forest.
After navigating through the caves, I reached an open chamber beyond the rubble, where I found the lizardman again.
The lizardman regarded me suspiciously, calling me an intruder. He claimed Bryma had been stealing bones from their ancestral tomb, which his people were trying to recover.
I attacked the lizardman, but my attack merely grazed it, before it fled deeper into the caves.
I tried to calm Emyro's worries. He hesitated but told me to visit their leader before disappearing into the shadows.
I tracked down and killed the lizardmen's leader, Elyzard.
I killed the rest of those slimy lizards. Bryma can now rest free.
I received a reward from Bryma for getting rid of the creatures.
To earn the trust of the tribe's leader, Elyzard. I swore to return the 13 stolen bones.
To my astonishment, I discovered that Bryma had ground the bones into dust for her research and fertilizer experiments.
Bryma suggested I retrieve replacement bones from other sources. She advised hunting the hostile red lizardmen in the nearby area until I could gather the required amount.
I delivered the bones to Elyzard, who acknowledged my effort but requested one more task. He instructed me to visit the Shadow Chaplain's cave for further guidance.
From Dominio, the Shadow chaplain, I learned that beasts of darkness were attacking the tribe from an ancient ruin on the western side of the cave.
To stop the attacks, I was tasked with destroying two crystals within the ruins by chanting the phrase "Kazaul thu'um kha'zan" before striking them.
I destroyed the first crystal.
I destroyed the second crystal.
Elyzard recognized my effort, and rewarded me with a trinbal artifact.
I offered the lizardmen a deal of cooperation to supply Bryma with animal bones as a sign of mutual respect.
Bryma agreed to stop intruding on the lizardmen's tomb, as they promised to supply her with bones for her research.
Bryma agreed to stop intruding on the lizardmen's tomb.

quests.name: A map of the Great Lake Laeroth

stages.logText: The cartographer Thyrope Splathershed asked me to join an expedition to get the maps of Lake Laeroth completed.
I should get beeswax from Leofric the beekeeper to make earplugs.
On a paradisiacal island, A woman named Kalypso welcomed me and offered refreshment.
I took a single grape to try her food. It gave me an extraordinary boost to my vigor.
Kalypso gave me a tiny green key as a present.
I realized that I didn't have a desire to leave anymore.
Once the magic had worn off, I was able to leave the island again.
You met Circe, a strange, lonely woman who kept pigs in her kitchen.
We docked at an unknown island. Captain Burry and his men set off to replenish supplies.
The ship was abandoned. Something was strange about that Circe, I decided to question her.
I realized that the Captain and his crew had been turned into pigs, and I forced Circe to turn them back.
Impressed, Circe gave me a golden key as a parting gift.
We approached the Sirens' Reef. Many sailors have lost their lives here. Captain Burry refused to sail any further.
I distributed earplugs to the crew so that the sirens' songs could no longer harm them.
Then I put in earplugs too.
I had myself tied tightly to the mast so that I could hear what the sirens were singing without jumping overboard.
We have managed to passage by the Sirens' cliff.
I was exploring a cave on an island with just sheep, when suddenly the dwarvish cyclops Polyphem enters, together with a flock of sheep. Polyphem has locked the door behind him.
He and his brothers would eat me in the next days.
Polyphem fell onto his bed and immediatly began to snore. I should find a way to leave.
I made a strong soap solution.
And poured it directly into Polyphem's eye.
Polyphem let all the sheep out so he could more easily search the cave for me. As he did so, he felt each sheep's back and counted them.
I hung myself from the side of a strong sheep to let it pull me to freedom.
It worked! I've left the cave.
Scylla, the six headed monster, had attacked our ship.
We managed to defeat one of Scylla's monstrous heads. Rather than weakening her, however, this only seemed to make her more furious.
We managed to defeat another one of Scylla's monstrous heads. We better had not...
We were swept into the abyss of the maelstrom along with the ship.
At last we resurfaced again.
Looks like we had got the map of the great Lake Laeroth complete.
Thyrope Splathershed is happy to have the map complete now. He seemed to doubt my story though, but he allowed me to use the ship for my leisure.

Nocmar refused to forge heartsteel in his shop, fearing discovery by Geomyr's men. He revealed that he once owned a glowing white house south of Fallhaven, where a special forge still burns. That forge was the only place he ever worked heartsteel. But after falling into debt, he lost the house to Alkapoan. If Nocmar is to forge again, I must help him regain it.

Nocmar told me that Alkapoan holds the deed and key to the glowing white house. He said the forge within never dies, always blazing, ready for work. If I can reclaim the deed and key from Alkapoan, Nocmar will finally have his forge back.
Alkapoan scoffed when I mentioned Nocmar. He said the only way to reclaim the glowing white house is to pay him fifty thousand gold. Nothing else will satisfy him.
I told Alkapoan I wanted the glowing white house for myself. He agreed to sell it for forty thousand gold, but only if I first complete a task for him to prove my worth.

Alkapoan asked me to collect an overdue 'operation tax' of five thousand gold from a card dealer in the back room of Brimhaven's tavern. I'll need to go there and retrieve the gold for Alkapoan before he will sell me the deed to the white house for forty thousand.
I was able to collect the overdue 'operation tax' from the dealer and now I should return to Alkapoan.
After I paid Alkapoan, he gave me the deed and the key to the white house south of Fallhaven. I should bring them back to Nocmar.
I was able to finally give Nocmar back what was rightfully his...possession of his forge house.

I found the skeletal remains of an adventurer near the mining rails in Undertell. Among the remains were a history book titled "Undertell: Its Ghosts and History" and a necklace marked "Jewel of Fallhaven", which made me wonder if this man was from Fallhaven.
Ysrine suggested that the history of Undertell records what could be measured, but avoids the voices of those who suffered here.
I brought the book to Fallhaven. Arcir recognized it as a deliberate account of Undertell's past and asked me to return and listen for what the book omits.
In Undertell, I spoke with Brenor, an Elytharan ghost who still remembers himself and the weight of the mines.
I encountered an Elytharan cooker slave who spoke only of labor and routine, remembering work but not belief.
I earned the trust of a shy Elytharan ghost named Cora, who would only remain when I approached in silence.
The Elytharan ghosts each revealed a different truth: identity, labor and silence. I think Arcir would like to hear about this.
I returned to Arcir with what I learned about the Elytharan dead and the omissions in the history of Undertell.

Anoa told me that my presence in this cavern of Undertell had reawakened 11 shades of the Kha'zaan, who were dormant. I needed to eliminate them before they destroyed Dhayavar. It was their devotion to Kazaul which had preserved their existence till now.
I approached a Kha'zaan shade. But it was powerful enough to throw me out of the caverns and even out of Undertell. I needed to talk to Anoa.
Anoa told me to try again.
I again approached a shade. Again, I was thrown. Hope Anoa had a better alternative.
Anoa again told me to try harder.
Once more I was thrown out of the caverns the moment I approached a shade. This time, Anoa better help me in a smart way.
Anoa told me to pray to the statue of the Holy One in Sullengard square.
I prayed to the Holy One. I saw a ring at the foot of the statue.
I picked up the ring. I needed to get back to Anoa to learn how it works.
Anoa told me to wear it and approach the Kha'zaan shade.
A shade pleaded for mercy, promising a reward someday. I decided to let it go.
The shade claimed it was no monster at all and begged for freedom. I chose to release it.
The shade insisted it did not deserve destruction. I chose to free it.
A shade spoke of oppression and suffering rather than evil. I released it from its binding.
One shade swore it meant no harm and only wanted to be free. I granted its request.
A shade appealed to my compassion, asking for release instead of destruction. I let it go.
The shade asked for freedom. I allowed it to depart.
A shade promised gratitude if spared. I chose mercy and let it slip away.
The shade asked to be released. I loosened its hold on this place.
One of the shades spoke with unexpected clarity, begging for freedom. I gave it what it asked for.
A shade insisted it only wanted release, not destruction. I freed it from its lingering prison.
I had eliminated all the Kha'zaan shades and Anoa thanked me. As the 12th shade, one in redemption, eliminating the rest had freed him.

Anoa informed me that he could have been redeemed, but because I freed at least one of the Kha'zaan shades, this was not to happen. Thus he became a monstrous shade. He and all of the freed shades swarmed and attacked me.
I killed all the shades including Anoa. I did not get any reward.

The PC learned from an Undertell ghost that during the Rise of the Shadow, a cult of descendants of Kazaul priests calling themselves the Shadow, used hearsteel weapons to defeat the  Elytharan mages.
I asked Myrelis how to get the barricades to Undertell removed and he told me to meet his friend Shannal inside the beach-scene house.
I met Shannal and she said I had to prove myself before she would remove the barriers. She feared that I am not ready to enter Undertell.
Shannal gave me a special Traders' Guild bronze coin and asked me to show it to Benbyr north of Fallhaven.
A frightened Benbyr told me these coins were payments his ancestor received for kidnapping people to work in the mines of Undertell.
Benbyr asked me to help save him from Shannal.
Shannal told me she did not want to kill Benbyr. She wanted him to pay toward helping her descendant, the drunkard named Rain who sleeps outside the Fallhaven Tavern.
Shannal asked me to help cure Rain by giving him one of Lodar's Potion of Heightened Senses and whatever I can get of value from Benbyr. But I should visit Benbyr first.
Benbyr offered me fifty gold to keep the matter quiet. I refused.
Benbyr then offered 500 gold. I still refused.
Benbyr became terrified and handed over 5000 gold.
I gave one of Lodar's Potion of Heightened Senses to drunkard outside the Fallhaven tavern, and he remembered his time in Undertell.
I assured Rain that Shannal was at peace and gave him the 5000 gold Benbyr had given me. He told me to keep the money safe with Bela until his hangover passed.
I entrusted 4850 gold to Bela for safekeeping. She agreed to hold it.
Shannal thanked me for helping Rain and warned me to be careful. She removed the barricades in front of the entrance to Undertell.
In Undertell, the Kazaul Masters spoke to me. They claimed a forgotten ritual could seal the Rift once and for all.
They told me that this ritual was stolen long ago by a Lethgar named Varnel, who fled Undertell with it. I agreed to recover it, believing it might save Dhayavar.

In the upper dormitory tunnels of Undertell, I met the ghost of a miner who remembered Varnel. The ghost said Varnel escaped through the northern caverns and headed east toward the Sutdover River. Could he have meant Sullengard?
I traveled to Sullengard and spoke with Kealwea, the local priest. He recalled a relic matching my description once being sent to the Shadow church library in Remgard.
In Remgard's church basement, I spoke with Gwendolyn, the librarian. She said she knew nothing of any ritual but allowed me to search the shelves myself.
I discovered a small, locked box hidden behind the books. Its surface was etched with strange curling runes and old scorch marks. The box refused to open.
After I asked Gwendolyn about the locked box that I found, she directed me to speak with Skylenar upstairs.
Skylenar told me the box was an ancient relic, sealed by dragonkind and said to open only to a dragon's claw.
Skylenar mentioned that some old Shadow tales spoke of ash-covered scales found deep within Undertell, hinting that one such beast may once have lived there.
In the glowing white house basement, I talked to Falkour the dragon. When I showed him the locked box, he recognized it as a relic once held by Varnel.
Falkour gifted me one of his claws, saying it could break the seal, and warned me to use it only for that purpose. Time to find a safe place in this basement to open the box.
Using Falkour's claw, I unlocked the ancient box. Inside were the five pages of the Kazaul ritual the Masters desired.
The Master that I brought "The Five Aspects" ritual to sent me to talk to Thalen, the Master of Knowledge.
I returned the ritual to Thalen. He told me to meet the "lesser kin" at Anavrin's shrine to perform the ceremony.

As the ritual completed, the Masters revealed their true intent. The rite was not to seal the Rift but to awaken the Fifth Master, whose power might reopen it. They told me the Shadow itself serves Kazaul. Their words left me doubtful, unsure whether I had been deceived or warned.
I left Undertell uncertain of what to believe. If what the Masters said is true, the Shadow may not be what it seems. Still, doubt lingers like smoke after the forge cools.
Two Elytharan slave ghosts spoke quietly of another who has not joined them at the table. They said she still hides east of them, afraid the Shades might return.
The ghosts said the girl believed she could protect herself with a folded copper talisman she made long ago, but she lost it before she could hide it away from the evil of Undertell.
They remembered that such objects were sometimes taken during inspections, gathered with other personal effects and carried upward to the Masters.
I was told that one of the Masters may still possess the folded copper talisman, kept not for protection, but for understanding.

A Master acknowledged the talisman when I asked about it. He spoke of fear made solid, and said such fear was useful to those who taught the Shadow obedience rather than faith. It can be found in the "lower records", whatever that means.
In the Undertell archival room, I found the folded coin talisman.
I found the terrified girl hiding behind a collapsed rock wall. She would not approach me, nor leave her hiding place.
I tossed the folded copper talisman to her. Only then did she step forward, no longer clinging to the corner she had claimed as safety.
The girl rejoined the others at the table. The Elytharan ghosts spoke her name softly, as if afraid to lose her again.

Ysrine introduced me to Saki, ghost of an Elytharan mage. Now that the Kha'zaan were destroyed, Saki wanted me to help revive his Elytharan colleagues. They had become incorporeal during the war, and their souls became soul pearls.
Saki wanted me to defeat the liches who had picked up the soul pearls, and get back all five of them.
I returned to Saki with all five soul pearls. He took them in haste and disappeared.
Ysrine told me that Saki's behavior had confirmed her suspicions that Saki was a Kazaul mage and wanted to absorb the Elytharan mage souls to make himself stronger.
Ysrine told me that Saki was trying to flee Undertell. I was to find him, defeat him, and get the soul pearls back.
Prevented from escaping Undertell by Shannal, I found Saki at the passage to Undertell.
Ysrine thanked me and told me to keep the soul pearls safe.

replies.text: Let me see what potions you have made so far.

conversationlist_fallhaven_church.message: Turn back while you still can, mortal. This is no place for you. Only death awaits you here.

conversationlist_fallhaven_church.message: Well, do you think you could find me 5 skeletal bones that I can use for ... church matters?

Thank you, these bones will do fine. Now I can start creating some ... things.
Give me some time to ... prepare. Come back in a little while.

Yes, the bo ... I mean, yes, I have some of these potions ready. For the small sum of 200 gold pieces, I can show them to you. Perhaps you'd like to buy some of them then. Just don't let anybody see them.

replies.text: Here are 200 gold. Now let me see the potions.
There was something else I wanted to talk about.

conversationlist_fallhaven_athamyr.message: Walk with the Shadow.

replies.text: Have you been down in the catacombs?
May I ask you a question? Do you know a way to climb over the graveyard fence to the south?
I will go and find your ladder.
I tried the ladder, but the window is locked.
The ladder is gone and the window shut.

conversationlist_fallhaven_athamyr.message: Yes, I have been in the catacombs beneath Fallhaven Church.
But I'm the only one that has both the permission and the bravery to go down there.

replies.text: How can I get permission to go down there?

conversationlist_fallhaven_athamyr.message: You want to go down in the catacombs? Hmm, maybe we can make a deal.
Bring me some of that delicious cooked meat from the tavern and I will give you my permission to enter the catacombs of Fallhaven Church.

replies.text: Here, I have cooked meat for you.

conversationlist_fallhaven_athamyr.message: You have my permission to enter the catacombs of Fallhaven Church.
Thanks, this will do nicely.
I hope you behaved well there.
No, there is no way over the fence.
Why do you ask?
You can tell me.

replies.text: Well, behind the fence is the shop of the tailor.

conversationlist_fallhaven_athamyr.message: That's right.

replies.text: And there is always a window open.

conversationlist_fallhaven_athamyr.message: Ah, I understand. You want to surprise your friend, the tailor.
Then I have a better idea. I am your man.

replies.text: Great! I will thank you with a delicious piece of cooked meat.

conversationlist_fallhaven_athamyr.message: Ten.
Make it ten. Ten cooked meat.
I have to smuggle a ladder into the basement of the church, which is very risky for me.
Then you can climb through a window and reach a path right to the back of the tailor's house.

replies.text: OK. I have ten deliciously cooked pieces of meat now.
I will go for it now.

conversationlist_fallhaven_athamyr.message: What about the cooked meat?

replies.text: I have ten deliciously cooked pieces of meat now.
I will go for it now.

conversationlist_fallhaven_athamyr.message: Ohh ...
I knew you would do that, my friend. So I have already hidden the ladder in the basement near the window.
Oh, is that so? Hmm.

replies.text: Yes. And you know it perfectly well.

conversationlist_fallhaven_athamyr.message: Well, maybe I could risk borrowing the key and unlocking the window.
Bring twenty more pieces of cooked meat. Yes, twenty should do. That's worth my risk of ending up as bonemeal.

replies.text: I have bought the twenty cooked pieces of cooked meat.
I will go for it now.

conversationlist_fallhaven_athamyr.message: Ohh, that smells delicious! You are a true friend.

replies.text: Here take it. And don't forget to unlock the window.

conversationlist_fallhaven_athamyr.message: The window is already unlocked.

replies.text: I hope for your sake that was all.

conversationlist_fallhaven_athamyr.message: Yes. I tidied up a bit again.
... unlock the window again for you? No, I have enough cooked meat for a long time.

conversationlist_fallhaven_drunk.message: No problem. No sireee! Not causing any more trouble now. I sits here outside now.
Wait, who are you again? Are you that guard?

replies.text: No, I am here to give you something.

conversationlist_fallhaven_drunk.message: Oh, guard. I'm not causing any trouble anymore, see? I sits outside now as you says, OK?
Oh good. That guard threw me out of the tavern. If I see him again I'll show him one thing or another.
Drink drink drink, drink some more. Drink, drink ... Uh how did it go again?
Were you saying something? Where was I? Yes, so we were in this dungeon.

No no, it was outside! Now I remember.

That's where we...

Hey, where did my mead go? Did you take it from me?

replies.text: OK, I'll go buy some mead for you.

conversationlist_fallhaven_drunk.message: I must have drunk it then. Could you get me a new mead do you think?

replies.text: OK, I'll go buy some mead for you.

conversationlist_fallhaven_drunk.message:
Oh sweet drinks of joy. May the sssshadow be with you kid.
[Makes big eyes]

[Takes a gulp of the mead]

replies.text: Treasure? I'm in! I'll go look for Unnmir right away.
Thank you for the story. Goodbye.

conversationlist_fallhaven_nocmar.message: Hello and welcome to my place.

replies.text: This place looks like a smithy. Do you have anything to trade?

conversationlist_fallhaven_nocmar.message: I don't have any items for sale. I used to have a lot of things for sale, but nowadays I'm not allowed to sell anything.
I was once one of the greatest smiths in Fallhaven. Then that bastard Lord Geomyr banned my use of heartsteel.
By decree of Lord Geomyr, no one in Fallhaven is allowed to even use heartsteel weapons. Much less sell any.
So now I have to hide the few weapons I have left. I won't dare sell any of them anymore.
I haven't seen the heartsteel glow in several years now that Lord Geomyr has banned them.
So, unfortunately I can't sell you any of my weapons.
Unnmir sent you huh? I guess it must be important then.
OK, these old weapons have lost their inner glow now that they haven't been used in a while.
To make the heartsteel glow again, we will need a heartstone.
Years ago, we used to fight the liches of Undertell. I have no idea if they still haunt the place.

replies.text: Undertell? Is that where I could find a heartstone?

conversationlist_fallhaven_nocmar.message: Undertell; the pits of the lost souls. Travel south to the devastated wastelands of Galmore Mountain and follow the tracks from there.
Beware the liches of Undertell, if they are still around. Those things can kill you by their gaze alone.
Have you found a heartstone yet?

replies.text: Yes, at last I found it.
Could you tell me the story again?
Actually, I found two. [extend your hands, one stone in each]
Yes, at last I found it.
[while shaking your head] It's in your hand.

conversationlist_fallhaven_nocmar.message: Please keep looking. Unnmir must have something important planned for you.
So you truly have it? The heartstone...beautiful and intact. Remarkable. You've done what few would dare. Can you see the glow? It's literally pulsating.
He studies it with reverence, then grows troubled.

But no, I cannot work it here. Too many eyes, too many whispers. If I were caught forging heartsteel in this shop, it would mean ruin for me. I need a place that is safe, hidden, yet...proper. Somewhere I can work without Lord Geomyr's men breathing down my neck. A place where I am allowed to be.
While pausing, Nocmar looks down, then sighs.

There was a time, before all this, when I had a place. A house. Not just any house...a white house on the edge of Fallhaven, glowing as if lit by the gods themselves. That glow comes from the forge inside. A forge unlike any other, always hot, always ready. It was there that I forged heartsteel in secret, while the shopfront stayed clean for coin and trade.

replies.text: Well, that time has come back! I have the deed and the key to your forge house. [hand them to Nocmar]

conversationlist_fallhaven_oldman.message: Would you help an old man please?

replies.text: Sure, what do you need help with?

conversationlist_fallhaven_oldman.message: I recently lost a very valuable book of mine.
I know I had it with me yesterday. Now I can't seem to find it.

Would you please go look for my book? It's called 'Calomyran Secrets'.

I have no idea where it might be. You could go ask Arcir, he seems very fond of his books.
 [Points at the house to the south]

replies.text: OK, I'll go ask Arcir. Goodbye.

conversationlist_fallhaven_oldman.message: How is the search for my book going? It's called 'Calomyran Secrets'. Have you found my book?

conversationlist_fallhaven_oldman.message: My book! Thank you, thank you! Where was it? No, don't tell me. Here, take these coins for your trouble.

replies.text: Let me see what food and drinks you have available.

Please keep these {4850} gold coins for safekeeping. Rain asked for you until he gets over his hangover, he'll come collect them when he is ready.

conversationlist_fallhaven_tavern.message: A room will cost you only 10 gold.

replies.text: As you know I can handle myself.

replies.text:
No, I didn't hear, and I also don't want to.
Please give me something to drink.

replies.text: Thanks for the warning. I'll avoid that area.

replies.text: Let me see what food and drinks you have available.

conversationlist_fallhaven_tavern.message: Oh no - what have I done? I shouldn't have talked of the giant snake. Promise me you won't go there!

replies.text: Well, if it makes you happy.

conversationlist_fallhaven_tavern.message: What a waste of such a young, promising life! Well...don't forget to pay your tab before you leave my tavern.

replies.text: Sure. And your little snake monster is no more.

conversationlist_fallhaven_tavern.message: Incredible! Let's feast now! Everyone have a free drink!

replies.text: At last, a fight. I have been waiting for this!

conversationlist_fallhaven_unnmir.message: Hello again. You should go talk to Nocmar.

replies.text: There was a drunk outside the tavern that told me a story about you two.

conversationlist_fallhaven_unnmir.message: That old drunk over at the tavern told you his story did he?
Same old story. We used to travel together a few years back.
Real adventuring you know, swords and spells.

Nice little town here. A lot of thieves around, but they don't bother me.

Yeah yeah, I get it. Your brother has probably run off to some dungeon, trying to go adventuring.
