Thank you for not inciting the argument any further. Maybe someday there will be something like peace again.

replies.text: I wish it for you. Can I go in here?

conversationlist_blackwater_lower.message: OK. I trust you not to do any mischief.

conversationlist_blackwater_herec.message: Welcome, traveller. You must be the one I heard about, that travelled up the mountain.
Would you be willing to help me with a task?

replies.text: Why would I want to help you?

conversationlist_blackwater_herec.message: Ah, a negotiator. I like that. If you help me, I will offer to trade the fruits of my labour with you. It should be most valuable to you.

replies.text: Fine. What task are we talking about here?
No, how can I agree to something when I don't know what it is? I'm out.

conversationlist_blackwater_herec.message: It is simple really. I am studying these wyrm creatures that lurk outside our settlement. I am trying to find what their strengths are, so that I can use it for myself.
But my expertise is in the studies of them, and not in actually going head to head with those things.
I need you to gather some samples from them for me. I hear that some of the white wyrm beasts have sharper claws that can be extracted at the time of death.
If you were to bring me some samples of those claws from the white wyrms, that would really speed up my research further.
Let's say, five of those claws should be enough.

replies.text: OK, sounds easy enough. I'll get you your 5 white wyrm claws.
Sure. Those things are no match for me.
No way I am going near those beasts again.

conversationlist_blackwater_herec.message: Good. Thank you. Please hurry back so I can continue my research on these beasts.
I assure you that my research is important. But it's your decision, and your loss.
Welcome back. How is the search going?

replies.text: What was I supposed to do again?
I haven't found everything yet. But I am working on it.
I have found what you asked for.

conversationlist_blackwater_herec.message: Very well done my friend! These will be very valuable in my research.
Come back in just a minute and I will have something ready for you.
Welcome back my friend! Good news. I have successfully distilled the fragments of the claws you brought earlier.
Now I am able to create effective potions that contain some essence of the white wyrms. These potions will be very useful in future dealings with these monsters.
Would you like to trade for some potions?

replies.text: Sure. Let's see what you have.

conversationlist_prim_bjorgur.message: Hello again, friend. Thank you for your assistance with my family grave earlier.
Hello again. Have you investigated if anything has happened to my family grave?

replies.text: [Lie] I went to check on the grave. Everything seems to be normal. You must be imagining things.
What was I supposed to do again?
Yes. I killed the intruder and restored the dagger to its original place.

conversationlist_prim_bjorgur.message: Hello there. You wouldn't happen to know anything about a grave to the southwest of Prim would you?

replies.text: I have been there. I met someone on one of the lower levels.

conversationlist_prim_bjorgur.message: My family grave is located in the tomb to the southwest of Prim right outside the Elm mine. I fear that something has disturbed the peace there.
You see, my grandfather was very fond of a particular valuable dagger that our family used to possess. He wore it with him always.
The dagger would of course attract treasure hunters, but up until now we seem to have been spared of this.
Now I fear something has happened to the grave. I have not been sleeping well the last couple of nights, and I am sure this must be the cause.
You wouldn't happen to want to go check on the grave and see what is happening over there?

replies.text: Sure. I will go check on your parents grave.
A treasure you say? I'm interested.
I have actually already been there and restored the dagger to its original place.

conversationlist_prim_bjorgur.message: Thank you. Please see if anything has happened to the grave, and what could be the cause of my nightly anxiety.
Nothing you say? But I was sure something must have happened over there. Anyway. Thank you for checking it for me.
Please hurry, and return here to tell me of your progress once you find out something.
An intruder? Oh thank you for dealing with this matter.
You say you restored the dagger to it's original place? Thank you. Now I might be able to rest during the nights ahead.
Thank you again. I'm afraid I can't give you anything except my gratitude. You should go see my relatives in Feygard if you get the chance to travel up there.

conversationlist_prim_fulus.message: Hey you! You shouldn't be here. This dagger is mine. Get out!

replies.text: Hey, that's a nice looking dagger you have there.

conversationlist_prim_fulus.message: You see the remains of rusted equipment and rotten leather.

You see the remains of rusted equipment and rotten leather. Something seems to have been recently removed from here since one place completely lacks dust.

The lack of dust looks distinctly dagger-shaped. There must have been a dagger here earlier that someone removed.

replies.text: Place the dagger back into its original place.

conversationlist_prim_fulus.message: You place the dagger back among the equipment, where it looks like it used to be.
Hello again, friend. Thank you for your assistance in obtaining that dagger earlier.
Hello again. Have you been able to retrieve that dagger from Bjorgur's family grave yet?

replies.text: I decided to help Bjorgur instead.
What was I supposed to do again?

conversationlist_prim_fulus.message: What?! Sigh. Stupid kid. That dagger is worth a fortune. We could have been rich! Rich I tell you!
Hello there. You seem like just the type of person I am looking for.
Oh wow, you actually managed to get the dagger? Thank you kid. This is worth a lot. Here, take these coins as compensation for your efforts!
Thank you again. Now, let's see ... how much should we sell this dagger for?
Would you be interested in hearing about a business proposal I have?

replies.text: If it leads to something for me to gain, then sure.
I couldn't possibly think you would have anything worthwhile to offer me, but let's hear it anyways.

conversationlist_prim_fulus.message: For some time, I have known about a certain valuable dagger that a certain family used to possess here in Prim.
Now hurry up. I really need that dagger soon.
This dagger is extremely valuable to me, for personal reasons.

replies.text: I don't like where this is going. I better not get involved in your shady business.
I like where this is going, please continue.
I have already helped Bjorgur return the dagger to its original place.

conversationlist_prim_fulus.message: Fine. Suit yourself, you goody two-shoes.
The family in question is Bjorgur's family.
Now, I happen to know that this particular dagger can be found in their family tomb that has been opened by other ... people ... recently.
What I want is simple. You go get that dagger and bring it to me, and I will reward you handsomely.

replies.text: Sounds easy enough. I'll do it.
No, I had better not get involved in your shady business.
I have already helped Bjorgur return the dagger to its original place.

conversationlist_prim_fulus.message: Good. Return to me once you have it. Maybe you can talk to Bjorgur about directions to the tomb. His house is just outside here in Prim. Just don't mention anything about our plan to him!

conversationlist_prim_merchants.message: Welcome friend! Would you like to see what equipment I have available?

replies.text: Sure. Show me what you have.

conversationlist_prim_merchants.message: Welcome traveller. Have you come to ask for help from me and the equipment I sell?
I must tell you that my supply is not what it used to be, now that the southern mine entrance has collapsed. Far fewer traders come here to Prim now.

replies.text: OK, let me see your wares.

conversationlist_prim_merchants.message: Regardless, I cannot help you. My services are only for residents of Prim, and I don't trust you enough yet. You might be a spy from the Blackwater mountain settlement.
Welcome traveller, what can I do for you?

replies.text: Let me see what you have available to sell.
What do you know about Lorn's crew's accident?

conversationlist_prim_merchants.message: Sell? I'm sorry, my supplies are all out. Now that the traders do not come here anymore, I don't get my regular shipments. So at the moment, I have nothing to trade with you unfortunately.
Talk to the boss instead.
Please don't hurt me! I'm only doing my job.
What are you looking at? These weapons in the crates over here are only for us guards.
[The guard looks down on you with a condescending look]
Oh, I am so tired. When will we ever get to rest?
Can't talk now. I'm on guard duty. If you need help, talk to someone else over there instead.
See these bars? They will hold against almost anything.

replies.text: Guthbered said I could choose anything from the vault. So let me in.
Guthbered said I could choose anything from the vault. So let me in.

conversationlist_prim_merchants.message: When my training is complete, I will be one of the greatest healers around!
Can't you see I'm trying to read over here? Talk to me in a while and I might be interested.
Can't talk now, I have work to do.
Are you the one I heard about? No, you can't be. I imagined someone taller.
Welcome friend! Would you like to browse my selection of fine potions and ointments?

replies.text: Sure. Show me what you have.

conversationlist_prim_merchants.message: Welcome traveller. Have you come to ask for help from me and my potions?
These bars will hold against almost anything indeed.
This heap of gold is a big too much even for you.
Furthermore, the people of Prim would be happy if you didn't take all their gold.
Cling!
He said so? [His piercing gaze unsettles you.]
Nice try, kid. Now go play again.

replies.text: Play? I'm going to play - with you!

conversationlist_prim_merchants.message: Well, well, well.

replies.text: Eh, you look bigger than before. And stronger.

conversationlist_prim_merchants.message: It's a good thing I noticed my colleague has left his post. He was pretty weak anyway.

replies.text: Listen, we could avoid some trouble. I'll give you 200 gold pieces if you let me pass.

conversationlist_prim_merchants.message: Make it {2000}, then we have a deal.

conversationlist_blackwater_throdna.message: Kazaul ... Shadow ... what was it again?
Oh, a visitor. Hello there. I have not seen you around here before. Did they let you in here?
Of course they did. What am I rambling on about. Harlenn and his gang always keep their worldly duties under control.
So, who might you be then, eh? Probably here to bother me with some worldly complaint about the settlement needing more resources or someone complaining about the cold drag from the outside again?
What do you want?

replies.text: What was that you talked about when I arrived, Kazaul?
Are you aware that there is a bitter rivalry going on between this settlement and Prim?

conversationlist_blackwater_throdna.message: And there you go with your mundane problems. I tell you, your worldly troubles do not interest me the least bit.
This is the mages' chamber in Blackwater mountain. We devote our time to the studies of the Shadow and its descendants.

replies.text: Let's go back to my other questions.

conversationlist_blackwater_throdna.message: I am Throdna. One of the most learned persons around, if you ask me.
Kazaul, the Shadow spawn of red marrow.
We have been trying to read all we can on Kazaul, and the ritual. It seems we might be too late.
The ritual. We believe that Kazaul will manifest in our presence soon.
We must learn more about the Kazaul ritual, to gain its power and learn to use it for our purposes.

replies.text: Can I help in some way?
What were you planning to do?

conversationlist_blackwater_throdna.message: As I said, we want to learn more about the ritual itself.
A while ago, we were on the verge of getting our hands on the whole ritual itself, but the messenger was killed under most interesting circumstances while traveling up here.
We knew he had the parts of the complete ritual on him, but since he was killed and we could not get to him because of the monsters - his notes were lost to us.

According to our sources, there should be five parts of the ritual scattered across the mountain. Three of them describing the ritual itself, and two describing the Kazaul chant used to summon the guardian.
Hmm, maybe you could be of use here...

replies.text: I would be glad to help.
Sounds dangerous, but I'll do it.
Keep your ritual of the Shadow to yourself. I am not getting involved in this.

conversationlist_blackwater_throdna.message: Fine, we will just have to find someone else then.
Yes, you might be able to help. Not that you really have any choice though.
OK. Find me the pieces of the ritual that the former messenger carried on him. They should be found somewhere on the path up to Blackwater mountain.

replies.text: I will return with your parts of the ritual.

conversationlist_blackwater_throdna.message: Yes, you will.
Hello again. I hope you come here to tell me you have the five parts of the ritual.

replies.text: I am still looking for them.
How many parts was I supposed to find?
What was I supposed to do again?
Yes, I think I have found them all.

conversationlist_blackwater_throdna.message: Then hurry and go find them! What are you standing around here for then?
You actually found all five pieces? I suppose I should thank you. Well then. Thank you.
It seems you have not found all five pieces yet.
We have more pressing matters to focus on. As I briefly mentioned before, we believe that Kazaul will manifest in our presence soon.
If that were to happen, we could not complete our research about the ritual or Kazaul itself, all our efforts would be lost.
Therefore, we intend to delay the process as much as we can, until we have learned of its powers.
You might be useful to us here again.

replies.text: What do you need of me?
I sure hope it involves more killing and looting.

conversationlist_blackwater_throdna.message: We need you to do two things. First, you must find the shrine of Kazaul. Our scouts tell us that the shrine should be located somewhere near the base of Blackwater mountain.
However, all passageways to the shrine are 'clouded in Shadow' according to our scouts. I'm not sure what that means.
Second, we need you to take a vial of purifying spirit and apply it to the shrine.
This vial is a vial of purifying spirit. It should delay the process well enough for us to be able to continue our research.

replies.text: Sounds dangerous, but I will do it.
This sounds like a trap. I won't agree to do your dirty work.

conversationlist_blackwater_throdna.message: Good, here is the vial. Now hurry.
Return to me as soon as you have completed your task.
Hello again. I hope you are here to tell me you have purified the shrine of Kazaul?

replies.text: What was I supposed to do again?

conversationlist_blackwater_throdna.message: Then hurry and go take the vial to the shrine! What are you standing around here for?
Good. We must hurry to continue our research on Kazaul.
You should get out of here to allow us to concentrate on our work.
...Kazaul, destroyer of bright dreams...
...Kazaul ... Shadow...
[Throdna continues to mumble on about Kazaul, but you cannot make out any other words]
Keep your voice down while in the inner chamber.
Are you also looking to become one with the Shadow?

conversationlist_blackwater_kazaul.message: [The guardian looks completely unaware of your presence]
[The guardian looks down upon you with its burning eyes]

replies.text: Kazaul, defiler of the Elytharan Temple.

conversationlist_blackwater_kazaul.message: [You see the burning eyes of the guardian instantly turn into a dark red haze]

replies.text: A fight, I have been waiting for this!

conversationlist_blackwater_kazaul.message: You see the shrine of Kazaul that you poured the vial of purifying spirit on.
The previously glowing hot rock is now cold as any regular piece of rock.
Before you stands a large cut out piece of rock, in what looks like a shrine.
You can feel an intense heat coming from the rock, almost like a burning fire.

replies.text: Apply the vial of purifying spirit on the formation.

conversationlist_blackwater_kazaul.message: You gently pour the contents of the vial onto the formation.
You hear a loud crackling noise from deep below the shrine. At first, the formation seems unaffected, but after a while you see the glowing of the rock decrease slightly.
The process continues more rapidly, while reducing the heat generated from the formation.
This must be the purification process of the Kazaul shrine.

conversationlist_erinith.message: Thank you for all your help earlier.
Please, you have to help me!
I was setting up camp here during the night, and was attacked by some bandits while asleep.
Ack, this wound doesn't seem to be healing itself.
At least I managed to keep them from getting my book. I'm sure they were after the book.

replies.text: Seems like a valuable book then. This sounds interesting, please go on.

conversationlist_erinith.message:
I managed to throw the book in among the trees over there during the attack.
[Points to the trees directly to the north]
I don't think they managed to get the book. It's probably still somewhere among those trees.
Oh, I can't say really.

replies.text: I could help you find that book if you want.
What would it be worth for you to get that book back?

conversationlist_erinith.message: You would? Oh thank you.
Please go look for it among those trees to the northeast.
Worth? Well, I was hoping you would help me anyway, but I guess 200 gold could do.

replies.text: 200 gold it is then. I'll go look for your book.
A lousy 200 gold, is that all you can do? Fine, I'll go look for your stupid book.
Keep your gold, I'll return your book for you anyway.
No, I am not getting involved in this. Goodbye.

conversationlist_erinith.message: Make it quick.
Have you found that book yet?

replies.text: Not yet, I am still looking.

conversationlist_erinith.message: You found it! Oh thank you so much. I was so worried that I had lost it.
You found it! Oh thank you so much. In return, here is the gold I promised you.
Thank you for helping me find my book earlier.
I am still hurt by this wound that I got from the attack during the night.
Ack, it hurts so bad and it doesn't seem to be healing itself.
I am really in need of some stronger healing here. Maybe some potions would do.
I have heard that the potion makers these days have major potions of health, and not just the regular potions of health.
One of those would surely do. Otherwise, I think four regular potions of health would be enough.

replies.text: I'll go get those potions for you.
Here, take this bonemeal potion instead. It's very potent in healing deep wounds.
Here, take this major potion of health.
Here, take this major flask of health.
Here, take these four regular potions of health.

conversationlist_erinith.message: Thank you my friend. Please hurry back.
Bonemeal potion? But ... but ... we are not allowed to use them since they are prohibited by Lord Geomyr.

replies.text: I have tried them myself, it's perfectly safe to use them.

conversationlist_erinith.message:
Hmm, yes. I guess you have a point. Oh well, here goes.
[Drinks potion]

Thank you for bringing me one.
[Drinks potion]

Thank you for bringing them to me.
[Drinks all four potions]
Wow, I feel slightly better already. I guess this healing really works.
Thank you my friend for your help. My book is safe and my wound is healing. I hope our paths will cross again.

conversationlist_hadracor.message: Stupid wasps...
Stay away from the road to the west, for it leads to Carn Tower. You most certainly do not want to go there.
When travelling, keep to the roads. Veer off course and you might find yourself in danger.
Maybe we shouldn't have cut down all the trees over there. Those wasps really seem upset.
I can still feel the sting from those wasps in my legs. Good thing we are done with all the trees now.
Hello there, welcome to our encampment. You should talk to Hadracor over there.
Hello there, I am Hadracor.

replies.text: Have you seen my brother Andor around here? Looks somewhat like me.
Do you by any chance have some spare wood to make fences out of?
I'm $playername, running up and down Blackwater mountain for errands.

conversationlist_hadracor.message: Looks like you eh? No, I would have remembered.
This is the encampment that we woodcutters set up while working on the trees here for the past few days.

replies.text: What have you been working on?
I noticed a lot of tree stumps around here.

conversationlist_hadracor.message: Our orders were to cut down all trees south of the Feygard bridge and north of this here road to Carn Tower.
I guess the nobles of Feygard have some plans for these lands.
We, we just cut down them trees. No questions asked.
However, this time we encountered some trouble.
You see, there were these really nasty wasps in that forest we cut down.
Nothing like we've seen before, and I'll tell you, we have seen a lot of wildlife in our days.
They almost got the best of us, and we were almost ready to quit it. But a job is a job and we need to get paid by Feygard for this job.
So we went ahead and finished all of them trees, trying to evade the wasps as much as we could.
However, I bet that whatever plans the nobles of Feygard have for these lands, they surely don't include these nasty wasps still being around.
See this scratch here? And this abscess? Yep, those wasps.
I would love to get revenge on those wasps. We, we aren't good enough fighters to take on those wasps, they are really too quick for us.

replies.text: Tough luck, you seem like a bunch of weaklings anyway.
I could try to take on those wasps for you if you want.
Just a couple of wasps? That's no problem for me. I'll kill them for you.

conversationlist_hadracor.message: I will pretend I didn't hear that.
You would? Sure, you have a try.
I noticed that some of the wasps are larger than the other ones, and the other wasps tend to follow the larger ones around.
If you could kill at least five of those giant ones and bring me back their wings as proof, I would be very grateful.

replies.text: Sure, I will be back with those giant wasp wings for you.
On second thought, I better stay out of this.

conversationlist_hadracor.message: Fine, I guess we can find someone else to help us get revenge on them.
Good, hurry back once you are done.
Hello again. Did you kill those wasps for us?

replies.text: Could you tell me your story again?
What was I supposed to do again?
Not yet, but I am working on it.
Yes, I killed six of them.
Yes, I killed five of them.
No, but I wanted to ask if you have some spare wood to make fences out of.
No, I'm too busy running up and down Blackwater mountain.

conversationlist_hadracor.message: Wow, you actually killed those things?
Wow, you actually killed six of those things? I thought there were only five, so I guess I should be even more grateful. Here, take these gloves as thanks.
Well done my friend. Thank you for getting revenge on those things.
Hello again. Thank you for your help with those wasps earlier.
As a token of our appreciation, we are willing to trade some of our equipment with you if you want.
It's not much, but we do have some really sharp axes that you might be interested in.

replies.text: OK, let me see what you have.
Do you by any chance have some spare wood to make fences out of?
No, thanks. I'm too busy running up and down Blackwater mountain.

conversationlist_tinlyn.message: You attacked my sheep! Get away from me you filthy murderer!

replies.text: I am sorry. But your brother sent me to ask if you knew where I could get fences for his sheep.

conversationlist_tinlyn.message: Hello again. Thank you for helping me find my lost sheep.

replies.text: I talked to Benbyr and heard the story about you two.
Your brother has sent me to ask where I could get fences from. Do you maybe know?

conversationlist_tinlyn.message: Hello there. You wouldn't happen to want to help an old shepherd would you?

replies.text: Your brother has sent me to ask where I could get fences from. Do you maybe know?

conversationlist_tinlyn.message: You see, I tend my flock of sheep here. These fields are excellent pastures for them.
The thing is, I have lost four of them. Now I won't dare leave the ones I still have in my sight to go look for the lost ones.
Would you be willing to help me find them?

replies.text: This doesn't sound like there will be any fighting involved. I only do things where there's fighting involved.
Absolutely, it would be my honor to assist you in locating your missing sheep.
What would I gain from this?

conversationlist_tinlyn.message: Oh well, it didn't hurt to ask.
Gain? Why, my thanks of course.

replies.text: This doesn't sound like there will be any fighting involved. I only do things where there's fighting involved.
Sure, I will help you find your sheep.
No thanks, I better not get involved in this.

conversationlist_tinlyn.message: Good, thank you. Please put these bells around their necks so I can hear them.
Return to me once you have placed bells around the neck of each of the four missing sheep.
Hello again. Did you find all four of my missing sheep?

replies.text: Yes, I found all of them.
Not yet. I am still looking.
What was I supposed to do?
I talked to Benbyr and heard the story about you two.

conversationlist_tinlyn.message: Yes, I can hear distant sounds of bells from the fields to the south. I am sure they will come back here now that they have the bells on them.

replies.text: That was some hard work. What about a reward?

conversationlist_tinlyn.message: I am sorry, but I am a simple shepherd. I have no wealth or magical trinkets to give you.
Is he still around? I thought the guards got the best of him.
Anyway, I do not want to talk about that. I have left that kind of life behind me. Herding sheep is what I do now.

replies.text: [Place Tinlyn's bell around the neck of the sheep]
[Place Tinlyn's bell around the neck of the sheep]
[Place Tinlyn's bell around the neck of the sheep]
[Place Tinlyn's bell around the neck of the sheep]

conversationlist_tinlyn_sheep.message: [You place one of the bells around the neck of the sheep]

conversationlist_benbyr.message: Hello again. We sure showed that bastard Tinlyn. That should teach him not to mess with me again.
I have nothing more to say to you. Leave me.
Psst, hey. Over here.
You look like an aspiring adventurer. Are you willing to do some ... [Benbyr pauses] ... adventuring? He he.

replies.text: What are we talking about here?
Depends on what I get in return.
I try to help people wherever they might need help.

conversationlist_benbyr.message: Straight to the point eh? I like that.
Ah, the adventurer seeks compensation. Tell me, is the thrill of an adventure not reward enough?
Then I will surely disappoint you. Return to me once you are ready for my task.
The noble adventurer. He he, I like that. Yes, you will do fine.
A while ago, I did some business with a certain man called Tinlyn, over here at this Crossroads guardhouse.
As to the nature of our business, I can't really tell you. Let's just say that our business was of the kind that was mutually beneficial and the guards did not know about it.
We were ready to finish the big deal, me and Tinlyn. That's when he decided to turn on me.
He reported me to the guards, and made me take the whole blame for our business.
I was sent to Feygard prison, while he himself was set free for reporting me.
Argh, that fool Tinlyn. I hope the Shadow never shows him any mercy.

replies.text: What do you need me to do?

conversationlist_benbyr.message: I want to get revenge on that fool Tinlyn of course. Now, my plan is the following:
I have heard that he is herding sheep these days. This is an excellent opportunity for ... shall we say ... an accident to happen to his sheep. He he.
You, my friend, would be the perfect walking accident. I want you to find all of Tinlyn's sheep and make sure they are forever united with the Shadow.
Do this, and I will have avenged that fool Tinlyn.

replies.text: Sounds like just my type of thing. I'll do it!
This sounds a bit shady, but I'll do it anyway.
No way, killing innocent sheep is beneath me. I will never do your task.

conversationlist_benbyr.message: Very well, but remember that I have my eyes on you ... adventurer.
Splendid!
I happen to know that there are eight of his sheep in total, and they should all be to the northwest of here.
Return to me with proof that you have slain all eight of them.
Ah, my walking accident returns. He he.

replies.text: Can you tell me your story again?
I am still looking for those sheep.
I have slain all eight of Tinlyn's sheep for you.

conversationlist_benbyr.message: Ha ha! That fool Tinlyn must be in tears. The Shadow surely walks with you my friend.
This is a glorious day indeed! Tinlyn should have known not to mess with me!
As for you my friend, seek out my friends in Brightport. I am sure they would extend their hospitality to you.

conversationlist_crossroads_1.message: Yikes! You scared me there.
I was just strolling through these woods ... eh ... killing anklebiters.
Yes. Killing them was what I was doing. Not running away from them. No, killing them.
*sigh*
Oh, who am I kidding. OK, I was trying to get through the forest here and got ambushed by these anklebiters.
I won't leave until nightfall, when they can't see me anymore and I might be able to sneak back.
This is my hiding spot! Now leave me.

replies.text: Umar sent me with the words "You are no one.No one knows you.No one has seen you." Now give me the journal please.

conversationlist_crossroads_1.message: Did you hear? Some thieves down in Fallhaven were planning an escape for one of the imprisoned thieves in the prison there.
Luckily, someone got wind of it and told the guard captain.
It's good to know that there are at least a few decent people still around.
Aren't you a bit young to be traveling around here all by yourself?
I sure hope you are not another one of those types trying to sell me your cheap junk.
Go away, kid.
Didn't you hear? They have all gotten ill.
It all started a few days ago. As the story goes, someone found one of the farmers passed out in one of the fields, completely white faced and shivering.
A few days later, the same symptoms started to show on a lot more people.
Then, all people showed the symptoms in one way or another.
Some old people even died.
Everyone started investigating what could be the cause. Currently, the cause is still unknown.
Luckily, now Feygard has sent patrols up there to help guard the village at least. The people are still suffering though.
Me, I am certain that this is the work of those savages from Nor City somehow. They probably sabotaged something up there.
What do they call it, the 'Shadow'? They are willing to do almost anything to upset the law and order around here.
I tell you. Savages - that's what they are. No respect for the laws or authority.

conversationlist_minarra.message: Hello there. Can I help you?

replies.text: You seem to have a lot of equipment around here. Do you have anything to trade?
What do you do up here?
You must have a good view of the surroundings up here. Have you seen anything interesting lately?

conversationlist_minarra.message: I might, but you would have to clear it with Gandoren downstairs. We don't trade with just anyone.
You return. Was there something else you wanted?

replies.text: Can you tell me again about those men you saw?
Do you have anything to trade?
What do you do up here?

conversationlist_minarra.message: Mostly, I see the travellers on the Duleian road from and to Feygard here.
Recently however, there have been a lot of movements to and from Loneford. I guess it is because of the problems they have been having up there.
I did see something very interesting yesterday though.

replies.text: You mentioned the Duleian road, what's that?
You mentioned some problems in Loneford, what problems were you referring to?
Never mind that, I wanted to ask you what your duty is up here?

conversationlist_minarra.message: Some farm animals today as well.

replies.text: You mentioned the Duleian road, what's that?
You mentioned some problems in Loneford, what problems were you referring to?

conversationlist_minarra.message: I handle the equipment storage for us guards here in the Crossroads guardhouse, and I keep a lookout of the surrounding areas.

replies.text: Do you have anything to trade?
Have you seen anything interesting lately?

conversationlist_minarra.message: See this wide road that goes outside this guardhouse? That's the Duleian road. It goes all the way from the glorious city of Feygard up in the northwest down to the wretched Nor City in the southeast.

replies.text: You mentioned some problems in Loneford, what problems are that?
I wanted to ask you what your duty is up here?

conversationlist_minarra.message: See this wide road that goes outside this guardhouse? That's the Duleian road. It goes all the way from the glorious city of Feygard up in the northwest down to the wretched Nor City in the southeast.

replies.text: You mentioned some problems in Loneford, what problems are that?

conversationlist_minarra.message: I saw a band of rough looking men travelling up the Duleian road. Usually, a band of rough looking men is not something that's worth getting all excited about.
But these men matched the description of some people that are wanted by the Feygard patrol.
If I saw correctly, these men were the band of rogues led by a man called Rogorn, that we are looking to apprehend for several ruthless cases of murder and theft.
Their leader, Rogorn, is a particularly savage man according to the reports from Feygard that I have read.

Now, usually, we would go out searching for them, to verify that the men I saw were indeed these men. However, now with the trouble up in Loneford, we cannot afford to spare any guards other than to guarding Loneford.
I am sure that those were the men. If we were to catch and kill them, the people of Feygard would be much safer.

replies.text: I could go look for them if you want.

conversationlist_minarra.message: Thank you. Good luck yourself. Now, if you will excuse me, I need to keep my eyes on the road.
Hey, that's a great idea. Are you sure you are up to it though? The people of Feygard would indeed be grateful if you were to find them.
Anyway, I saw them travelling the road west of here. You know that road that leads to Carn Tower? That's the last I saw of them. You might want to follow that road and see if you can spot them.
They have stolen three pieces of a very valuable painting from Feygard, from the report that I have read. For their crimes and the savageness of their way, they are wanted dead by the Feygard patrol.

replies.text: I will be back once they are dead. Anything else?

conversationlist_minarra.message: Yes, I should also tell you that they most likely will try to persuade you into believing their story.
In particular, their leader, Rogorn, is a well known villain by Feygard. Nothing he says should be trusted.
I urge you not to listen to their lies. Their crimes must be punished in order to uphold the law.

replies.text: I will return once the task is done.

conversationlist_minarra.message: You return. Did you find those men that we talked about?

replies.text: I am still looking for them.
Yes, I killed them and recovered the three pieces of the painting.
I travelled west and found a travelling group of men, but they did not match the men you described.
I'd rather talk about the troubles in Loneford that you had mentioned.

conversationlist_minarra.message: Good. Return to me as soon as you have anything to report. We would really like to recover those three pieces of the painting they stole.
That is excellent news indeed! I knew that we could trust you.
Your services to Feygard will be greatly appreciated.
Are you sure that they were not the ones? I have a keen eyesight, that's why I am up here. I was sure that they matched the description of the men.
I guess I will have to take your word for it.
Thank you for helping me investigate this matter.

replies.text: Do you have anything to trade?
You must have a good view of the surroundings up here. Have you seen anything interesting lately?

conversationlist_minarra.message: Thank you for helping me investigate the men earlier.

replies.text: Do you have anything to trade?
You must have a good view of the surroundings up here. Have you seen anything interesting lately?

conversationlist_minarra.message: Sure, take a look.

conversationlist_rogorn.message: For the Shadow!
Good to hear that there are at least a few people left out there willing to take a stand against Feygard.
Should you really be out here all by yourself?
Look fellas, a kid! Out strolling here in the wilderness!
Should you really be out here kid? These areas are dangerous.

replies.text: You are right, I better leave.

conversationlist_rogorn.message: I bet you can.
Well, west of here is not much. No towns for quite a while, only the harsh and dangerous wilderness.
Of course, there is Carn Tower if you travel really far west, but you really do not want to head there.
So, what brings you to these parts of the land?

replies.text: I am looking for a group of men led by someone by the name of Rogorn. Are you him?
Just looking for any treasure that might reveal itself here.

conversationlist_rogorn.message: Well, keep on looking then.
That depends, why do you want to know?

replies.text: You are wanted by the Feygard patrol for the crimes you have committed.
I am seeking to deal justice wherever I can, and I heard that you are in need of being shown some justice.
I am sent by some guards over at the Crossroads guardhouse to look for you.
The guards from Feygard are looking for you, and I came to warn you.

conversationlist_rogorn.message: Hah! We? Crimes?
Justice? What would you know of justice, kid?
If there is someone that deserves punishment, it surely isn't us. By the Shadow, it's those snobs from Feygard that should be taught a lesson.

replies.text: I will not listen to your lies! For Feygard!
Talk all you want, I happen to know that you have stolen from Feygard, which is not acceptable.
What's your side of the story then?

conversationlist_rogorn.message: I tell you, we did not steal anything from those snobs.

replies.text: You are still wanted dead by the Feygard patrol. For Feygard!
Why are they looking for you then?

conversationlist_rogorn.message: I had hoped it would not come to this. For the Shadow!
Talked to those guards from Feygard eh? Tell me, what is your opinion of Feygard?

replies.text: They seem to have honorable ideals of law and order, and I respect that.
Their ideals seem to be a bit oppressive of the people, which I do not like.
I have no opinion, I try not to get involved in their business.

conversationlist_rogorn.message: Interesting. But now that you are part of their business by coming here to look for me on their behalf, how does that fit into your unwillingness to take sides?

replies.text: I will not listen to your lies! For Feygard!
I was told that you have stolen from Feygard, which is not acceptable.
I want to hear your side of the story.
I am just looking to see if there is some treasure to be gained from this.

conversationlist_rogorn.message: You should make up your mind about what your priorities are. Tell your Feygard friends that we will not be oppressed by them. Shadow be with you, child.
You have got that right. They are always trying to make life hard for us little people. Let me tell you my side of the story.
Law and order? What use do we have of that if we are always persecuted by them and do not even have the freedom to live our lives the way we want?
They are always looking for us, trying to oppress us in some way. Always trying to make our lives a little bit harder.
Good to hear that there still are some people willing to make a stand against Feygard. Let me tell you my side of the story.
Me and my boys here travelled from our home in Nor City to these northern lands a few days ago.
We had never been here ourselves. We had only heard stories about how tough the guards from Feygard were, and how they held their precious law above all.
Anyway, we got wind of a certain business opportunity here up north. One where we would be on the receiving end of a very profitable deal.

So we went here to conduct our business. Shortly thereafter, I guess the guards from Feygard must have been tipped off about us, since we noticed that we were being followed by the guards after a while.

Not willing to risk anything, considering the rumors we had heard about the guards from there, we did the only reasonable thing we could do - we abandoned the plan right away and left, before we could conduct the business we had planned.
However, something must have upset the guards there anyway. Now we hear that we are accused of murder and theft in Feygard, without even being there ourselves.

replies.text: I will not listen to your lies! For Feygard!
Your story does not add up.
I believe your story. How can I help you?

conversationlist_rogorn.message: I can't really say. We do our business on behalf of Nor City, and our business is our own.

replies.text: I will not listen to your lies! For Feygard!
Your story does not add up.
I believe your story. How can I help you?

conversationlist_rogorn.message: What are you, a spy for Feygard? I told you, the accusations against us are false.
Thank you for listening to our side of the story.

replies.text: What now? I was sent here to find you by some guards in the Crossroads guardhouse.

conversationlist_rogorn.message: You tell those guards that you searched for us, but did not find anyone.
You are back.

replies.text: Can you tell me your side of the story again?
I will not listen to your lies! You must be held accountable for your crimes against Feygard!
I believe your story. How can I help you?

conversationlist_rogorn.message: Thank you for listening to our side of the story.

conversationlist_gandoren.message: Hello there. Welcome to the Crossroads guardhouse. How may I help you?

replies.text: You guards seem to have a lot of equipment here, anything to trade?

conversationlist_gandoren.message: I'm sorry, we only trade with allies of Feygard.
This guardhouse is a safe haven for merchants travelling the Duleian road. We keep law and order around here, for Feygard.
Noticed the large road outside? That's the Duleian road. It goes all the way from the glorious city of Feygard up in the northwest down to the wretched Nor City in the southeast.
Oh sure. Recently, we have had to focus our attention to the troubles up in Loneford.
That situation has forced us to be more alert than usual, and we have had to send some guards up there to help them.
This also means that we cannot focus as much on our usual tasks as we normally do, but instead need help with doing basic tasks just to hold our grounds.

replies.text: What troubles in Loneford are you referring to?
Anything I can do to help?

conversationlist_gandoren.message: Hello again. Welcome to the Crossroads guardhouse. How may I help you?

replies.text: Can you tell me again what you told me before about recent events?

conversationlist_gandoren.message: Well, we usually do not employ just any civilian. Our tasks are important for Feygard - and by extension, important for the people. Our tasks are usually not suited for commoners like you.
But I guess the recent situation really leaves us no choice. We need to keep the guards in Loneford, and we also need to deliver this shipment. At the moment, we cannot do both.
Tell you what, you might be able to help us after all if you are willing to work.

replies.text: Anything for the glory of Feygard.
If the pay is sufficient, I guess I can help.
I had better not get involved in your Feygard business.

conversationlist_gandoren.message: I'm glad to hear that.
Pay? Oh, I guess we could pay you.
I need you to take a shipment of equipment to another one of our outposts further south on the Duleian road.
Those outposts further down south are in greater need of equipment than us, them being closer to that wretched Nor City and all.
Take this shipment of 10 iron swords to the guard captain stationed in a tavern called 'The Foaming Flask', near a village called Vilegard.

replies.text: No problem. Anything for the glory of Feygard.
You did not mention any amount that I would be paid.
Why should I help you people? I have only heard bad things about Feygard.
I had better not get involved in your Feygard business.

conversationlist_gandoren.message: Hello again. Welcome to the Crossroads guardhouse. How may I help you?

replies.text: What was that you told me before about a shipment?

conversationlist_gandoren.message: I'm sorry to hear that. Good day to you.
Bad things? Who have you been talking to then? I would urge you to make up your own opinion of Feygard by travelling there yourself.
Personally, I cannot think of a greater place to be than in Feygard. Order is kept and people are friendly.
As to why you would help us, I can only say that Feygard would be grateful for your services if you help us.

replies.text: Fine, whatever. I will carry your stupid swords. I still hope there will be some reward for this.
Sounds good to me. Anything for the glory of Feygard.
I had better not get involved in your Feygard business.

conversationlist_gandoren.message: Excellent.
I cannot promise you any amount on a reward.
OK then.
Here is the shipment that I want you to transport.
As I said, you should deliver those 10 iron swords to the guard captain stationed in a tavern called 'The Foaming Flask', near a village called Vilegard.
Return to me once you are done.
I feel that I should warn you about something also. See that fellow over there in the corner? Ailshara. She seems very interested in our dealings for some reason.
I would urge you to stay away from her at all costs. Whatever you do, do not speak to her about your mission with the shipment.
You return. Good news about the shipment I hope?

replies.text: You guards seem to have a lot of equipment here, anything to trade?
I am still working on transporting that shipment.
What was I supposed to do again?
Yes. I have delivered them as you ordered.
I'd rather talk about the troubles in Loneford that you had mentioned.

conversationlist_gandoren.message: I'm sorry, we only trade with allies of Feygard. Help me with the task I gave you and we might be able to work something out.
Splendid! Feygard is in debt to you.
Splendid! Feygard is in debt to you.
I hope you managed to stay away from the savages of Nor City as much as possible while being over there.
From what I hear, things are rough down south.
As for you, you have both my and the rest of the Feygard patrol's gratitude for helping us with this.
You return. Thank you for helping with the shipment earlier.
Is there anything I can do for you?

replies.text: Do you have anything to trade?

conversationlist_gandoren.message: Absolutely, as thanks for the help you provided earlier to both Minarra and me, we could agree to trade with you.
Go up in the lookout tower over there and talk to Minarra about equipment. She has our supply.
I hear that Minarra up in the lookout tower over there wants help with something. Why don't you go up to her and ask her about it, and we might be able to work something out after that.

conversationlist_ailshara.message: Hello again my Shadow friend. How may I help you?

replies.text: Let me see what you have to trade.

conversationlist_ailshara.message: Sigh, it's you. What do you want?

replies.text: Let me see what you have to trade.

conversationlist_ailshara.message: Psst, hey. Interested in doing some trading? I am always looking for acquiring ... well, items of others...

replies.text: Sure, let me see what you have.

conversationlist_ailshara.message: Oh yes. You see, these Feygard patrol guards carry some really interesting things. They don't seem to care much if some of their shipments ... well, disappear.

replies.text: OK, let me see what you have.
I should really not get involved in this. Goodbye.

conversationlist_ailshara.message: Psst, hey you! I saw you talking to Gandoren over there, and I happened to notice that you exchanged some items. Anything interesting?

replies.text: Never mind that, let me see what you have to trade.
I better not talk about it.
Gandoren specifically asked me not to talk to you about it.
Yes, Gandoren wants me to deliver some equipment for Feygard. Do you want a part of the deal?

conversationlist_ailshara.message: Hah, of course. Gandoren would not like it if I were to get a glimpse into his business. I assume you are helping him deliver those items somewhere. Tell me this, what did he promise you in return? Gold? Honor? No?

replies.text: Now that you mention it, he didn't actually say there would be a reward.
I am doing this for the glory of Feygard.
Helping Feygard seems like the right thing to do.

conversationlist_ailshara.message: As usual, Feygard keeps all its riches to itself. What if I were to tell you there was a way for you to gain from all this as well?

replies.text: I have no problem helping Feygard without any personal gain.
I better not get involved in this, goodbye.

conversationlist_ailshara.message: By the Shadow, you sound like one of those deceptive snobs from Feygard.
Shadow help you, child. You should question yourself whether you really are making the right choice here.
Let me tell you my plan. As you might know, everyone believes there will be some coming conflict between the deceptive snobs of Feygard and the glorious people of Nor City.
Any help we can bring to Nor City in this matter is welcome. These items that Gandoren gave you would be useful to our people in the southern lands.
These items, if you were to deliver them to our allies down in Vilegard, then the Shadow would look favorably upon you.
This way, the people could get back some piece of the riches that Feygard has stolen from all of us.
If you indeed are walking in the Shadow, then deliver these items to the smith in Vilegard. He will be able to make good use of them. He might also have some other task for you.

replies.text: I will see what I can do.
No. I will help Feygard instead.
Whatever, I choose my own path.

conversationlist_ailshara.message: Shadow be with you. May the Shadow guide you on the clouded paths that you walk.
Hello again. Did you deliver those items to the smith in Vilegard?

replies.text: Never mind that, let me see what you have to trade.
No. I will help Feygard instead.
Can you tell me again what I was supposed to do?

conversationlist_ailshara.message: Good. You should also try to convince Gandoren into thinking that you helped him.
Excellent! You do indeed walk with the Shadow my friend. I am glad to hear that there are at least a few decent folk still around.
Your help will be most appreciated by the people of Nor City, and you will be welcome among us.

conversationlist_vilegard_v0610.message: Oh, this is most unexpected but very welcome. I will not question how you acquired these items, but instead express my gratitude for bringing them to me.
Thank you for bringing me these items, they will be most useful to us here in the southern lands, and Vilegard in particular. We rarely get our hands on Feygard items, so these are really welcome.

replies.text: I was sent to deliver these items to a Feygard patrol stationed in the Foaming Flask tavern.

conversationlist_vilegard_v0610.message: Instead, you brought them to me. You have my thanks.
Hah, this means that we have another opportunity here. What if you were to deliver some other items to the Feygard patrol instead? Hah, this will really make my day.
I might have something that will do just fine... Let me just find them.
Here they are. Ha ha, these will do just fine for those deceiving Feygard snobs.
Take these items and deliver them to wherever you were supposed to deliver the items you gave me.
Excellent, I have been waiting for these. Thank you for bringing them to me.

conversationlist_crossroads_2.message: Welcome to the Crossroads guardhouse. I am Gallain, the proprietor of this place.

replies.text: Do you have anything to eat around here?
Is there any place I can rest here?

conversationlist_crossroads_2.message: As I said, this is the Crossroads guardhouse. The guards from Feygard are using this place as a place to rest and gear up.
Because of this, it is also a safe haven for merchants travelling through here. We get a lot of those.
The guards have set up some beds downstairs. Go check with them.
And who might you be? Come to sell me one of those trinkets that you people sell, eh?
No, let me guess - you want to know if I have any items to trade?
Let me tell you something. I do not want to buy anything from you, nor do I want to sell you anything. I just want to be left alone here, now that I have made it all the way to this safe haven.

I have travelled all the way from my home town of Sullengard, and on my way to Brimhaven, I have stopped at this place to get a break from all the commoners that always bother me with their trinkets and whatnots.
So, if you will excuse me, I really need my well deserved rest here. Without you bothering me.

replies.text: Wow, you're the friendly type aren't you?
I should put my sword through you for talking like that.
I'm here to give you a gift from Eryndor. He died, but I was told to give you something from him.

conversationlist_crossroads_2.message: Are you still around? Did you not listen to what I said?
Did you hear about what happened up in Loneford? The guards seem like a bunch of angry bees about it.

conversationlist_crossroads_3.message: Hello there. Can I help you?

replies.text: Mind if I use one of the beds over there?

conversationlist_crossroads_3.message: Hello again. I hope the bed is comfortable enough. Use it as much as you like.
No, sorry. These beds are for guards and allies of Feygard only.
Say, aren't you that kid that helped the guards down in Fallhaven? With the thieves that were planning an escape?

replies.text: Yes, I helped the guards in the prison find out about some plans that the thieves had.

conversationlist_crossroads_3.message: I knew I had heard about you somewhere. You are always welcome by us guards. You can use that second bed over there to the left if you need to rest.

replies.text: But there's a hole in the wall there. Where does it lead?

conversationlist_crossroads_3.message: Lead? Oh nowhere. Nothing back there at all.

replies.text: There's something you are not telling me.

conversationlist_crossroads_3.message: Oh no, no. Nothing interesting here. Move along now.

replies.text: How about I pay you 100 gold to move out of the way?

conversationlist_crossroads_3.message: You would do that? Hmm, let me think.
Look, you are not getting back there, and there is nothing to see back there.

replies.text: OK, final offer, 800 gold? That's a fortune.

conversationlist_crossroads_3.message: Hmm, 800 gold you say? Well, why didn't you say so from the start? Sure, that could work.
I should tell you however, that there is something in there that we won't dare go near. I just guard here to make sure it doesn't get out, and that no one goes in.
Some other guards went in there earlier, and came back screaming. Enter at your own risk, but don't say I didn't warn you.

replies.text: Never mind, I was just kidding.
Here is the gold, now get out of the way.

conversationlist_crossroads_3.message:
*Hssss*
[You hear squishing sounds as the creature starts moving towards you]

replies.text: You will not survive this, you pathetic creature.
A fight! I have been looking forward to this!

conversationlist_fields_1.message: Sorry, the road to Feygard is closed until further notice.
Crossroads guardhouse, housing for allies of Feygard.

Southeast: Nor City
Northwest: Feygard
East: Loneford
South: Fallhaven
The guard shouts at you: Hey! You cannot sleep here!

Welcome to peaceful Loneford.
[The sign also contains a drawing of a bale of hay with what looks like a farmer sitting on top]

conversationlist_loneford_1.message: What have we done to deserve this?
Didn't you hear about the illness?
It all started a few days ago. Selgan found Hesor passed out on his old crop field, completely white faced and shivering.
A few days later, Selgan started showing the same symptoms as Hesor, with stomach aches. I also started feeling the pains and got the shivers.
Then, all people showed the symptoms in one way or another.
Poor old Selgan and Hesor apparently got the worst of it, and both died the day before yesterday.
Cursed illness, why did it have to be Selgan and Hesor? I wonder who is next.
We all started to investigate what could be the cause. We still aren't certain what the cause is, but we have our suspicions.
Luckily, now Feygard has sent patrols up here to help guard the village at least. We are still suffering though, and we fear who will be taken by the illness next.
Please report any suspicious behavior you might see to Kuldan.
What have we done to deserve this? Please, will you help us?

replies.text: What do you think is the cause of the illness?

conversationlist_loneford_1.message: My guess is that this must be something done by those arrogant people from Feygard.
They are always looking for ways to make our lives a little bit harder.
We try to farm our lands to feed ourselves, but they demand that they get a share of whatever we bring in.
Lately, the crops haven't been as good as they used to be, and the guards apparently think we are withholding some part of their share.
I am sure that they did something to us as punishment for not following their *rules*. They are always talking about how the laws and rules are so precious to them.
There's something else also. I talked to that drunk, Landa, in the tavern earlier today. He said he saw something but didn't dare tell me what it was.

replies.text: Thank you, I will go talk to him.
Great, another drunk that I have to talk to.

conversationlist_loneford_2.message: We keep the order around here. I wonder what the people of Loneford would do without us guards from Feygard. Poor things.
*cough* Please help us, soon there won't be many left of us!
I can't feel my face anymore, please help us!
Don't disturb me, I need to finish chopping this wood. Go bother someone else.

replies.text: Do you by any chance have some fences?
Do you by any chance have some fences?
Unfortunately the fences you gave me are not tall enough. Do you have others?
The Craftsman told me that I should get some wood from you.

conversationlist_loneford_2.message: I fear for our survival. It seems we are getting worse every day that passes. It's a good thing Feygard helps us at least.
Don't I know you from somewhere? You look familiar somehow.
Wha? You!? No, get away from me!

replies.text: I heard that you saw something that you won't talk about.

conversationlist_loneford_2.message: [Landa gives you a terrified look]
You were there! I ssssaw you!

Or was it you? No, it looked like you, and I have a good memory!
[Bites lip]
Get away from me, whatever you did over there, it's your business and I don't want any trouble!

replies.text: You must have me confused with someone else.

conversationlist_loneford_2.message: Please don't hurt me!

replies.text: Landa, you must have me confused with someone else! What was it you saw?

conversationlist_loneford_2.message: No, you are smaller than him.

replies.text: Are you going to tell me what it was you saw?

conversationlist_loneford_2.message: The boy. He was doing something. I tried to sneak up closer to see what it was he was doing, I did. But he ran away before I could see.
He did something by the well here in Loneford.
It was in the middle of the night, on the day before everything started. The day after, I was sleeping it off during the day, so I didn't notice all the turmoil about when they brought Hesor back.
Almost the whole village wanted to see what had happened to Hesor. I kept to myself and didn't dare talk to anyone.
The same day, others started to get pale as well. I could see it in their faces.
The following night, I was getting ready to go to the well myself to look for any traces of what the boy had done.

I peeked out the window to see if there was anyone that might see me. Instead, I saw someone skulking around the well, filling up several vials with both dirt around the well, and water from the well itself.
I am sure it was Buceth, from the chapel. I have a good eye for people, and a good memory. Yes, I am sure it was Buceth.
Also, isn't it strange how Buceth has not gotten ill, while all the others in the village have gotten ill?
He must be up to something. He and that boy that looked like you. Are you sure it wasn't you?
Never mind. Please don't tell anyone that I told you all this.

Now, get out of here kid, before anyone sees you talking to me.
[Looks around anxiously]

replies.text: Thank you Landa. Your secret is safe with me.
Thank you Landa. I'll consider it.
Are you done? Phew, I thought you were never going to stop talking.

conversationlist_loneford_2.message: You again? I already told you. Get out of here before anyone sees you talking to me.

conversationlist_buceth.message: You again. Thank you for the gold earlier.
Welcome back my friend. Walk with the Shadow.
Shadow be with you.

replies.text: I know of your business at the well the night after the illness broke out.
Can you tell me more about the Shadow?

conversationlist_buceth.message: Oh, I am sure you do. But what proof do you have, eh? Anything the guards would believe?
Let me ask you something first, and we might talk after that.

replies.text: How about some gold, would that make you talk?

conversationlist_buceth.message: Let me start by telling you a story.

replies.text: Let me guess, this story is going to take forever to listen to. How about I give you some gold, and instead we can discuss what you were doing at the well.

conversationlist_buceth.message: Hmm, that might be an interesting proposal. How much gold are you suggesting?
Hrmpf. Thanks for the gold, but I am not interested in talking to you. Now, please leave.
You seem to realize the true value of the Shadow. Yes, this will do fine, thank you.
Let's assume you live in a village that, for the most part, keeps to itself. Your village is self-sustainable and the crops have been good for some years.
With the few exceptions of some fights here and there between villagers because of misunderstandings, on the whole, your village is a friendly, peaceful village.
You work in the same profession as your parents, which in turn worked in the same professions as their parents.
Let's also assume that the way you conduct your business is the same way that the people in the village have been conducting their business for generations past.
Everyone respects one another in the village, and your appointed leader does a good job at keeping everyone's interests satisfied, while at the same time being reasonably fair.
Then, one day, a group of men come walking into the village. Shining armor, white teeth, combed hair, trimmed beards.
The men claim that their lord owns this land, including your village.
They claim that they keep the land safe of wrongdoers and evil creatures.
For their help in protecting your village, they ask that the village compensate them with a share of the harvest.
Now, tell me. Would you support those men by agreeing to their terms?
I am sorry to hear that. You should make up your mind and return to me once you have done so. Then we might be able to talk more.

replies.text: How about I give you some gold instead?

conversationlist_buceth.message: How interesting.
Let me continue the story of our hypothetical case.
A while later, the men return. They explain that some of the ways things are done in the village have now been prohibited across the whole land.
Without going into specifics, let's say that these are ways that have been used for past generations in your village.
Changing the way things are done will require quite an effort for people to adjust. A lot of people in the village are upset because of this news from the men.
Now, tell me. Would you in secret continue using the old ways your past generations have used, or would you instead convert to the ways that the men are advocating?

replies.text: I would continue using the old ways in secret.
I would continue using the old ways, and fight the ruling that prohibited them in the first place.
I would only use the ways that are allowed.
I can't decide without knowing the specifics.

conversationlist_buceth.message: How interesting.
I am glad to hear that there are people still around that are willing to stand up for what is right.
How interesting. You have a different view of the world than what I and the priests of Nor City have.
You are of course entitled to your opinion, but you should know that your opinion might conflict with the Shadow.
You wanted to know about some business that you accuse me of. Since you have no proof, I will claim innocence. I know that my conscience is clean.

replies.text: Fine. How about I give you some gold instead, would that make you talk?

conversationlist_buceth.message: Your views match those that I and the other priests from Nor City believe in. Tell me, would you be interested in following the glow of the Shadow?

replies.text: I am ready to follow the Shadow.
How can I agree to something without knowing what it entails?
No, I will go my own way.
No, I will go my own way. Your stupid Shadow is nothing but talk and fancy words.
(Lie) I am ready to follow the Shadow.

conversationlist_buceth.message: If the answers you gave previously were indeed your views, then I can assure you that the path that is guided by the Shadow is the right one.

replies.text: I am ready to follow the Shadow.
No, I will go my own way.
No, I will go my own way. Your stupid Shadow is nothing but talk and fancy words.
(Lie) I am ready to follow the Shadow.

conversationlist_buceth.message: I am sorry to hear that. I guess we do not share views after all.
I am glad to hear that, but then again, I had a feeling all along that you would say that.
You wanted to ask me something?

replies.text: What were you doing at the well during the night?

conversationlist_buceth.message: Let me first tell you my background.

I am appointed by the priests of Nor City to help guide the people of Loneford towards the Shadow. Our mission is to see that the Shadow casts its glow over Loneford as well as other settlements around here.

Most folk in these northern parts seem too occupied with obeying the will of Feygard and Lord Geomyr. We want to help people see the light of the wrongdoings that Feygard advocates, and to point out the errors in their ways.
That's my mission here. To see that the Shadow casts its glow over Loneford.

replies.text: How does this relate to what you were doing at the well?

conversationlist_buceth.message: Nor City sent word to me that something was about to happen here in Loneford. Something that would help our cause.
They were sending a boy to do some business here, and I was assigned to make sure that the mission was successful.

replies.text: Do you know where he went after he left Loneford?

conversationlist_buceth.message: I was tasked with gathering samples from the water in the well and from the ground around the well. Also, I was given some vials whose contents should be poured into the well.
Apparently, the boy they sent was successful in his mission. The task that I did was also successful, if I may say so myself.
So, currently, that's where we stand now. The deed is done, and the Shadow will look favorably upon us.

replies.text: So, the well was poisoned, that's horrible. How could you?

conversationlist_buceth.message: Horrible!? What is horrible? What those people from Feygard are doing - that's what's horrible!
Now, I ask you to keep this story just between us two. You understand that, right?

replies.text: I promise not to tell anyone.
No, I will report you to the guard.

conversationlist_buceth.message: I urge you to rethink your reasoning. The way of the Shadow is the righteous way.

replies.text: Very well. I promise not to tell anyone.
No. Your crimes will be punished!

conversationlist_buceth.message: Infidel, you will not defeat me! For the Shadow!
Thank you, my friend.
If you want to learn more about the Shadow, please visit the chapel custodian in Nor City. Tell them I sent you, and they will surely extend their gratitude towards you.
Welcome back my friend. May you bask in the glow of the Shadow.

replies.text: Do you know anything about the illness here in Loneford?
Do you have anything to trade?
I need some help finding out who is responsible for casting a Shadow spell that causes a person to become noticeable.
Sorry, we were interrupted. You were just talking about the Striking Spectacle Shadow spell.
Here I've brought you the things that you require for the dispelling.
Do you know the whereabouts of Sly Seraphina?
I've brought you the things you had required for dispelling.
Borvis said you could provide me with some information.
The blessing has worn off too early. Could you give it again?

conversationlist_talion.message: The people of Loneford are very keen on following the will of Feygard, whatever it may be.
Normally, this would not be a problem. But Lord Geomyr seems to have something against the Shadow. He will do almost anything to oppose all actions that in some way extend the reach of the Shadow.
Because of this, the people of Loneford are now actively abolishing the thought of the Shadow guiding them through their lives.
People around here would rather follow the law of Feygard than follow the old ways.
My feeling is that this illness is caused by the Shadow, as punishment to all of us here in Loneford.

replies.text: Do you know anything about the illness?

conversationlist_taevinn.message: I'll tell you what I know. We try to follow the law around here. Without rules and laws, how would we be any different from the savages that roam the southern lands?
But even if we here in Loneford keep as peaceful as possible, there's always someone that has a desire to cause mischief.

Have you seen him? That fool Sienn. Him and his 'pet' are always trying to cause some trouble. We can't have that around here in our friendly village. Especially not in times like these when we are trying to show our good side to those magnificent guards from Feygard that are here.
Did you know I tried to talk to him on several occasions about his so called 'pet'? I couldn't really make out what he was trying to tell me, but that thing of his nearly tried to kill me, it did!

I tell you, there's mischief all around him and that thing he keeps around. I am sure they are up to something. They probably caused this illness somehow. Maybe we caught something contagious from that thing of his that he keeps around?

conversationlist_loneford_kuldan.message: Please report any suspicious behavior you might see.

replies.text: I know what the cause of the illness is. Have a look at this vial that Buceth had on him.

conversationlist_loneford_kuldan.message: I am Kuldan, captain of this here detachment of guards in Loneford. Now, if you will excuse me, I have work to do.
Feygard is grateful for your assistance in solving the mystery of the illness here in Loneford.
We are trying to help the last few people that are still ill here now. Loneford might require our assistance from Feygard for quite some time.
What is this? This smells like Narwood poison. You say you retrieved this from Buceth?

replies.text: Buceth was part of a mission by the Nor City priests to poison the water well here in Loneford.

conversationlist_loneford_kuldan.message: But this means ... it is the water that the people are getting ill from? This explains a lot of things.
You my friend have done Loneford a great service by finding this, and by extension, Feygard as well. We should go catch Buceth for what he has done.
Dead you say? Hmm, not quite the way we do things in Feygard, but I guess this is an exceptional case.
I always suspected that those savages from Nor City were behind this all along.
It's good to know that we now at least have some evidence to back up our claims.
As for Loneford, I guess we will have to start bringing in water from Feygard to help the people here. Good thing they have us around, what would they do otherwise?

And you, my friend - you should of course be sufficiently rewarded for your assistance in this matter. You should travel to the glorious city of Feygard to the northwest and report to the castle steward there for further instructions.
I happen to know the castle steward personally, and I will send word to him about your help here.
For the glory of Feygard, the people of Loneford may live on thanks to your help.

conversationlist_loneford_3.message: Ha! You look funny. You small.

replies.text: What is that thing you are keeping around?
What is that thing you are keeping around?

conversationlist_loneford_3.message:
Pet, cute!
[Sienn makes cuddly sounds while scratching the pet under its chin]

replies.text: Did you know that Taevinn thinks you caused the illness here in Loneford?

conversationlist_loneford_3.message:
Aaargh!
[The creature looks up at you, showing all its teeth, while making a high-pitched piercing sound]
Hello there. Have you come to browse my selection of items?

replies.text: What's the deal with Sienn over there with his pet?

conversationlist_loneford_3.message: I don't know where he got it from. Anyway, they don't harm anyone, so I'm fine with them being in here. I figured someone should help them have some place to stay, and no one else wanted to help them, so I let them stay here.
Sienn may be a bit thick, but he sure can be funny when you get to know him and he trusts you. He can do a lot of those hilarious facial expressions.

conversationlist_loneford_4.message: Hello and welcome to Loneford. Please have a seat, I'll be right there.

replies.text: Do you have anything to eat around here?
Is there a place where I can get some rest around here?

conversationlist_loneford_4.message: Sure, the guards have set up some beds downstairs. Go talk to Arngyr down there, he might be able to help you.

Arngyr grabs you by the shoulder and pulls you back.
If you want to rest over there, you need to check with me first.

replies.text: Mind if I use one of the beds back there?

conversationlist_loneford_4.message: Oh no, not at all. Go ahead. After all you have done for us here in Loneford, it would be a privilege to be able to give something back to you.
These beds are mostly used by us guards. But I guess I could make an exception since you're just a kid. Shall we say, 600 gold and you may use it?

replies.text: What?! That's a bit much, don't you think?

conversationlist_loneford_4.message: Use the bed in the back over there as much as you like.
Look, kid. I make the rules around here. If that's my price then that's my price. Take it or leave it.
Hello again. I hope the bed is comfortable enough.
Oh, poor old Selgan. Why did it have to be him? I wonder who is next, and I fear for the worst.
I can't see how we could make it without the help of those nice guards from Feygard around here. We are truly lucky to have their assistance.
We are lucky to have Feygard here helping us.
Who are you? Have you seen my father Selgan? They all tell me he will be back shortly, but they are all lying! I know it, I know it! He wasn't home yesterday, and he isn't home today.
This is no place for a kid like you. I think you had better leave now.

replies.text: I met a man named Forlin who recommended that I speak with you in regards to a possible murder investigation that I am conducting.
I did as you suggested and found the scene of a murder and I found this glove.

conversationlist_pwcave.message: Get away! No! Turn back while you still can!
You don't know what they'll do to you!

Fourth is Emerei, that can probably be found in his house to the southeast of Remgard.
