conversationlist_algangror.message: You see, I used to live in the city of Remgard. The times were good, and the city prospered.
Our crops grew well, and some people had very fortunate trading agreements with other cities, making the life for most of us living in Remgard very easy.
I even sold some of the baskets that I used to make to a wealthy merchant that visited us from Nor City.
However, even the easy life gets boring after a while. I believe it is in our nature to strive for new and better things, to free us from the boredom of day-to-day life.
I wanted to learn more of things that I knew nothing about, and wanted to explore things I had only read of in books before.
So I went to Nor City myself, and visited many ... interesting people and ... dark corners.
Naturally, I was thrilled of the knowledge I gained from the experience, and from what I learned while there.
As I got back home, I wanted to continue practicing what I had observed and learned while in Nor City.
You could say I got obsessed with learning more. I guess the others living in Remgard did not ... share my enthusiasm. Some of them even questioned the fact that I wanted to learn more.
So I told myself that others would not hinder me in my curiosity to better myself.
Those books that I bought from the Blackmarrow residence in Nor City - I must have read them all perhaps five times over. This was something completely new to me, and at the same time very exciting.
For some reason, the others in Remgard started giving me strange looks, and I could hear the whispers behind my back.
I was even barred from the tavern. 'People come here for a good time, and we don't want people like you here ruining that' they said. What fools they are.
I heard one woman whispering to her boy, 'Don't look at her, she'll turn you to stone!'. Others just turned the other way when they met me.
What fools they are.
One day, Jhaeld showed up at my doorstep with a group of guards.
The people of Remgard had decided that I could not stay there anymore, he said. The things I did were causing other people harm, he said.
What had I done, I asked myself? I had never hurt anyone, much less affected anyone with my ... experiments. Am I not allowed to do what I wish?
I had little chance to argue, however. The guards led me out of the city. They did not even let me gather my things. All my books, all my notes and all my findings - gone. I lost everything.
All this happened several seasons ago. I knew I had to get revenge for what they did to me.
Oh, how I despise them all. The people that gave me those looks, the people that whispered behind my back, and most of all that fool Jhaeld.
So, I decided to extend my ... experiments ... to larger things. To people, to living things. This is the perfect opportunity to learn even more than what is in the books.
To think that I could do it while at the same time get revenge on those despicable people - it's an excellent plan, if I may say so myself. He he.

replies.text: So, what happened to all those people that have gone missing?

conversationlist_algangror.message: I lured them here. Once I managed to trap them, I placed a curse on them that, in theory, should have only made them unable to speak.
Maybe I haven't understood everything correctly from the books that I have read, since instead of making them unable to speak, they were all turned into rats instead.
Practice makes perfect, I suppose. Ha ha.

replies.text: Wait, does this mean that those rats I killed for you were...

conversationlist_algangror.message: Oh yes. With your help, they are now one less problem to deal with, so to speak. He he.

replies.text: I understand, and I agree with your actions.

conversationlist_algangror.message: Thank you. It is good to know there are more people interested in learning more.

conversationlist_remgard_bridgeguard.message: Halt! No one is allowed to enter or exit Remgard.
Wrong? You bet there is. Several of the townspeople have disappeared, and we are still conducting the investigation.
We are searching for them in the town, and questioning everyone for clues on where they might be.
No, I highly doubt that.

Considering our town is surrounded by lake Laeroth, we guards are able to keep a watchful eye on everything going on here. We are able to keep a log of who comes and goes, since this bridge is our only connection to the mainland.
For your sake, it is probably safer for you to remain out of town until our investigation is complete.

replies.text: I am willing to help you with the investigation if you want.

conversationlist_remgard_bridgeguard.message: No. As I said, no one except us guards are allowed to enter or exit town until our investigation is completed. I suggest you leave now.

There is an abandoned house some way to the east of here, on a peninsula on the northern shore of lake Laeroth.

We have reason to believe that this cabin is inhabited by someone, since we have seen candlelight coming from there during the night across the lake. We are not certain though, it could just be the moonlight on the water.
That's where you come in, and might be able to help us.
I must stay here and guard the bridge, but you could go over there and peek inside.
Now, I must warn you - this could be dangerous. If it is as we suspected, then the person in the cabin could be a ... shall we say ... persuasive talker.
So, if you really want to help us, the task I ask of you is that you only peek inside that cabin and identify if there's anyone there, and if so who that might be.
Report back to me as soon as possible, and do not speak for too long with anyone that might be there.
Would you be willing to do this task for us?

You can probably find him in the tavern to the southeast, since that's where he spends most of his time.

replies.text: You are welcome. Anything else I can help you with?

conversationlist_remgard_bridgeguard.message: I guess you have proven yourself to be useful. We might have more work for you if you are interested.

The writings on it have almost vanished, but I have managed to read parts of it. It speaks in an ancient Kazaul tongue, so all parts are not clear to me.
I am sure that this shrine is part of the cause for these ... these ... things ... that lurk in this cave. I will do anything in my power to defeat whatever mischief that comes from it.

replies.text: How come these creatures do not attack you?
What have you translated so far?

conversationlist_ulirfendor.message: Ah, the allaceph. I had not seen one for many years until I entered this cave. They are a remnant of the guardians of Kazaul.
Have you noticed how they seem to feed upon whoever tries to fight them? Cursed things, almost got a hold of me, they did.

replies.text: How come these creatures do not attack you?
What have you translated from the shrine so far?

conversationlist_ulirfendor.message: I have placed a blessing of the Shadow upon this small island here, so that I may work uninterrupted. Strangely enough, it seems to be very effective on them.
They seem to be very cautious about it. So far, not even one has dared to approach me. Even those pesky lizards are keeping their distance.

replies.text: What have you translated from the shrine so far?

conversationlist_ulirfendor.message: It speaks of Kazaul and of the misery that comes to anyone that opposes the will of Kazaul.
Something about 're-birth from within the followers'. Not sure I have translated that part correctly, but I think that is what it says. Definitely something about re-birth or birth.
It also speaks of someone or some ... thing called the 'Dark protector'. Most parts of the text for that is missing from the shrine however.
Whatever it means, it seems important. It is also obvious that the 'Dark protector' brings power to Kazaul, and misery to any opposition.

Regardless, it must be stopped, whatever it means. Maybe it refers to something deeper down this cave? I have not ventured further into the cave to the east since I could not get past those ... things.
Forgive me, I must continue translating the few readable parts left on this shrine.

replies.text: Would you like any help with that?

conversationlist_ulirfendor.message: Thank you. Goodbye.
Hmm, maybe. I need to figure out what this last part should be. Hmm...
The last part of this piece has been eroded from the rock. It begins with 'Kulauil hamar urum Kazaul'te'. But what is the rest of that?
Argh, if this cave wasn't so damp, I bet the rest of the text would still be there.

replies.text: I could go look for other clues about the missing parts if you want?

conversationlist_ulirfendor.message: Sure, you do that.
I have looked thoroughly for any clues in the western part of this cave, but have not found any. I have not entered the eastern parts of the cave however.

Also, I should warn you that I believe the shrine talks of a powerful creature somewhere in this cave. Maybe if you find that creature, it will provide some clue as to what the missing parts are? You need to be careful though.

replies.text: I will go look in the eastern parts of the cave then.

conversationlist_ulirfendor.message: Hello again. Did you find any clues about what the missing parts are?

replies.text: No, I have not found any clues yet.

conversationlist_ulirfendor.message: If you really want to help, then please go look for any other clues you might find.

replies.text: It's not that bad. I have had worse.

conversationlist_aulowenn.message: For Feygard!
Halt! Do not come any closer. The contents of these crates is property of Feygard.

replies.text: I mean you no harm. Who are you?
Sure. I'll just stay right here. Who are you?

conversationlist_aulowenn.message: I am Aulowenn of Feygard.

replies.text: What are you doing out here?

conversationlist_aulowenn.message: I'm guarding these crates. That's what I do. At least until my company gets back from their scouting party.
Oh I hope they do get back. Come to think of it, they have been away for quite some time now.
I sure hope they are well. Unlike the others...
In my squad, we were a band of six guards that, together with other squads, were sent out here to find a dangerous madman that takes his refuge somewhere in the nearby hills around here.
But something started to happen once we got here. Some of my fellow guards started acting ... odd.
I don't know if it was just me imagining things or if something truly happened to them. Anyway, one by one, we started to get fewer and fewer.
Some of my men were killed by the creatures that live in these woods, some ran away by themselves and some have never come back from their scouting trips.

replies.text: What do you think has happened to them?

conversationlist_aulowenn.message: I have two theories. My first thought is that some of the local creatures that we've been having problems with here might have captured them, or even killed them. I know for a fact that some were killed by the creatures, since we even buried some of my men to the east of here, but I am not certain of the others.
The creatures in these woods are intelligible, but fierce. Luckily, we've been able to kill them off before they've been able to spew their foul lies. There are still a few of them around though.
My second theory is that the madman that we are looking for must have done something to them. Maybe the madman has smeared some of his madness onto them.
Regardless, there isn't much that I am able to do here. I need to guard these crates.
Also, I do hope that those creatures that seem to live here don't return. They've been a real pest.

replies.text: Anything I can do to help?

conversationlist_aulowenn.message: Oh yes, would you? There is one thing you could do.
As I mentioned, some of my men were killed by the local creatures here. We buried them to the east of here.
I haven't been there for a few days now, but last I visited the graves, there was one of those foul creatures standing over the graves.
I've seen that particular creature there before, it seems to be haunting the graves of my fellow men.
Of course, it must be up to no good. I would like your help in either removing or defeating that thing.

replies.text: So, you want me to go visit the graves to the east and defeat whatever creature is there?

conversationlist_aulowenn.message: Yes, that's it. I should also warn you that those creatures are intelligible, so I would urge you to act quickly when encountering it, before it can spew its foul lies.

I should leave before there is more bloodshed.

replies.text: You will be no match for me.

Thank you for finding our missing people!

replies.text: What do you think caused the monsters to appear?

conversationlist_kantya.message: I told them we shouldn't be digging deeper!
But they did anyway. Now, look what it got us.
It all started with a few of the miners coming back from their shift. They reported having found some sort of markings on the ground.
Strange markings. Unnatural. Nothing like we've seen before.
We don't know. No one could make any sense of them, not even Morenavia. I told them all that we should just leave it be.
But they didn't listen.
Then some people started hearing strange noises coming from below the ground around those markings. Almost like there was something below - a cavern or something.
Strange noises filled the whole mine, loud rumbles and shrieking noises from within the rock.
They wanted to find out what was below those markings.
So they started breaking through further down.
I wasn't there myself, but I heard from some of the miners. As they broke through, there was a rush of air and a clattering noise, almost like claws, coming from the dark hole beneath.
Below the ground with the markings, there was a cavern, just as they had suspected.
A foul sulfurous smell crept into the mine, most likely coming from that cavern.
They started hearing chattering in strange voices from inside the opening.
Then they saw it. As I've heard it, it all started as a small flame from within the dark cavern.
The flame grew stronger, and more lights appeared.
Out of the dark, they came. Out from the depths of the mine.
Those foul smelling things.
I told everyone that we shouldn't have breached that deep. We should have stopped when we first saw those markings on the ground.
Those markings must have been some sort of warning.

replies.text: Is that how this all started?

conversationlist_kantya.message: Yes. Whatever was in that cavern, we should not have let it out. Maybe that way, Morenavia and Ayell would still be alive.

I like that. That way, I am not bothered, like I used to be.
Oh yes, I too grew up in the city. But that life is behind me.
Right now, this suits me well. I hope there won't be any more ... disturbances, like the one you helped with.
No! Get that thing away from me, I want nothing to do with it. I can almost hear the cries of the many lives that that thing has taken.
I tell you - that thing should be destroyed.

replies.text: I think I'll hold on to it a bit longer.

conversationlist_lodar.message: You should go see the smith in Vile ... haven? Vile ... fall? Argh, I'm not very good at names.
Vilegard - yes, that's the place. You should go see the smith there. He might be able to guide you further.
Anyway, It's good that you defeated the Hira'zinn. I can't imagine what could have happened if the Hira'zinn would have given that thing into the wrong hands.
Oh yes. These are the ones I have available right now. If you want, I can also create some other special potions for you.

replies.text: Let me see the ones you have.

conversationlist_lodar.message: Yes, yes. I have some even more interesting recipes that I might be able to mix for you. However, I am all out of some of the most important ingredients for them.
If you want me to mix them for you, you'll have to help me get those ingredients.
Yes, were you able to get some of that Spotted Hornbeam fungus from the potion-maker in Fallhaven?

replies.text: No, not yet. I'd like to see what potions you have available right now.

conversationlist_lodar.message: Oh yes, this will do nicely. Good, good. Thank you, my friend.

With your help, I can now create additional potions from the remains of certain animals if you would like.
Actually, the most important ingredient is the one that I am out of. Most of the potent mixtures that I know of require the spores from the Spotted Hornbeam fungus.
And that, my friend, is not easy to come by here in the forest. Believe me, I have scoured the nearby forest in search for it, and I have even tried to cultivate some of it myself, to no avail.
However, I can imagine that the merchants in the larger settlements might have some.

replies.text: Do you want me to find you some of that fungus?

conversationlist_lodar.message: Yes please. Maybe the potion-maker in that Fall-something town has some? Fall ... brim? Fall ... port?

conversationlist_lodar.message: Yes, that's what I was looking for. Fallhaven. Go visit him and ask him if he has some. I am sure he has some, if you know enough to ask.

replies.text: I'd like to see what regular potions you have available.

conversationlist_lodar.message: Ah yes, the Hira'zinn. It nearly had me fully in its grasp as well.

replies.text: You seem a bit crazy to me.

conversationlist_lodar.message: That's the effect of the Hira'zinn. Its desire is to consume the minds of all it finds.
I have only heard of it through tales in books. It has been many generations ago since it last showed itself.
Last time it crept up on the world, it got its grip on whole villages, I've read. People were fighting their own brethren, after having been consumed by the Hira'zinn.
Imagine, sisters and brothers fighting, husbands and wives going at each others throats, all because the Hira'zinn had twisted their minds.

replies.text: Let's go back to the other questions.
What caused it to appear the last time?
Hah, those people seem like weaklings. That thing was no match for me, I could have defeated it while blindfolded even.

conversationlist_lodar.message: Now, don't be so quick to underestimate the Hira'zinn. It has many tricks up its sleeve.

replies.text: Let's go back to the other questions.
What caused it to appear the last time?

conversationlist_lodar.message: I do not know. The tales I have read do not tell how or why it all started - only that there was some kind of conflict going on at that time.
The wise men during those days also spoke of having seen some sort of signs before things got worse.
I don't know. Something about some rocks turning to life. Sounds like crazy-talk to me.

replies.text: Yes, maybe they too were affected by the Hira'zinn?
I saw some odd looking rock formations on my way here through the forest. Some of them even seemed to have some inner glow in them.

conversationlist_lodar.message: Yes, they might have been.
Anyway, it's good that you defeated that thing.
Formations of rocks you say? Hmm. I don't recall seeing any of that the last time I ventured out.
Could that be how the Hira'zinn extends its reach?
Yes, that would explain a great deal. The tales speak of it slowly creeping up on the world.
It could be that those formations are the way it gets closer to the people and things that it wants to consume.
It could be that the Hira'zinn has some way of affecting the life of the forest itself, causing these formations to appear.
That's what I think, at least.

replies.text: You still sound a bit crazy to me.

conversationlist_lodar.message: Oh, you must be referring to that older boy that was here recently.

replies.text: You've seen him? Andor has been here?

conversationlist_lodar.message: He did not tell me his name, but he had some similarities to how you look. Yes, then he probably was the person you are looking for.
You say his name is Andor? That's an odd name, don't you think?
Anyway, enough of that. What would you like to know?
Well, even from the first time I saw him, I knew something odd was going on.
He seemed overly friendly to me, almost like he seemed to know me already.
You should know that most people that stumble into my cabin here have either been lost in the maze some time, or are just happy to see another living being.
He showed no such signs. Almost like he knew who I was and that he expected me to be here.
He very kindly asked for some Narwood extract.

replies.text: I recognize that name 'Narwood extract' from somewhere.

conversationlist_lodar.message: It can be used to make quite a nasty poison.

replies.text: Oh right. I've visited a village whose town well had been poisoned with that.

conversationlist_lodar.message: Those poor poor people. They have my sympathies. I hope it's not my things that brought this misery upon them.

replies.text: Please continue your story about Andor.

conversationlist_lodar.message: So, he asked for a sample of Narwood extract. Normally, I wouldn't give that out to just anyone.
However, as I said, there was something odd about this whole meeting. I actually felt a bit threatened, even though he was so polite and friendly.
Fearing something would happen to me if I rejected his request, I reluctantly gave him a small sample of the Narwood extract.
He gladly accepted the sample, and left shortly after. That's when it started to get even more odd.
As he left, I happened to glance out the window. There, in the forest I saw the bright flash of the light from the sun hitting a blade.
If I hadn't seen that light coming off the blade, I would not have spotted the person there at all. He seemed to be hiding in the forest.

replies.text: Someone was hiding in the forest?

conversationlist_lodar.message: Yes, so it would seem. It was quite obvious that he did not want me to spot him. After your brother left, I saw them both speak some words to each other, before they both left together.

replies.text: So, Andor was here, wanted some Narwood extract, and he was travelling with someone that did not want you to spot him?

conversationlist_lodar.message: Yes, that's basically it. But that's not all.
Shortly after they left, strange things started happening in the forest.
I saw a pack of wolves that were fighting each other. Tearing up each others sides, and eating the remains.
I saw birds flying over my cabin, totally covered in red blood. Blood covered birds - now that's something that I have not even heard about.
I tell you, something affected the forest. Myself, I felt my stomach turning even more often than it usually does.
I had this strong urge to eat more than usual. I even found myself having lapses of time where I could not remember what I had done for the past couple of hours.

replies.text: What could have been causing that?

conversationlist_lodar.message: In hindsight, I think it's pretty clear what started to happen. The Hira'zinn awoke. To make matters worse, at least for me, it awoke in the tomb beneath my cabin here.
What I find disturbing is that this all started to happen right after your brother and that other person were here.
Maybe they visited that tomb. Now, I'm not pointing any fingers here, but it certainly seems like they had something to do with this, considering that the tomb has been quiet for ages.

replies.text: Are you implying that Andor awoke the Hira'zinn?
I don't think I like where you're going with this. Andor is my brother, and he would never do such a thing.

conversationlist_lodar.message: I don't know the details of course, and I have no proof. I only know that asking for Narwood extract is an odd request, and that the Hira'zinn started to creep up on me shortly after that.
Now, I am no expert in these things. I have only read bits and pieces from old books. I mostly focus my thoughts on herbs, mixtures and potions.
But I do know other people that might be able to provide you with further guidance.
Since you defeated the Hira'zinn, I think those people would be more than happy to speak to you. I would be happy to help you in any way I can too, of course.

replies.text: Who do you have in mind?

conversationlist_lodar.message: Seek out Lady Lydalon in the Valanyr temple of the Shadow in Nor City. She is one of the wisest people I know, and an excellent mentor.
Here, take this letter.
Present the letter to the guards at the temple, and they will grant you an audience with Lady Lydalon.
Also, while you're there, please give her my warmest regards. It has been too long since I last visited her.

replies.text: I will go to Nor City and visit Lady Lydalon in the Valanyr temple of the Shadow.
He he, a temple. That must mean a lot of riches in there.

conversationlist_lodar.message: Show some respect will you?
Just one more thing.
The person that was hiding among the trees here, that your brother was travelling with - I happened to get a quick view of his cloak.
I've seen cloaks like that before. The fabric is similar to a fabric commonly used in Nor City.
It could mean that whatever group of people he belongs to - there might be more of them in Nor City. Either you might want to stay away from them, or seek them out. You decide.

replies.text: Thank you for all the information. I will travel to Nor City.

conversationlist_lodar.message: You have done a great deed here. Goodbye. Take care, my friend.
Hmm, I remember seeing a cave under the former cave of the Hira'zinn. I don't know where it leads to but maybe you could give it a try and search for a shortcut through this cave?

replies.text: Thanks for your advice! I'll check it out!

conversationlist_lodar.message: Hmm, this is interesting. I have heard of such artifacts being teleporters but have never seen one myself. Here, take this vial and pour it over the torch. We will see what happens. I should tell you that this may be very dangerous. The artifact could respond differently than I think and could even kill you.

replies.text: Thanks, I'll try it. Danger is my specialty.
I hope it will be OK.

conversationlist_lodar.message: Well, that's great to hear. But don't tell this to anybody else because I don't want to have some Feygard soldiers in front of my house one day.

replies.text: Sure, this will be a secret between us.
[Lie] Sure, this will be a secret between us.

conversationlist_lodar.message: Sure feel free to use any bed in the main hall you like.

conversationlist_lodar0g.message: He he, but funny not enough to let you pass.
Master says only ones with password can pass. You have password?

replies.text: No, I don't have the password.
[Lie] Your master has allowed me to get through without the password.
'By the moon and stars, the path is laid clear to me.'

conversationlist_lodar0g.message: [The guardian pushes you away and shakes its head]
[The creature moves out of the way, and gestures with its hands almost like it is welcoming you further into the forest]

conversationlist_lodarfg.message: You there! What are you doing here?
This place is not safe. I urge you to turn back and to venture no further into this cursed forest.

replies.text: I think I can handle myself.
OK, I'll turn back. Thanks for the warning.

conversationlist_lodarfg.message: This place - oh why did we ever agree to go on this mission?
Me and some other guards were sent here to find a madman that is wanted by the Feygard authorities.
The madman is wanted for a number of crimes committed against Feygard, none of which I am allowed to disclose.
At first, it seemed like just any ordinary mission - go find some crazy fool.
But once we got here, it started happening. One by one, my fellow guards got more and more ... well ... I don't know how to put it, but something started to happen to them.
Now, these flies that inhabit these woods can drive a grown man mad, I'll tell you that. But that wasn't it. There was something else.
The first guard said he had seen something among the trees, and went to look for it. We never saw him again.
Some time later, one of the other guards seemed like he didn't know who we were, and ran off into the forest.
Another guard said he'd nearly gotten lost in a what he called the 'green maze'.
Yes, it seems so. None of the scouts have come back. Or rather, the ones that have come back have been ... afflicted by something.

replies.text: What could be causing them to behave that way?

conversationlist_lodarfg.message: I don't know. Maybe something in the woods.
Maybe it's something that the madman that we were looking for has done.

replies.text: That's a really touching story. I really need to get going.

conversationlist_lodarfg.message: No, none.

replies.text: I'll keep my eyes open for any dangers when traveling through the forest myself.
Best of luck on your mission.

conversationlist_lodarfg.message: Oh, before you go. As I told you before, one of the guards mentioned 'the green maze', that apparently is somewhere around here.
Thank you.

I don't know if it's the twisty paths themselves or something that the madman has done that caused my fellow guards to behave the way they have - but consider yourself warned if you venture further into the forest!

replies.text: Your fellow guards must have been weak. I'm surely not as weak as them.
OK, I'll be on the look-out for any dangers.

conversationlist_lodarfg.message: Consider yourself warned. I can't come help you if something happens.
Oh, it's you again.
Oh, it's you again.

conversationlist_lodarfg2.message: Ouch, my head. It hurts so much.
No no. You are too small. You can't be him.
Crazy old fool, that's what they said he'd be.
[The guard mumbles something that you can't understand]
Must get away! Soon we all will be able to see it.

replies.text: Are you even listening to me?

[The guard launches himself at you, raising his sword]

[The guard turns towards you, almost as if he didn't notice you before]

replies.text: [Lie] Yes, I an one of them. Bow down to me.

conversationlist_lodarfg4.message: Oh yes, you are one of them. What lurks beneath demands that I purge this land from all of you.
You will be the first of my glorious victories.

replies.text: All right, a fight! I've been wanting to slay more of you Feygard scum.

conversationlist_lowyna.message: Whoa, you look small. I must be seeing things. That last batch I did must have gotten stronger than usual.

replies.text: What are you people doing here?

conversationlist_lowyna.message: I am Lowyna, of course. These people that you see in here and in the other huts, you could say that we're sort of in the same ... family.

replies.text: What are you people doing here?

conversationlist_lowyna.message: What smell? I can't smell anything out of the ordinary. It must be you.

replies.text: What are you people doing here?

conversationlist_lowyna.message: I really shouldn't be discussing this with you. You look way too inexperienced for this.

replies.text: Two-teeth sent me to get some rat poison.

conversationlist_lowyna.message: I'm amazed he's still around, good old two-teeth.
For his sake, I'll let you browse my wares.

conversationlist_maevalia.message: You there! This is no place for children!
Thank you for all your help!
Hello again. Did you reach the lower parts of the Charwood mine?

replies.text: Yes. I encountered a dragon-like creature in the fiery depths of the mine.

conversationlist_maevalia.message: It's good to see that Falothen and Fayvara are well. Anything else that I can help you with?

replies.text: Where do you think the monsters came from?
I talked to Kantya about what happened in the mine.

conversationlist_maevalia.message: Hello again.
Hello again. Did you find our missing people?

replies.text: Can you tell me the story about what happened here, again?
What was I supposed to do again?
Who were the people that I was supposed to look for, again?

conversationlist_maevalia.message: You again.

replies.text: Can you tell me the story about what happened here, again?

conversationlist_maevalia.message: The Charwood area has become a dangerous place as of late. You should leave at once unless you want to get killed ... or worse.
For your sake, I urge you to leave. While we need all the help we can get, we can't take responsibility for the dangers that has befell our mining town of Charwood.
We were attacked. We didn't stand a chance, they were too many and we are no fighters.
They started pouring out of the mine and the surrounding hills.
The monsters. Disgusting, foul smelling monsters. Nothing like we've ever seen before.
They ransacked our whole mining camp. Even burnt down the wooden carving that Morenavia had created last year.
We did the only thing we can, seeing as none of us were equipped to fight. We ran.
We ran down the mountain, leaving behind our mining settlement of Charwood. Some of us made it here to our former cabin.
The few of us that's left have been able to hold them off from here, at least for now.
Our mining town up in the Charwood hills is completely overrun, however. All our belongings are back there.
There are also several of us that haven't made it down the hill. Many of our friends and relatives from the mining town have not been accounted for yet.

replies.text: What do you think has happened to them?

conversationlist_maevalia.message: I don't want to think about that. Either they've been killed by the foul monsters, or worse.
You know, we saw one monster carrying around what looked like a net of some sort, instead of weapons like the other ones.
He shoved the other monsters around, and they all seemed to look up to him, like he was some sort of leader.
I don't know what that net was for though. I wonder if he was supposed to capture some of us.

replies.text: As I said, I'll try to find out what happened to them.

conversationlist_maevalia.message: I sure hope that the people that we are missing are all alive at least.
In particular, I'm worried about what happened to Morenavia - our leader. None of us that made it back to this cabin saw what happened to her.
I sure hope she's still alive. We could use some of her wisdom and leadership right now to guide us.
I'm also worried about Falothen, our weapons trainer. As I ran down the hills myself, I thought I heard him call for help.
There's also Ayell, our healer, and Fayvara, our armorer. They always stayed together, those two. We don't know what happened to them or where they are.

replies.text: What are you going to do?
As I said, I'll try to find out what happened to them.

conversationlist_maevalia.message: With your help, we might at least get somewhere.
I honestly don't know. We've sent out runners to try to find help. So far, none have returned with help.

replies.text: Tough luck. They're probably dead. You should move on with your lives.

conversationlist_maevalia.message: Yes, I guess so. Thank you for listening to our story.
Well, I wouldn't want to be responsible for putting you into any trouble.

replies.text: I might be able to sneak by the monsters undetected.
A few puny monsters won't stop me!

conversationlist_maevalia.message: OK. Frankly, I don't know what else we can do. We really need the help.
I would be very grateful for knowing what happened to the people we are missing.
Head up to our mining town of Charwood heights, and look for the missing people.
Please, try to be safe! If you spot any danger, or if those foul monsters are too much for you, don't hesitate to retreat back here.

replies.text: OK, I'll try to find your missing people.

conversationlist_maevalia.message: Thank you. The path up to Charwood heights is just east of here.
Yes, what about them?

replies.text: I'm still trying to find out what happened to all four of them.

conversationlist_maevalia.message: Thank you for helping us.
Yes, what about them? I saw that Falothen and Fayvara have returned.

replies.text: Yes, Falothen and Fayvara were alive. Morenavia and Ayell had been killed by the monsters.

conversationlist_maevalia.message: While I am very happy to hear that Falothen and Fayvara are alive and well, it saddens me to hear that we've lost not only Ayell, but also Morenavia.
Morenavia was truly a great leader for us. Now, how will we ever be able to find the right paths?
Things will never be the same again for us.
It is at least some comfort to know that we still have Falothen and Fayvara with us.
I hear they are both anxious to talk to you now that they're safe. You should go meet them downstairs in the basement.

replies.text: OK, I'll go see them in the basement.

conversationlist_maevalia.message: Good. We are truly grateful for the help that you have provided to us from the Charwood heights.
Absolutely. Pick any bed you want over there.
I have my guesses. Go talk to Kantya about it. I hear she has the full story, and some interesting theories.
Good. Did she tell you about that marking on the ground? I saw it myself. Nothing like I've ever seen before.
I wonder what is down there, in the deeper parts of the mine. I bet that whatever is controlling those monsters is still down there.

replies.text: I can go look down there if you want.
This all sounds too dangerous for me. I better not get involved.

conversationlist_maevalia.message: Can't say I blame you. Thank you for the help you've provided so far.
You would do that for us? Thank you. I don't know what we would do without your help.
Please try to be safe, and be on the lookout for the dangerous monsters that inhabit the mine.
Whatever lurks down there, I'm sure it's not happy to get any visitors.

replies.text: I'll go down into the Charwood mine and investigate.

conversationlist_maevalia.message: Thank you.
None of us ever dared to venture that deep.

replies.text: I haven't killed the creature yet though.
Whatever that thing was, it won't bother you any more now that I've killed it. Here is one of the bones from its corpse.

conversationlist_maevalia.message: You actually killed it?
You are truly a hero to us.
Not only did you manage to find our missing people, but you also freed us from the creature that caused all this trouble.
We are forever in your debt. What can we do to ever repay you?

replies.text: How about some gold for all my troubles?
I think that one of your most precious items will suffice as payment.

conversationlist_maevalia.message: You are truly our hero. Thank you yet again.
Certainly. Here is what we can spare. Thank you yet again.
After helping us, you still want to deprive us of more things that we cherish?
I guess we have no choice but to agree. Here, take these. They used to belong to my mother.

conversationlist_thukuzun.message: You are unable to enter the Charwood mine.
The air around here is much hotter around the hole in the ground here than in the rest of this room. This must be where the miners found the strange markings on the ground.
Ah, another mortal that has come to bow before the might of Thukuzun.
You will be a fine specimen in my army of bones.

replies.text: Your bones will be a fine specimen in my collection.

conversationlist_tiqui.message: You not belong here. You leave now.

replies.text: I am sent here by Aulowenn to take care of you.

conversationlist_tiqui.message: No, you die now! You one of them! Tiqui angry!

replies.text: Sorry, I wasn't listening since I was so distracted by your hideous appearance and your foul smell. Here, let me fix your face with my dagger.

conversationlist_tiqui.message: You are not allowed to use Aulowenn's bed.
My helping friend! Thank you, thank you!
Tiqui not want fight. Tiqui angry that men who smell bad kill his friends.

replies.text: I won't listen to any of your lies. You'll die now!

conversationlist_tiqui.message: They did. Men who smell bad do not belong here. Everything quiet before they came.

replies.text: I won't listen to any of your lies. You'll die now!

conversationlist_tiqui.message: You can smell them from far away even. We sense something bad would happen when we first noticed them.

In the past, troublemakers that bothered the citizens or merchants. Nowadays, it's mainly the monsters, when I can handle them.
You should talk to our priest about that.
I do recall some kid that looked a bit like you a while ago. He stayed here a couple of days, and never came back as far as I can tell.

replies.text: Do you know where he was going?

conversationlist_stoutford.message: I can't really tell. No known trouble at least. He headed straight to the tavern, and I didn't see him again before he left.

replies.text: Do you know where he was going?

conversationlist_stoutford.message: No.
How dare you come back here after all you've done?

replies.text: Actually, it's the first time we have met.
I need you as a witness for...

conversationlist_stoutford.message: Go away! You're not welcome here!
Nonsense! Go away!
Go with the shadow.

replies.text: Tahalendor told me that you may have items to trade.
What can you tell me about the area around here?
I have dealt with Erwyn's army.
I cleared Flagstone of an evil demon.
Is there anything I can do to help?
I need some help finding out who is responsible for casting a Shadow spell that causes a person to become noticeable.

conversationlist_stoutford.message: Walk in the shadow kid. I have to apologize for my master, Tahalendor.

replies.text: Crazy old geezer... What's wrong with him?
Let us talk about something different.

conversationlist_stoutford.message: My master is wise and old, but his sight is not as sharp as it once was. He took you for someone else.
To his credit, I have to admit you do look a bit like him. I don't know his name.

replies.text: That must be my brother Andor!

conversationlist_stoutford.message: He came around here not long ago, with a shady looking travelling companion. He stayed a couple of days from what I heard. Since then, we have been hearing frequent rumbles in the church, coming from underground.
It can be so loud as to make the whole church shake. It has even damaged the walls and the roof.
This church is the refuge for all the villagers when monsters attack. We are really worried now.

replies.text: I can't believe Andor has anything to do with this. Can you tell me more?
Is there anything I can do to help?
Whatever... It's none of my business.

conversationlist_stoutford.message: I told you all I know. Maybe others in town have seen him.

replies.text: Guess I'll have to look into it.

conversationlist_stoutford.message: Shadow be with you.
Hello again. Have you found anything about what is causing the noises in the church?

replies.text: Let us talk about something different.

conversationlist_stoutford.message: Wanna trade?
Hey kid. A "common friend" told me about you.
Shhh! Quiet here. You helped the guild, so I'll help you too.
A kid that looked like you was here. He apparently did some business with the owner and the regulars.
They were very careful, and even I couldn't catch a glimpse of their deeds, but you should be cautious if you deal with them.

replies.text: Thanks for the advice. I'll take care.
I can handle myself! I don't fear them, or anyone else!

conversationlist_stoutford.message: Just sayin'. Do what you will.
Psst.
An unknown force prevents you from going further.
I'm Glasforn, proud owner of this fine establishment.

replies.text: Can I use one of your beds?
What can you tell me about the strange noises in the church?

conversationlist_stoutford.message: Sorry, none are available today.

replies.text: What can you tell me about the strange noises in the church?

conversationlist_stoutford.message: What about them?

replies.text: Well, I heard they may be related to my brother Andor. I'm looking for him.

conversationlist_stoutford.message: You indeed look a lot like him...
OK, I can believe that you are Andor's sibling. You should have told me earlier!
Hello.

replies.text: Can I use one of your beds?
What can you tell me about the strange noises in the church?

conversationlist_stoutford.message: Well, you see, I keep some beds for occasions like this one. You can use the one in the corner, near the painting, if you wish to rest.
Sure.
Oh, you'll definitely enjoy our beds. I'm very proud of them.
Our food isn't bad either. Go see our cook. He's weird, but does great work.
So kid, have you tried that bed? Our beds are the best!
You really should try that bed. You'll thank me afterwards.
You hear a loud rumble, then nothing. Silence. What was that monster?
Wha... Impossible...! How did you...?

replies.text: I should kill you right now!
What did you do to me?

conversationlist_stoutford.message: You ... you should be dead!
Wait. OK. I stand no chance against you. I'll tell you all I know.
It was Andor. He made us do it, and promised to rid us of the Shadow church if we helped.
When he came, he asked me for a "private" place where he could do his weird stuff undisturbed. It had to be underground, and it had to be in the city. I have no idea why.
I showed him the cellar under the old derelict house.
I think he spent several days in there, as we didn't see him. Around that time, the rumbles in the church began and we knew he would be keeping his promise.
When he returned he put this horrible necklace on me. He told me that thing in the cellar needed lives to grow stronger, and either I could give it those lives or the necklace would take mine.
I'm sorry! How was I to know you could actually kill it? You're just a kid! Anyway, now I can remove the necklace. Please take it. I never want to see it again.
That's all I know, I swear. Please spare me. You can use the bed safely now.

replies.text: I'll spare you. For now. But no more tricks. Or else...
I guess this was all necessary.

conversationlist_stoutford.message: I swear. You'll be my honored guest for life.
Hello again. Have you found anything about what is causing the noises in the church? It seems they have stopped.

replies.text: Yes. I think I found the cause.
Let us talk about something different.

conversationlist_stoutford.message: Great. You should talk to my master. I told him you were not who he thought you were.
You! You saved us!

replies.text: That was the right thing to do.
Would you come with me to talk to Blornvale? He wants to confess something important.

conversationlist_stoutford.message: My sincerest apologies for earlier. I took you for someone else. Do you know what was causing the rumbles?

replies.text: [Show Demon heart] Some monster. Here's what it left when I killed it.

conversationlist_stoutford.message: Oh my. It's the heart of a lich! These are nasty creatures.

replies.text: These? You mean there are others?

conversationlist_stoutford.message: They aren't common, but I have heard stories. They are powerful and live underground. They seem to be related to Kazaul somehow.
I'm surprised such a young kid as you managed to survive encountering one, let alone actually kill it.
Too bad. Come back when you know more.
You know, since those monsters' attacks, we don't have much to offer, but take these. By the way, do you have any idea who might be responsible for all this?

replies.text: It was all Glasforn's doing. The tavern owner.
It was my brother Andor. I need to find him.

conversationlist_stoutford.message: It's a shame we cannot punish the culprits. Thank you for your help kid.
That fool! We'll make him pay. Thank you for your help kid.
That is troublesome. I have no idea where he went when he left Stoutford, but Kazaul has always been linked to the Undertell, south of here. Thank you for your help kid.
Go with the shadow child.

replies.text: Would you come with me to talk to Blornvale? He wants to confess something important.
Yolgen told me that you could provide me with an artifact that could be used against powerful undead.
Do you have anything to trade?
I need some help finding out who is responsible for casting a Shadow spell that causes a person to become noticeable.

conversationlist_stoutford.message: Thank you for your help. Do you have any idea who might be responsible for all this?

replies.text: It was all Glasforn's doing. The tavern owner.
It was my brother Andor. I need to find him.

conversationlist_stoutford.message: What are you talking about?

replies.text: I met an undead lord in the castle, but every time it seems that I have destroyed him, he rises again. Do you have any advice?
I want to help you clean the castle of the undead. Yolgen seems to be worried, perhaps because he believes the undead could be too strong.

conversationlist_stoutford.message: Most undead can be destroyed quite easily, but there is a rare and powerful kind that are much more difficult to permanently destroy.
I think I have a solution though.
First, I need two coins. Please give me 2 gold coins.

Now I will bless them with a special enchantment...
[Tahalendor holds the coins over the altar and mutters something you can't hear]

Here you go. As soon as the undead lord appears to be destroyed, place one coin on each eye. This will prevent him from rising again, and soon after you have placed the coins his remains should disintegrate, as he returns to his natural state.
Boohoohoo ... the whole town hates me now. Even my dear customers left. Just the old hag who only drinks water stayed, and Lord Bourbon who never pays.
Boohoohoo...
No. Sorry.
Halvor? Yes! He's so nice! Do you know him?

replies.text: I hate the guy. He's nothing but trouble...
Sure, we keep meeting around the world in the most unusual places. I even helped him gather some items.

conversationlist_stoutford.message: He's always been good to me. If you don't like him, I don't like you!
So that's you! He told me about you.
He told me you were of great help.
Anyway. I made these boots with the items he brought me.

I'm really proud of the result.
They are light, but sturdy, thanks to the bones and insect wings.
They are comfortable but tough thanks to the animal hair and venomscale scales.
They are stiff when adjusted, thanks to the rat tails.
Here. Take these. I've given one pair to Halvor, and I'll keep the last one for myself.

replies.text: Wow. I have to try these. Goodbye.

conversationlist_stoutford.message: Do you want to trade?
Hey. Be careful what you do.
Kids should not walk around alone in these times.
It was terrible! I could feel the necklace draining the life out of me, and the only thing that made me feel better was giving it another victim.

replies.text: Why didn't you just take it off?

conversationlist_stoutford.message: I couldn't. When I tried, and failed, he laughed. He told me it was bound to that thing in the basement, which needed me to be its servant.
Then he laughed some more, and told me that all I had to do was kill that thing, and I would be able to remove the necklace. I'm no fighter though. I was too scared to even go near it.

replies.text: I guess you are lucky I visited, although just asking me to kill it would have been easier. And nicer.

conversationlist_stoutford.message: I didn't dare. The evening after Andor left his companion returned briefly. He warned me you might come here, and that if you found out what I had done you would kill me. He told me that my only hope was to make you the next victim.
If I must. Well, go ahead, I'll be there when you get there.
What now?
Well, I don't really believe it, but we could try. Blornvale, how did you kill Aryfora's father, your own brother?

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: Hey, did you try to open that treasure chest?

That chest is something of a local legend. Been there for generations. They say it is sealed with magic and can only be opened with a special key, which hangs on the neck of one of the undead that roam in a cemetery directly south of here.

replies.text: Killing the undead is my specialty.
Undead? I would love to hear the rest of your story but I am on a mission to find my brother.

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: You don't think someone has already tried? It's a treasure chest ... left outside ... in plain view ... unguarded.

Listen kid. A hundred 'adventurers' before you have tried and failed to open that chest. The problem isn't killing some undead. It's getting into the cemetery, because it's protected by a magical barrier that prevents anyone from entering.

replies.text: Interesting. Is there anything else you can tell me about the chest or cemetery?

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: That is all I know ... Come to think of it ... Hagale from the Wood Settlement was out here a few weeks ago asking about the chest. Something about him struck me as odd. It was as if he was in a trance.
Oh yeah? What's it to you kid? ... BURP ... If you want to know, it will cost you two bottles of Lowyna's special brew.

I heard rumors about an unguarded treasure chest. I heard that the key that opened it, hung around the neck of an undead roaming the cemetery south of the chest. I also heard that the entrance to the cemetery was sealed by magic.

I thought nothing more of it. I was a simple trader in Loneford with a beautiful wife and daughter.
[Hagale takes another long swig from the bottle of Lowyna's special brew]

[Hagale takes another swig from the bottle of Lowyna's special brew]
I realized that she wouldn't make it.
I watched as she suffered in agonizing pain. I knew without treatment she would die in a matter of weeks.

Still, I did not give up. I thought that if I opened the chest and gave its treasure as a gift to Lord Geomyr, I could plead with him to lift the bonemeal ban in time to save my daughter. It sounds stupid but I was desperate.
A few days later, I tracked the bandits down. I begged and pleaded but they would not volunteer any information. They were obviously after the chest themselves, and they attacked me.
[This man smells of alcohol and some plant-like substance; he is clearly intoxicated]

replies.text: I defeated the undead monster and opened the chest. I found a powerful sword inside.
I heard you were interested in that unattended treasure chest by the Waterway house.
Don't breathe on me! I'm leaving!

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: You actually opened the chest? That sword must be worth a lot of money ... could buy a lot of Lowyna's special brew ... Sorry kid, but I need that sword!

replies.text: I went through hell to get this sword. I won't give it to you without a fight.
I went through a lot to get this sword ... but you suffered more than me. I won't fight you. If you want it that badly, the sword is yours.
Yes, I have the sword, see here!
I did find the sword, but I don't have it anymore.

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: I should not have doubted you. Well done.
In plain sight, you find a large extravagantly adorned treasure chest. Glancing around, it appears the chest is unattended. You think to yourself...

replies.text: I have the key right here.
I should take a peek inside.

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: The chest is locked.
You think to yourself...
Multiple strikes from your weapon do not damage the chest. The chest is protected by some form of magic.

The text begins to radiate light. The ground begins to shake as darkness fills the sky. A loud cracking sound is followed by a rush of cold air that sends chills down your back. You watch as corpses begin to claw their way to the surface. The stench of rotting flesh fills your nostrils, making you gag.
As you approach the cemetery's entrance, your steps become heavier and heavier.
[You notice this undead is wearing a key around its neck]
Let's go.

replies.text: I'm sorry it has come to this.

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: Alright hand it over. Be quick about it.
You no brain.
You open the chest and discover a powerful sword infused with unholy magic.
Thanks for letting me have the sword kid. I decided that with the money I can get for this I can rebuild my life. I'm going to sober up and start trading again. I'll be leaving here soon.
Greetings, young traveler.

replies.text: I opened that chest and got a powerful sword.

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: The text described a cemetery sealed by magic to contain a powerful undead monster roaming within it. My source was correct, it was a reference to the cemetery south of that chest.

The ground began to tremble and darkness filled the sky. This was followed by a cracking sound, the loudest sound my ears ever heard, making a gust of cold air rush past me. Then, corpses began to claw their way to the surface. The odor ... it was putrid.
Suddenly, a horde of undead attacked me. I fought them off as best I could but there were just too many. I barely escaped with my life and I never went back.

[Hagale finishes the second bottle of Lowyna's special brew]
Sure do. I hope you know what you're doing kid.
That is probably why the chest was left outside in plain sight, unattended.
Good luck.

My daughter passed away shortly after I returned. I failed my wife and my daughter. I lost everything. I buried my family in Loneford, gave up my trade, and came here. Now, I drink Lowyna's special brew all day ... it helps me forget.

replies.text: I'm sorry for your losses. You have suffered a lot. I want to finish what you started. Do you still have that text?

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: Here lies Damurrela of Loneford, wife of Hagale and mother of Aradilles. Killed by Plaguestriders.
Here lies Aradilles of Loneford, daughter of Hagale and Damurrela. Died from blistering skin.
You must not be from around here. If you were, you would know that it is impolite to barge into homes without invitation.

replies.text: Sorry. I didn't mean to be rude. I'm $playername. I come from a small village where people tend to leave their doors open.

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: The surrounding forest is usually quiet, but for some time now it has been under a monster invasion. I am surprised you managed to reach my home.
I heard something similar was occurring in Charwood until a young adventurer killed a vile beast in the mine beneath the city.

replies.text:
I was in Charwood recently and what you heard was true.
[You describe your experiences in Charwood and the battle with Thukuzun]
That is interesting, but I am supposed to be looking for my brother. I should leave.

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: I do not know if it began happening here before the events in Charwood or after. However, from what you tell me, maybe there is a connection between the two.

There is a cave system that runs underneath the forest. If something sinister is afoot, it could be emanating from the ground below. Please, you must help me investigate the source of the monster invasion in this forest.

replies.text: Sorry, I cannot help you right now.
How much "investigating" will you be doing in this proposed partnership?

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: Thank you. You will have to pass through the forest to reach an opening to the cave where you can enter. The opening is roughly east of my home.
The Guardian stares at you. You feel an overwhelming sense of dread, and dare not even approach it.
You have found the entrance to the cave Cithurn was talking about.
You notice that the air has become much damper as you make your way towards the end of the cave system.
Ah, another puny mortal that has come to die and serve Tesrekan.
Hmm ... I'll work on the parts that aren't dangerous. A brave and expert fighter like yourself is better suited to the dangerous parts.

replies.text: Danger is my middle name! I'll help you.
Sorry. Flattery will not persuade me to risk my life for some piece of forest with one old man living in it.

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: Well I'm the only one here. Perhaps you should leave. Come back when you have learned some manners.
Meow ... Meow.

replies.text: [You scratch the cat behind the ear]

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: Baah!
You find a partly visible gem sticking out of the exposed rock.
You find a partly visible gem sticking out of the exposed rock.
The ancient text crumbles and turns to dust. The defeat of the undead master seems to have lifted the spell animating the remaining corpses and they return to their graves.
It is good to see you again $playername.

replies.text: I explored the cave. You were correct. I found a monster called Tesrekan, which was similar to the one I found in the Charwood mine.
I think I need more help to be able to complete my mission.
I haven't found out what is happening yet, but I wanted to let you know I'm still working on it.

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: Hey kid! Why don't you be a good little boy and fetch me some Lowyna's special brew?

Alright kid!
[Hagale immediately opens one of the bottles and takes a big swig, which he loudly swallows before wiping his mouth on the sleeve of his tattered shirt]
Yeah, I know something about that chest ... *burp* ... I almost opened it.
That was until I had to travel to Remgard to purchase some new inventory. I normally make the trip alone. This time however, my wife and daughter decided to accompany me to Remgard.
Well done! A thousand thanks young adventurer. I am in your debt. However, I would still like my talisman back. I need it to keep me safe.

replies.text: You are right about that debt. I think I'll keep the talisman as payment.

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: Was?

replies.text: I killed the monster. I brought one of its bones as proof.

conversationlist_graveyard1.message:
We were only halfway there when we were attacked by Plaguestriders. My daughter and I managed to escape...
[Hagale takes another long swig from the bottle of Lowyna's special brew]
...but my wife did not survive.

My daughter was afflicted by a nasty form of blistering skin. I rushed her back to Loneford. I thought with rest, good food, and water she could pull through ... but although the blisters were gradually healing, my daughter's health continued to decline.

I had to do something. I went to Fallhaven and begged Thoronir to make me a bonemeal potion. Although it would have cured my daughter completely, he refused because Lord Geomyr banned all use of bonemeal as a healing substance!
[Hagale takes another long swig from the bottle of Lowyna's special brew and finishes it. He proceeds to open the second the bottle.]
I searched the land for information about the chest and graveyard. I spent my entire fortune in the process. My last few coins resulted in a tip that directed me to a group of bandits.

I may be a trader, but traders have to learn how to protect themselves. The first few went down easily, but the leader was an experienced fighter. We fought for over an hour, but eventually I managed to kill him. I searched the body and found an ancient text.
The magical barrier at the cemetery could only be penetrated by someone carrying the text, which contained several magical inscriptions.

I took the best weapons and armor from the bandits, and made my way to the cemetery. Carrying the ancient text in my front pouch, I approached the entrance to the cemetery. I was only a few feet away when the text began to glow.
Maybe he knows more. You should give him a visit.
Well $playername, you are young, and you apologized, so perhaps I will be a little forgiving. Just remember that not everywhere is like your small village. My name is Cithurn.
You have small brain but small brain better than no brain. ARGH!!!
An unearthly force prevents you from entering the cemetery.
What's a kid like you doing around here? It's a dangerous place to be.

replies.text: I'm looking for my brother, Andor. He looks a bit like me.

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: Sorry. I haven't seen anyone like that.

replies.text: Thanks. Maybe I can help you with whatever is dangerous around here?
Thanks. I need to get going.
Thanks. Maybe I can help you with whatever is dangerous around here?

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: I don't think so. It would need an experienced fighter to help with this problem.

replies.text: Fine. If I'm back around here sometime in the future maybe I'll offer my help again. Or maybe I won't.

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: I will clarify. A more experienced fighter than you.

replies.text: OK. I can take a hint.

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: Here. Take this talisman. It does much to dispel evil forces. I acquired it long ago, and it has kept me safe over the years. Since you have agreed to help me I think your need is now greater than mine. My only request is that if you are successful, you return it to me.
Good luck young adventurer. I await your return.
Thank you. I see you are not just a great fighter, but also an adventurer that keeps his word.
I see. You are apparently a great fighter, but not a very honorable one.
Have you come to return my talisman?

replies.text: Yes. I changed my mind about keeping it.
No. I already told you that I am keeping it as payment for my work.

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: Thank you. It seems you do have more honor than I thought.
Then I have nothing to say to you.
You have found a hatchway that appears to give access to something underground, but it is locked, and you can't open it.
You found some gold amongst the bones!
There is nothing more to be found here.
Don't you know that it's rude to walk into someone's house without knocking?

replies.text: Your neighbor was right. He said you were not always a nice person.
Sorry. I'm looking for my brother, Andor. He looks a bit like me. Have you seen him?

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: No. And little boys like you should not be wandering around on your own. I'm sure your father would not approve.

replies.text: My father sent me to look for my brother.

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: Then he must be a very bad father. He should look for your brother himself. Tell me, are your father and brother as rude as you?

replies.text: Thank you for talking to me. I will leave now.
They are certainly not as rude as you. Goodbye.

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: Hello kid. What can I do for you?

replies.text: I'm looking for my brother, Andor. He looks a bit like me. Have you seen him?
Can you tell me anything about the local area?

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: Sorry. I don't recall seeing anyone like that.

replies.text: Can you tell me anything about the local area?

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: There's not much to tell. Loneford is mostly a quiet place, although I have heard rumors that there is some criminal organization based here. Personally, I don't believe it.
The nastiest person in town is probably my neighbor. *laughs*. Be careful about walking in on her!

replies.text: I appreciate the warning, but unfortunately it's too late. I already met her.
You are right. I told her you warned me that she was not always nice to strangers, but I think that just annoyed her.

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: Is there anything else I can help you with?

replies.text: I'm looking for my brother, Andor. He looks a bit like me. Have you seen him?

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: Did he now! Well, I'll have a word or two to say to him later! What do you want?

replies.text: I'm looking for my brother, Andor. He looks a bit like me. Have you seen him?

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: Thanks kid. *sigh*. I expect she will be around here later to complain about that. You should be more careful what you say to people.
Is there something I can help you with?

replies.text: I'm looking for my brother, Andor. He looks a bit like me. Have you seen him?

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: No. Is there anything else?
Like many folk in Loneford, I'm a farmer.

replies.text: OK. Thanks. I need to get going.
Do you have anything to trade?

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: I'm a farmer, not a shopkeeper. So yes, if you want to buy a cartload, no otherwise.

replies.text: OK. Thanks. I need to get going.

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: [You have stumbled upon the remains of an adventurer that came before you. Looking at what is left of their equipment, they were ill-prepared for a place such as this. Now they have no use for their equipment or gold. You debate whether to loot the corpse. In the past you have done worse, but...]

replies.text: You decide to leave the corpse undisturbed.

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: You again? What do you want this time?

replies.text: I wish to apologize. I'm $playername. I come from a small village where people tend to leave their doors open. I didn't mean to be rude.

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: Purr ... Purr.
Purr ... Purr.
You have discovered a hidden room!
I will kill you, and then you will join my army of undead servants and soldiers.

replies.text: I just destroyed a lot of your army.
If you are so powerful why do you need an army?
I have destroyed others like you, and I will destroy you!

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: All the more reason for me to kill you and replenish what you have destroyed!

replies.text: An army with no leader is not an army, so I will destroy you!

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: Insolent human! I will make you my undead slave!

replies.text: You don't have what it takes!

conversationlist_graveyard1.message: OK. Thanks for keeping me updated. Please come back when you have more information.
You dare approach me? You will die!
The Guardian stares at you. You feel a sense of dread, but you resist the urge to turn back.
Thanks for your help, but I don't think we have anything else to discuss.
You found some crates that look as though they have been here for a very long time. One of the crates has some old, tattered clothing in it.
The clothes smell musty and are falling apart.
You found some crates that look as though they have been here for a very long time. The crates are empty now.
You found some crates that look as though they have been here for a very long time.
The cemetery is quiet now.
There is nothing left to take from the corpse.
South of the Duleian road, close to Fallhaven.
Hey kid! Stop waving that thing at me! If you want to talk to me, put it away first!
So where is it?
