Thank you again for your effort.

replies.text: It could have been a bit more gold.

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: What? Do I hear ungrateful words?

replies.text: Eh, no, it is nothing. Bye.
I will take my gold now - attack!

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: Omm...
Omm...
Ommmmm...
Omm... ommm... ommmmm...
Very good. Finally a learned being in this rat hole.
In gratitude for the great joy I give you this rat skull.
Come again whenever you want. It is a nice diversion to talk with someone with a bit of brain at least.
Greetings, young being.

replies.text: Do you have something to trade?

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: Young people are always in a hurry. In my time, you introduced yourself first.
We'll try again from the beginning.
I am Whootibarfag, wise of the Blackwater mountains.

replies.text: Nice to meet you. I am $playername from Crossglen, if you should know the village.
Do you have anything to trade?

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: Sigh. Always in a hurry. Again - who are you?
Now, what brings you to this lonely area?

replies.text: I'm helping a cheeky little rat find an artifact.
Do you have anything to trade?
I recovered and brought back Rat King Rah's skeleton.

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: I should have known. No one comes up here to ask for wisdom.

replies.text: Not now. Let us trade first.
All right, let's get this over with. Enlighten us.

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: I have great knowledge, you know?

replies.text: Maybe another time. Let's just trade.
Then finally say what you want to say. And after that show me your goods.

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: Sigh. Well, I have interesting items to sell. However, no food, I need it for myself.

replies.text: Then what do you have for sale?

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: Torches to light your way.
Hand carved snowballs.
And finally, a medallion that will help you find your way here if your memory fails you.

replies.text: Now that sounds interesting. Show me your items, please.
However, I am as poor as a church rat.

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: Well, I have too good a heart. Here, take the amulet for 100 gold pieces.

replies.text: Oh thank you! Here is the gold.

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: Well, now some wisdom ...

replies.text: All right, let's get this over with. Enlighten us.

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: Ah, a sacred quest for a mystical object. Good luck on your way.

replies.text: Thanks. Then we'll go looking further.

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: Who knows? Tell me about your artifact.

replies.text: Maybe another time. Let's just trade.
It's big, round and yellow. Clevered, what else do you know about this?

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: Oh, whoever possesses this artifact will be rich and never go hungry again.
Who needs gold?! It is much better.
Clevred tells and tells.
Hold on!
I'm afraid I can't help you much there. I'm more familiar with the events out here on the mountain.
But you might ask an old friend of mine. He has a small but valuable collection of important items and I'm sure he'll be happy to show you around.

replies.text: You mean Wart? We have already met him.

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: You may find him in the caves below, even deeper in the mountain.

replies.text: Do you have anything to trade?

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: Good, so that's settled. Now I could share a little of my wisdom with you?

replies.text: Not now. Let us trade first.
All right, let's get this over with. Enlighten me.

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: I know that I know nothing.
But at least I think, so I am. Then I left the cave.

replies.text: From the shadows to the light.

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: Yes, yes! How did you know?
Now I need to know what is louder: the noise of a lonely falling tree, or the sound of one hand clapping.
I didn't really expect you to know.
There are many paths leading to happiness.
One of them is to stop whining.
Hey - I'm the one with the wisdom here!
Arrogance is the surest path to failure.
From failure we learn.
Learn as if you were to live forever.
Seize the day.

replies.text: Enough! What. do. you. have. for. sale?
I give up. Come, Clevred, let us leave.

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: Oh, yes. Of course I know.
Nothing remains hidden from me that is happening here in the mountain.

replies.text: I really had to run around a lot.

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: Well, I see you've learned a lot by searching the rat kingdom. But you're still missing one thing ...

replies.text: Yes, I lack patience. The patience to keep listening to your babble.

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: Wisdom? No, hahaha!
Leave wisdom to the wise. So to me.

replies.text: I will. What do you have for sale?
As you wish. I leave the wise now. Bye.

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: You've seen enough rats skilfully flee and escape.
You just haven't understood that you can make this ability your own.
Come closer.
Closer ...

replies.text: [You hold your breath - from tension, and because of his bad breath.]

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: Whootibarfag let you in on the secret of the rat escape. This increases your ability to flee and escape.

replies.text: Hey! Yes of course! That's how it works!

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: Use this knowledge well. Go now, I need some rest.

replies.text: Thanks for all your help. Good bye.

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: I cook my own meat, thank you very much!

replies.text: I've been looking for a way to cook my meat.

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: I could use some extra gold. So I can cook them for you for let's say 30 gold a piece.

replies.text: Well, here is 1 piece and 30 gold.
OK, I have 5 pieces and 150 gold.
Here, I have 10 pieces that I would like cooked. Here are 300 gold pieces too.
I'm hungry! Here are 20 pieces and 600 gold.
Oh, my mistake, I forgot that I have no meat.
Oops, I'm still poor. I can't afford to pay your price.

conversationlist_ratdom_npc.message: Only one? That's no problem. Here's your cooked meat.
Just five? That's no problem. Here's all your cooked meat.
10 meat at once? That's no problem. Here's all your cooked meat.
20 meat at once?! You may even love this stuff more than I do. Here's all your cooked meat.
No, sorry. I can't let you use my kitchen. But...

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: You try to push the door open, but it's blocked from the inside. Best to try the other door.
With all that gold that you helped us get back, we plan to fix the bridge so we will be able to ship our beer to the west.

replies.text: Oh, that's great news indeed! It's going to make my life easier.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Don't you know? The bridge that crosses over the Sutdover River that flows between here and Stoutford. It's been broken for a while now.
It should be ready by the time you get there.
The bridge that crosses over the Sutdover River has been repaired thanks to you.

replies.text: Yes. I am aware. In fact, I've already used it.
I am aware of this, but I am here on another matter.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: You can't continue over the broken boards. It's time to turn around and find another way across.
Hey, kid! Just where do you think you're going?

replies.text: Across the bridge, of course. After all, I can't swim.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: The bridge is broken. You're going nowhere.
Let me guess, you're wondering if I know how to cross the river?
Please move along. There's nothing to see here.

replies.text: I've been wondering, do you have anything to sell?
Hi Seraphina, you were away so quickly after you gave me Luthor's ring.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Well, as a matter of fact, I do. I have a board right here under the bridge that you can place over the hole. But it's going to cost you {1000} gold.

replies.text: Wow! All you thieves are alike. Here, take it.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Great! Now, let me see. Where is that board?
Seraphina bends down to look under the bridge.
Um, it's not here.

replies.text: What do you mean "it's not here"? Where is it?

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: It must have drifted down river. Sorry!
Maybe next time you come by I'll have the board?
Why are you looking at me like that?

replies.text: I want my gold back. You thief!

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: I'm just the muscle around here. Go talk to Defy.
I'm just the...um...
Um, yes. One of those.
Are you lost, kid?
Shh! What was that? Did you guys here that?
I heard nothing. Greedy, you need to relax. Here, have a Bandit's Brew.
There it is again! Please tell me that you guys heard that?
Greedy! That's enough! Stop it. We are safe here.

replies.text: Wait a minute, I recognize those guys.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Ugh. Whatever.
You should get a better understanding of who these men are before you crash the party.
Lookie what we have here! Sullengard's five most wanted men, all in one location. This is my lucky day.
Oh, it's the child from Crossglen. Umar's little toy.
Why are you yelling from across the woods? Please walk over here and we can talk.
Oh, how interesting your timing is.
Well, you see, we are in kind of a predicament.

replies.text: Oh, you are feeling guility for what you did to the great people of Sullengard and want to turn yourselves in, but don't want to go to jail?

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Now that's funny. No! Now back to what I was trying to tell you...
We are planning a heist, but we need your "skills" to pull it off.
Please. Just hear me out.
We have knowledge of this vast repository of gold and other treasures, but it is well secured under lock and key.

replies.text: OK. You had me at "treasures". Please go on.
And you want me to help you return it to its rightful owners?

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: The problem of needing the key is where your "skills" come in.

replies.text: These "skills" that you keep mentioning, what are they?

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: [Laughing loudly]. Kid, you are certainly as funny as you are funny looking, I'll tell you that right now. Now, back on topic...
I was just getting to that. If you would stop interrupting me, I could get to the plan quicker and how you play a major role in it.

replies.text: A "major" role you said. So what, I get fifty percent of the loot?

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Again with the humor. No, you will not be getting fifty percent. Anyways...
Well, before I get into any more details. Hey Alaric [the lost traveler's real name], do we trust this kid enough to tell him the details?
Well Defy, $playername did let me go after discovering my crime.

replies.text: [Keep quiet about the facts and agree, for now] That's true.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: That's fair enough. Now let us move on to the details, shall we?

replies.text: Yes, please. I'm getting bored here.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: You see, we want to get back some of what is ours. What we helped to accumulate over the years. We want to hit them where it really hurts.
Well, yes. But not right now. Those adventures are too big for us right now.
I'm talking about the Thieves' Guild.

replies.text: Why would you want to do that?

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Exactly!

Well, for starters, Umar and his sidekick brother have wronged us over and over again. Keeping all the wealth for themselves. And don't even get me started on the emotional stress and abuse we suffer from at their hands.
You know what I am talking about, don't you?

replies.text: I'm not so sure that I do.
Actually, yeah, kind of. Well, at least that thought has crossed my mind once or twice recently.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Come on, $playername. Open you eyes. Think. Your are just a tool to him. Something for him to use to accomplish whatever his agenda is that day.

replies.text: Actually, yeah, kind of. Well, at least that thought has crossed my mind once or twice recently.
I'm not so sure, but please, get on with your plan.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Anyways... The Guild has a vault. A repository of treasures and wealth hidden and secure in a location just south of Fallhaven.

replies.text: I've been all around the Fallhaven area a thousand times and I've never seen any vault.
I don't believe you. I would have stumbled across it.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Oh, trust me, it's there all right.

replies.text: Trust you? You want me to trust you? A dishonorable thief? Where is it then?
Tell me. I want to know.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Are you familiar with that vacant house southwest of Fallhaven? The one next to the cliffside?
The entrance to it is found inside that house. It's hidden and secured. You will need to find the passage that leads underground in order to gain access.

replies.text: That sounds easy. I'll do it.
I guess I can try and get in there.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: You won't be doing it.
No. We will be doing that.

replies.text: Then what do you need from me?

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: What I need from you is more of an inside job. I need you to get the key to the vault from Troublemaker without him suspecting any trickery. Do you think you can handle that?

replies.text: Why should I help you? What do I get out of this?
If I do this for you, then I expect to get paid!

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Oh, you aren't as dumb as you are funny.
How does 10 percent of the total treasure sound?

replies.text: Nope. I will go no lower than 25 percent
I'll do it for twice that amount. 20 percent.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Fine! [Shh] I'll take it out of Greedy's portion. He'll never know the difference.
We will be leaving this campsite in favor of our hideout. Meet up with me there and you can give me the key then.

replies.text: Sounds good, but where is your hideout?

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: It's where the rail tracks end. West of the Sutdover River.

replies.text: The Sutdover River? Where is it?

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: The Sutdover River flows between Sullengard and Stoutford.
As you sneak a peek inside, a terrifying voice yells out. Warning you not to step foot inside.
Go talk to Defy. I have nothing to say to you.
Great! Give it to me and when I have time, whenever that may be, I will add it to our bank.

replies.text: Well, if you are so busy, I don't mind making the deposit for the greater good.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Hmm... well I guess you could do that for me considering Umar trusts you a lot.

replies.text: Great! Just tell me where to go and you can consider it done.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Well, it's not that easy. You need more than the location. You need this key.

replies.text: Thanks, but where is the vault located?

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: You can find the empty house just south of here. Enter it and you will find your way.

replies.text: Thank you so much! I will bring the key back as quick as possible.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: You what? How? Where? Tell me all you know.

replies.text: I found them by pure luck, really.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Where did you find them?

replies.text: Southeast of Deebo's orchard. They were simply sitting in the woods around a campfire enjoying some of Sullengard's "Bandit Brews".

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: What else can you tell me?

replies.text: They wanted to hire me to rob you guys. Defy wants your stash of gold and treasures.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Really? What did you say?

replies.text: Well, I agreed to, but only because I want to help you guys catch him.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: You know, $playername, for just being a young adventurer, you are learning a lot.

replies.text: Thanks a lot. I do feel a lot smarter now than I did before joining your guild.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Listen, kid. Let's use this to our advantage. Take this fake key, bring it to Defy and we will be waiting for them at the vault.

replies.text: Sir, that sounds like a great plan. What do you want me to do after handing him the fake key?

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: You should go with them to the vault as we may need your help there.

replies.text: Great! Just tell me where to go and you can consider it done.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: You can find the empty house just southwest of here. Enter it and you will find your way.
It's so weird working with you after all that we've gone through.

replies.text: I would love nothing more than to see you punished for your crimes.
What are you waiting for? Go take the fake key to Troublemaker.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Do you have the key? Hand it over.

replies.text: Oops. I forgot to bring it with me. I'll be back soon.
Yes, but you are not having it. I will loot the vault myself and keep everything I find.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Thank you so much. Now take this fake key that Zachlanny's has made and return it to Troublemaker before he suspects anything. Then meet us at the vault to collect your share of the loot.
Thank you very much!
I'm rich. I'm finally rich!

replies.text: Only in gold. You have no friends.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Here is your reward for your role in our success.

replies.text: It was nice doing business with you.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: We are leaving now. Too close to Fallhaven for my liking.
Come again?

replies.text: You heard me the first time. I'm keeping the key and looting the vault myself.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: I will be taking that key now!
I have killed Defy, his three helpers and Alaric. I really should go back to Fallhaven and talk to Troublemaker again.
You what? How? Where? Tell me all you know.

replies.text: You're never going to believe this, but they were inside that vacant house when I walked in.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Then what happened?

replies.text: They looked up to no good, so I questioned them. Then the next thing I know, I'm caught up in the heat of battle and they are dead.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Can you prove this? Can you show me something that proves that all four are dead?

replies.text: Yes. I looted their rings. [Shows them to Troublemaker]
Yes. I looted their rings, but I forgot to bring them with me. I'll come back.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Well, this is great news indeed. However, we would like to have them alive.
Thank you so much. Now take this fake key that Zachlanny's has made and return it to Troublemaker before he suspects anything. Then meet us at the vault to collect your share of the loot.
Ah, $playername has finally returned. Please, take this crystal and some gold as our thanks to you.
You will be happy to hear that we have captured Defy and his four accomplices before they could steal from us.

replies.text: That's great news indeed. Where are they now?

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: We are keeping them in our holding cage in Fallhaven.

replies.text: Is there anything else that I should know about?

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Yes. That fifth man, the one that was not one of us...
His name is not important to me...
We've learned that he was part of a crime in Sullengard. You may want to visit Sullengard and inform them that we have their guy.
I am here now to watch out for suspicious activity and people.
Hey, you are just the person that I wanted to see. I've been wondering that with all of your adventures, have you encountered "the lost traveler" again?
Where? Can you get him back here to be punished?

replies.text: Actually, he is in a Fallhaven jail. Locked up with Defy in fact. I was able to capture them and lock them up there.
Actually, I had a chance encounter with him and after attempting to drag him back here, he attacked me and I had no other option than to end his life.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Oh, thank you so much!

replies.text: Of course. It was my pleasure.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Well, I would have preferred to see him punished instead of killed, but thank you so much for putting an end to all this.

replies.text: Of course. It was my pleasure.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Please, take this as a gift of gratitude.
I don't know if you will like it, but let me tell you, nobody down here wants it.

replies.text: Oh, really? I will play with it. Thanks again.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: As you step between the trees, the crunch of the dry leaves beneath your feet startle you.
As you step between the trees, the crunch of the dry leaves beneath your feet startle you.
Do you want to unlock the hatch?
The lock creaks open, revealing a staircase.
Oh, gross! It's full of spiders.
Do you have the key? Hand it over.

replies.text: Yes, Here it is. [Handing over the fake key]

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: You will regret this, kid!
Do I know you?

replies.text: Oh, you want to play dumb? Umar will hear about this!
No time to joke - the Guild needs you. Umar ...

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: I should come back with the Thieves' Guild key.
Thank you very much!

replies.text: I encountered Defy and his men and was forced to kill them!

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Did you hear about the kidnapping?

replies.text: Not now, I have something else to talk about.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: [Looking extermely confused and terrified] ... Well, why would it be you?
[Looking extermely confused] ... Who?
Well, while you were off hunting and killing that giant snake, I had a customer.
A customer with a very interesting report about a kidnapped girl and a witch.
That's the thing. He is no longer here. He just left before you walked in.
You should ask around town if anyone has seen or heard about it.

replies.text: OK. I think I will do that. Thanks.
OK, but first please give me something to drink.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Of course, my dear.

replies.text: Did you see a witch around here or hear about a witch kidnapping a girl?

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: No, I'm sorry, I didn't.
Hello there. Please do not bother me, I have a lot of work to do.

replies.text: Can I have just one minute of your time, please?
Could you tell me the story about the wicked witch again?

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: I suppose.

replies.text: Great! I was wondering if you know anything about a kidnapping or a witch?

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: [Taken aback by the question] What did you just ask me?

replies.text: I asked if you know anything about a witch and the possibility that she took a girl.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Leave me alone! I don't want to talk about her!

replies.text: So you know something about the kidnapping?
What about the witch? Do you know something about her?

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Nope!
I may, but I don't want to tell you about her as I am terrified of her.

replies.text: Wow! Now I have to learn what you know. Please tell me your story.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: No way! I have no way to protect myself and believe me, I will need to if I tell you anything.

replies.text: I will protect you. Trust me.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: [Laughing uncontrollably] ... You? You are just a child of a farmer. So you are weaker than I am.
Of course I do. He lives a stones throw away from me and we are both farmers.

replies.text: Oh. I didn't know. But I can protect you.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: And how can you do that? Have you ever done anything like this before?

replies.text: Well, actually, I have. In fact, I just finished protecting this entire town from a giant snake.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: That was you?
Well, if that's the case, then I will tell you my story.
My story starts a very long time ago, when I was just a kid.
You see, one day, my best friend Addie and I were playing amongst the trees south of town when we encountered her.
She was a young beautiful woman, but terrifyingly alluring. So much so, that she easily coerced us into following her into her house.
Now, I will tell you right now that I have chosen to block out most of the details as it was such a painful experience.
All I remember was being kept in a dark room for what felt like weeks without food and being alone. You see, the witch kept Addie in another room ... I think.
Yes. You see, after I escaped, I never saw Addie again.
After a couple of weeks passed, I saw a chance to escape and I took it. Never to look back and never to talk about it. Well, until now.

replies.text: Thank you for telling me your story. I want to stop this witch once and for all. Where can I find her?

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Thank you! You can find her house just south of here. You can't miss it as it is covered in beautiful flowers.
While raising your arm and waving your hand, you yell over the water: "Excuse me."
Shh. You are scaring the fish.

replies.text: Please? I need your help. I'm looking for my brother. His name is Andor. He looks like me. Have you seen him?
That's a really cool boat. Where can I get one?
[While Pointing behind Isobel, you yell] Look at the size of that fish behind you!

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Where?!

replies.text: [While laughing uncontrollably] "Shh, your scaring him away."

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Excuse me, young one! Wait! Thank you for sparing me earlier. You've shown true compassion.

replies.text: What ... do I know you? You're just a young girl?

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Yes, I was under a spell that made me appear as the witch. She wanted to test your heart. I'm glad you proved kind.

replies.text: Thank you, but you don't look well.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: I am not well. Which is why I have not run far from this awful place and this awful witch.

replies.text: What's wrong? Why can't you leave?
What happened to you here? How did you get here?

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Thank you again, my savior! I will go now.
I need nutrients! You see, I've been held down in that basement of that horrific house for what feels like a year.
I am too sick to talk about this right now.
All the witch ever gave me is something called 'Tonic of Blood'. At first, I refused to drink it, but soon I became desperate and I drank it.

replies.text: I've had one or two of those. They are not that bad.
Are those things even good for you?

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Yes, maybe in moderation. But after a few dozen, they do something to your body as I can no longer consume anything but them.
I really need to get my hands on a lot of those 'Tonic of Blood' potions. Can you help me? I need a lot.

replies.text: Well, I have twenty-five of those for you.
Well, I have twenty of those for you.
Well, I have ten of those for you.
Well, I have five of those for you and I'm not sure where I got them. Do you know where I can get some?
Well, I only have one of those for you and I don't remember where I got it. Do you know where I can get some more?
I'm sorry, but I don't have any of those.

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Well, I am not exactly sure about that as the witch would make it. Damn! I hate that smell. Damn! I love that taste however.

replies.text: Can you help me out a little bit? Do you know anything about them?

conversationlist_mt_galmore.message: Hold on. Let me think....
Ah, YES. I remember her saying that an "undead" friend of her's east of here taught her how to make them.

Dear Theodora,

I've come to visit you again today, but once more, I find your home empty. It's been nearly a month since I last saw you, and my heart grows heavier with each passing day.

Where have you gone, my dear? The village seems so quiet, as if all life has been drawn away. I've knocked on your door, looked through the windows, and even asked the few people I saw on the Duleian Road (do you know Rosmara, the "fruit lady"), but no one has seen you or heard a word.

Please, if you find this letter, send word to me at once. I cannot bear the thought of something having happened to you. If you've simply gone away for a time, I understand, but let me know that you are safe. I will return again in a week's time, praying that I find you here.

With all my love,
Mother

conversationlist_feygard_1.message:
It's been days since anyone has seen Odilia. At first, we thought she might have gone to visit her sister in Feygard, but she never mentioned leaving. The same happened with Philippa, and now Godelieve too. It's as if they vanished without a trace, all in their sleep. I remember Godelieve looked troubled the night before she disappeared, as though she was fighting some invisible force, but I dismissed it. I should have known something was wrong.

The village feels different now, quieter, emptier. The men are on edge, but we can't make sense of what's happening. The nights are the worst, filled with a heavy silence that chills the bone. I fear for Leofwyn and Theobald, and I can't help but wonder if something in the night is calling to them.

We're losing hope, and I'm terrified of what might happen next.

End Entry

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message:
The air around it feels heavy, pressing on your chest. Whispers you can't quite hear seem to emanate from the mark, tugging at the edges of your mind.
Do you dare to touch it?

The moment your hand meets the mark, an icy jolt shoots through your body. A voice echoes in your mind, low and venomous, yet pleading:
"You...You must help me...End this torment... Seek the one I am bound to... in the place you call Crossglen..."
Your vision blurs, and a suffocating sense of dread wraps around your heart. For a fleeting moment, you glimpse a shadowed figure, writhing in agony, before it vanishes.

You stagger back, your body cold and trembling. Something has changed.

The weight of the mark grows heavier on your mind. A strange, oppressive feeling claws at your chest, urging you to leave this place and return to Crossglen.
You can't shake the feeling that something is terribly wrong there--your father, Mikhail, needs you. You must hurry.

The pull of the mark is becoming harder to ignore. A sudden wave of dizziness washes over you, and the whispers grow louder. They speak of danger, of a life lost if you do not return.
You must turn back... time is running out. Crossglen calls. You cannot linger here.

Your steps grow heavier, the air thick with oppressive energy. The pull within your chest tightens, and the whispers now sound desperate, almost frantic.
Return to Crossglen... You cannot stay here. Your father's life is in peril. Do not test fate any longer!

You feel your breath catch in your throat, the world around you warping and twisting. The mark is burning, a cold fire coursing through your veins, clawing at your very soul.
GO NOW! Crossglen is in danger. You are too far from what matters. Return at once--before it is too late!
What's gotten into you? I'm fine, but the same can't be said for Leta. I've seen her pacing in that house of hers, muttering to herself like a madwoman. You might want to check on her.
I am most certainly not in the mood to deal with you right now. Why can't Mikhail ever control his kids?

You want to know? You want to understand? Fine. You'll see...but you won't like what you find.

[taunting] You shouldn't have meddled, little one. This vessel belongs to me now, and so does its anger!
The Dark spirit has been defeated, but you feel as if this issue is unresolved. Something is telling you that it has fled back to the devastated lands south of Stoutford.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: They weren't like that yesterday. I saw Leta in the fields, tending to her garden, just as spry as ever. Then this morning...well, you've seen it yourself.

[shaking his head, grim] Not a word. Just that vacant smile of hers, like everything's fine. Oromir, though...he's got this strange look in his eye. Like he knows something we don't.
[With a gentle smile.] Of course. Ask what you will. We owe you that much.

replies.text: Why were you affected too? Leta was the one possessed by the spirit, not you.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: While sighing, his voice remains steady.

Well, my child, you see, once I entered into the sacred bond of marriage with Leta, I too became bound to the spirit. Our lives, our fates, were entwined by the very vows we spoke. When she was touched by its darkness, I could not help but share in the burden.

replies.text: So, the bond between you two extended even to the curse?

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Yes. That's the nature of true union, is it not? In love and in struggle, we are as one. Her pain became mine, just as her redemption became ours. The spirit's malice sought to age us, to wear us down. But we endure, thanks to you.

replies.text: Do you regret it? Being tied to her curse?

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: While shaking his head with a warm smile, Oromir continues...

Never. Leta is my heart, my reason for every breath. If carrying this weight was the price of sharing my life with her, then I'd pay it a thousand times over. Love isn't just about the light, it's about standing together, even in the shadows.

replies.text: [pausing] That's admirable. I hope you both find some peace now.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: We will. Time may have taken its toll, but the darkness is gone. Now, we can live what remains of our days in quiet gratitude. Thank you, truly.
Oromir's voice is somber, yet a slight trember can be heard within it.

replies.text: Tomas? How could this happen to him? He's a grown man now, but he acts as if he's still that frightened child.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Our son...Yes, you are right. That is Tomas. Though, to him, he may as well be a stranger to himself.
Oromir sighs deeply while clasping his hands.

replies.text: ...grew older like you both, why does he seem...stuck, mentally?

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: When the spirit latched onto Leta, its curse didn't just affect her. It spread to everything close to her--her home, her family, even our boy. He was only two years old when it began...always holding her hand, always by her side. The spirit saw him as an extension of her, and so it bound him as well.

The spirit didn't just age us. It fed on our memories, our sense of self. Tomas was too young to defend himself from its grasp. It stripped away his connection to who he was. Trapping him in fear and confusion, unable to grow in mind, even as his body aged.

replies.text: Is there any way to help him? He's terrified to leave the basement.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Perhaps, with time. The curse is gone, but the scars it left behind are deep. He needs patience, kindness and someone to guide him back to himself. I fear we may not have the strength to do it alone.

replies.text: Yes, he needs time. I hope it works out for you three.

You've proven resourceful. Perhaps you are worthy of the knowledge I carry. The swamp holds more than muck and mire, and so do the creatures that call it home.

replies.text: You mentioned leeches earlier. What did you mean by that?

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Leeches are simple creatures, but they hold incredible power. With the right knowledge, they can purge poison, stop bleeding, and heal wounds that no salve can touch. Few have the courage to learn their secrets.
I don't waste my time on fools, but you've proven yourself. Watch closely.

See how the leech attaches itself? It draws out the bad humors, cleansing the blood. Placement is everything. Here, take this.

replies.text: [Extend my hand and take the leech.]
[Extend my hand and take the leech.]

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Don't underestimate them. In skilled hands, they are as effective as any blade or potion. Use them wisely.

replies.text: Thank you. Is there anything else I should know?

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Vaelric hands you a leech.
Yes. Don't waste them on minor cuts or trifling ailments. Save them for when they're truly needed. The swamp still has more to teach you, if you are willing to learn.

Once, I was a celebrated healer. They called me a miracle worker for curing the incurable. My methods were...unconventional. Leeches, parasitic creatures, even plants most would call poisonous. I used whatever the swamp could offer.

Innovation often breeds fear. When a Laumwill noble entrusted me with his life, I used every method I knew to save him. But he died under my care, and the courts called it murder. The Laumwills made certain there was no place for me among civilized men.
It's time to revisit Vaelric.

The pull of the mark is becoming harder to ignore. A sudden wave of dizziness washes over you, and the whispers grow louder. They speak of danger, of a life lost if you do not return.

Your steps grow heavier, the air thick with oppressive energy. The pull within your chest tightens, and the whispers now sound desperate, almost frantic.
Return to Mikhail...You cannot stay here. Your father's life is in peril. Do not test fate any longer!

You feel your breath catch in your throat, the world around you warping and twisting. The mark is burning, a cold fire coursing through your veins, clawing at your very soul.
TURN BACK NOW! Mikhail is in danger. You are too far from what matters. Return at once--before it is too late!

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: I came to Vaelric in my hour of greatest need, bearing little but a token of my past. A ring of no great value to anyone but myself. I was desperate, suffering, and he agreed to help me for a price. Not gold, not silver, but my ring. I was too weak to refuse, too lost to question his demand.
I have a story to tell only to "friends". So being my "friend" means giving me those two items you found.
There's nothing else of value or interest in this drawer as you've already stolen the ring.

Various trinkets and vials clutter the space, but your eyes are drawn to a small, unassuming pouch tucked toward the back. It feels too light for coins, too solid for herbs. Loosening the drawstrings, you reveal a ring, simple yet striking, just as Eryndor described.

As you slide open the wide drawer, its wooden frame creaks loudly, echoing through the quiet house. You freeze, heart pounding, listening for any sign that Vaelric may have heard from downstairs. After a tense moment of silence, you refocus and scan the contents.
And?

replies.text: I wasn't able to find any clues surrounding the grave site. Is there something you're not telling me?

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: No, just a suspicion I had. In any event, thanks for looking into it for me. Good luck on your search for Andor.
So, you return with my ring?

replies.text: Yes, here it is. [Hand it over]
Yes, here it is. [Take it off and hand it over.]

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Eryndor's ghost flickers with anticipation as you hold out the ring. His spectral fingers pass through it at first, but he quickly pulls back, composing himself.
You really did it? You took it from him? Hah... good. Maybe now he will understand what it is to have something stolen away.
Vaelric's expression darkens, his fingers tightening around his staff. He turns away for a moment, exhaling slowly before speaking.

replies.text: He says you treated him once, but you buried him alive. That's why he haunts you. He wants his ring back, or the hauntings will continue.
Please tell me more about Eryndor.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Eryndor... Yes, I remember. He came to me alone, desperate, barely able to stand. His condition was severe, far beyond anything my tinctures and poultices could mend. I did everything I knew. I bled out the sickness, cooled his fever, forced broth past his lips. But it wasn't enough. One morning, I found him still as death. No breath, no warmth. His skin had gone pale and lifeless.
He rubs his temple, his voice quieter now.

I had no choice but to lay him to rest. There was no kin to claim him, no priest to see to his rites. So I carried him to the graveyard myself, dug the earth with my own hands, and gave him what peace I could. It was the right thing to do... or so I thought.
His jaw tightens, regret flashing in his eyes.

But I was wrong. I was wrong. Somehow, he still lived. I don't know if it was some illness that mimicked death or if I simply failed to see the life still in him. Either way, my hands put him in that grave, and now his suffering is on me.
He hesitates, then steps toward a cabinet, opening a drawer with a sigh.
If his spirit will rest with this ring, take it. If that will end this curse, then let it be done.
So, you return with my ring?

replies.text: Yes, here it is. [Hand it over]
Yes, here it is. [Take it off and hand it over.]
I already gave it to you.
I have it, but I've decided to keep it for myself.
I'm wearing it, and you can't have it.
Yes, but I forgot to bring it with me. I will have to come back later.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Eryndor's ghost reaches out, his translucent fingers trembling as they hover over the ring in your hand.
You... you actually found it? After all this time?
His voice is softer now, no longer laced with bitterness. He takes the ring, though it merely passes through his spectral palm. For a long moment, he stares at it, lost in thought.
When I came to that swamp, I still had my bell, my music box, and this. But this ring was the only thing of real worth. The only thing I had left to bargain with when my body failed me.
He exhales a slow, weightless sigh, the glow of his form dimming slightly.
Vaelric took it as payment, believing he had done all he could for me. And I hated him for it. Hated him for leaving me in the dark, for shoveling earth over me when I still had breath in my lungs.
He clenches his fist, as if testing the solidity of his fading presence.
But now... now I see things clearer than I did in life. He was wrong, but not cruel. He truly thought I was beyond saving. And perhaps, in a way, I was.
He lifts his gaze to you, his expression unreadable, yet calm.

I have been bound to this world by resentment, by the belief that my suffering was without meaning. But now, with my ring returned, I feel... lighter. It's time to let go.

[With a final, grateful nod, Eryndor begins to fade, his form unraveling like mist in the wind. A whisper lingers in the air before vanishing entirely.]
He stares at the ring for a long moment, the glow of his form pulsing unevenly.

This was mine. My last possession, my last choice. He had no right to claim it when my body still had breath. And now? Now it is back in the hands it belongs in.

[Turning the ring in his hand, lost in thought.]

But don't think this is over. No... he will still know my presence. He will still feel my breath in the dark. This was never just about the ring. It was about what he did. About what he took from me that I can never get back.
His expression shifts, something unreadable in his flickering gaze. A strange hesitation. He looks away for a moment before turning back to you.
You have done me a service, and for that, I am grateful. But there is something else I need from you. Something unfinished. A debt of my own that I must see repaid.

There was one rival who stood above the rest. A relic hunter like myself, relentless and cunning. Her name is Celdar. We crossed paths often, always chasing the same artifacts, always trying to outmaneuver one another. And when it came to one particular prize, I won. The music box. It was something she sought desperately, something she believed should have been hers. I held onto it, not just for its rarity, but because I had bested her.
You did it? You were able to help me? You have prevented the future hauntings?

replies.text: Yes. Hence my being here with my hand out.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Well, let me start by saying that you have done me a great service, and for that, I will offer you something few others could. I am no merchant, but I do have remedies, ones you will not find elsewhere. One in particular may prove invaluable to you: the Insectbane tonic.

This tonic does more than ease a fever or numb the pain of a bite. It eliminates the infection entirely. If you have already fallen victim to the Insect contagion poison, one dose will purge it from your body. But more than that, it grants temporary immunity against reinfection. For a time, no swamp vermin, no festering bite, no tainted sting will take hold of you.

But such a remedy does not come cheaply. If you wish for me to prepare this tonic, you must gather the necessary ingredients yourself. Here is what I require:

Five Duskbloom flowers. These rare blossoms can be found in the deepest parts of the swamp, but the creatures there tend to be attracted to them. Their properties are delicate, so bring them fresh.

Five Mosquito proboscises. Harvested from the swamp mosquitoes. You will find no shortage of these creatures near stagnant waters, but mind their bites.

Ten bottles of swamp water. You will find plenty just outside my home. Surface water won't do. You'll need to reach deep, past the filth floating on top. The best stuff is settled at the bottom. Dark, thick, and rich with what gives the swamp its potency. Fill the bottles with that. Take these empty bottles and fill them yourself.

One sample of Mudfiend goo. A secretion found in the depths of mines and tunnels along the Duleian Road. It is the key component that binds the other ingredients together.

I require:
Five Duskbloom flowers. These rare blossoms can be found in the deepest parts of the swamp, but the creatures there tend to be attracted to them. Their properties are delicate, so bring them fresh.

Five Mosquito proboscises. Harvested from the swamp mosquitoes. You will find no shortage of these creatures near stagnant waters, but mind their bites.

Ten bottles of swamp water. You will find plenty just outside my home. Surface water won't do. You'll need to reach deep, past the filth floating on top. The best stuff is settled at the bottom. Dark, thick, and rich with what gives the swamp its potency. Fill the bottles with that. Take these empty bottles and fill them yourself.

Bring me these, and I shall prepare ten vials of the tonic for you. But understand this: my craft is no charity. If you seek to replenish your supply, you must pay the price. Four hundred and eighty gold per vial. A steep price, perhaps, but a fair one for something that could mean the difference between life and death.
I'll take all of the ingredients and your {4800} gold now and I will mix you up a batch of ten tonics
You see, I have to make ten tonics at a time and because I refuse to waste any of them, you must buy all ten at a cost of {4800} gold. Do you have the gold?
Here you go, ten Insectbane tonics.
I'll take all of the ingredients and your {4800} gold now and I will mix you up a batch of ten tonics
I also have other potions for sale. Would you like to take a look?
This must be where Vaelric suggested that you collect the swamp water from. Do you want to proceed?

replies.text: No way. That stuff looks nasty! Plus, there could be something in there that might badly hurt me.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: You kneel by the swamp's edge and roll up your sleeve. Surface water will not do. Bracing yourself, you plunge your arm in up to the elbow, feeling the thick, murky liquid seep between your fingers. With a slow, steady motion, you fill each bottle, ensuring they contain the dense, dark water Vaelric requires.
You dare? That ring is mine by right! It was stolen from me in death, just as my life was stolen before its time. I will not suffer another thief to profit from my misery.
Eryndor's spectral form flickers violently, the air around him growing thick with a bitter chill.
You may hold it now, but I promise you, it will not remain in your grasp for long. I will tear it from your fingers, along with the flesh that clings to it!

replies.text: I just hope I don't die for this.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: As Eryndor's spectral form wavers, his anguished cry echoes through the Galmore encampment before fading into the night. His essence shatters like mist caught in the wind, dissolving into nothing, but the air remains heavy, charged with an unseen weight. The encampment is silent, yet the silence is not one of peace.
So, it is done? You struck him down, ended his torment by force?
I suppose I should have expected as much.
His gaze lingers on you, his expression hard to read. Somewhere between frustration and resignation.
And what of the hauntings? Is it over?
With your hesitation preventing you from getting a word in...
I see. You took the ring for yourself and left his spirit unfulfilled. That was your choice.
He lets out a slow breath, his voice quieter now, laced with disappointment.
Andor would have done better.
[Turning away, he mutters:] I will take what peace I can, while it lasts. But do not expect my gratitude.

He worked his craft, took his payment, and let me rest. But I never awoke under his roof. I awoke beneath the earth, buried like a thing to be discarded. I clawed my way free, but the world had already moved on without me. My body failed, my breath faltered, and I perished alone.

And now, even in death, I remain. I am left with nothing while Vaelric hoards the last piece of my past. That ring was mine, and it was never his to take.
Return my ring, and this torment ends for both of us. Vaelric can go on with his life, and I will trouble him no more. That is my offer.

replies.text: You have been wronged, and I will not let that stand. I will get your ring back, one way or another.
If what you say is true, then this should not be settled with more deceit. I will speak to Vaelric. Maybe there is a way to resolve this fairly.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: We were in the middle of my story...
Then you see the truth. Vaelric took from me when I had nothing, and now he clings to what is not his. I will be waiting, but not always here in this spot. I will not forget this, friend.

Fair? What was fair about what he did to me? Do you think words will undo my suffering? I have lingered here too long for empty promises. But... if you truly mean to help, then do not return with excuses. Only with my ring.

replies.text: I will come back with answers.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Eryndor looks down at the music box, his expression unreadable.
But now? What does a dead man need with a relic? It is time to put an old contest to rest. I want you to find Celdar and give this to her. Not as a gesture of kindness, but because it is right.

replies.text: "Celdar", you say? I think I met her.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message:
Celdar is from Sullengard. If you don't recall speaking with her, that would be the place to start. But I suspect you have met her before. She is not one easily forgotten. She does not tolerate fools, nor those who waste her time with petty sales or empty words. Always clad in that garish purple dress of hers, standing out as if daring the world to challenge her. And she has never taken a loss lightly.

[He holds out the music box, waiting for you to take it.]
Have you brought the music box to Celdar yet?
Thank you!
What are you waiting for? Get going!
I thought you were looking for your brother? What's the matter, you couldn't find Andor, so you gave up and are now looking for someone new?
Now there's a name I haven't heard in a long time. I don't think she's been in town for a long time.
Oh, how can I help you? It's not Mayor Ale is it?

replies.text: What? No. I am looking for Celdar. I've heard she lives here. Is she around by chance?

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Yes she is a local, but she hasn't been seen around here for a while. Last I heard, she was headed for Brimhaven to do some shopping. Although, it is a long journey so she probably had to rest along the way.

Eryndor? That scoundrel finally got what was coming to him, did he? And now you're here, dangling a prize in front of me, expecting what? Gratitude? Payment? Hah! Whatever trick you think you're playing, I'm not biting.
Celdar pauses, and narrows her eyes as she assesses you.

replies.text: I have this music box. [Showing it to her.]

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Wait... you're serious, aren't you? He actually sent you to bring me the music box? Hmph. That doesn't sound like him. He was always the type to take, not give.

replies.text: He wanted to do the right thing.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: The right thing? Eryndor always did have a flair for the dramatic, but this... this is unexpected.
While crossing her arms, she begins to study you.
I spent years chasing that wretched box, only for him to snatch it out from under me. And now, after death, he decides to hand it over? What, am I supposed to be touched?
She scoffs but reaches out for the box.

replies.text: You reach out, your hands meet with the mysterious music box held between your hands and she takes it from you.
I can't believe this, but I forgot to bring the music box. Sorry. I will have to come back later. Stay here.
I just gave you that music box...

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Hmph. Fine. If he truly meant it, then I'll take it. Not that it changes anything. Eryndor and I were never friends, and his little gesture won't rewrite history. But... at least he finally understood what was mine to begin with.
She examines the box for a moment, running a hand over it before giving you a final look.
Here, take this longsword, I have no need for it. But...
Tell me, does he rest easy now, or is he still out there, clinging to unfinished business?

replies.text: No, he's not at peace. He's still out there, lingering about, bound by unfinished business.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Celdar exhales sharply, her fingers tightening around the music box as she looks away for a brief moment.
Hmph. Figures. The stubborn fool never knew when to let go.
She turns the box over in her hands, her expression briefly unreadable. Then, softer, almost to herself:
Chasing relics, chasing victories, chasing debts that can never be repaid... I suppose it doesn't matter now.
She shakes her head, composing herself before glancing at you once more.
Well, he made his choices. And I made mine. But... I wouldn't wish that kind of fate on anyone. Not even him.
With that, she straightens her posture, her usual sharpness returning, though the moment of reflection lingers in her eyes.

replies.text: I hope that in the future, that music box brings your happiness.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: What are you waiting for? Go get my ring back from Vaelric.
I feel restless here, I was a traveler when I was alive.
Thank you, friend.
He exhales sharply, shaking his head.

The hauntings have ceased. Vaelric will know relief, at least for a time.

And yet, a lingering unease settles in your gut. Something about the way Eryndor vanished, unfinished and unresolved, leaves you with the gnawing certainty that his story is not truly over.
Sticky mud coats your fet and legs, making every motion sluggish and heavy.
As you move your hands up the vine, you begin to hear the vine snapping...
The brittle vines blow off into the wind while you go tumbling to the ground.
As you walk by the table, in the corner of your eye, you catch a glimpse of someone's journal. Do you want to read it?

replies.text: Nah, I don't have the time or the interest.
Why not? I might learn something. Let's start with the page on the bottom of the pile.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message:
Day 1
I don't know if I'll ever see Remgard again, but if anyone finds this, know that I tried. I ran the moment I saw a chance, slipping past the guards, through the tunnels, and into the night. I thought the mountain would be my salvation, but it has become another prison. My leg is wounded from a bad fall, and my rations were left behind in my haste. This cabin is the only thing keeping me from dying out in the cold.

I think about you, Elira. About little Matrin and your sweet voice by the fire. I promised I would return, but now I fear I will break that promise. If only I had been stronger. If only I had never been taken to Undertell.

Day 2
I tried again tonight. The moment darkness swallowed the land, I hobbled my way to the river's edge, thinking I could follow the water down the mountain. But they were there - the river wretches. I heard them first, the awful gurgling croaks, the splashing as they slithered from the water. Their eyes glowed like dying embers, watching me, waiting.

I barely made it back inside before one of them lunged. My leg is worse now, and I have nothing left to bind it.

The hunger gnaws at me. I tried fishing, but the hooks in this cabin are rusted, the line too weak. There are old nets, but I do not have the strength to set them.

Tomorrow, I will try again. I have to.

replies.text: This is mildly interesting. Let's read the next page.
I've had enough. Time to go kill something.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message:
Day 3
The cold seeped into my bones last night. It is colder here than in the mines, though there we had fire - if we dug enough, if we obeyed. My hands shake too much to write properly. I tore the floorboards loose, hoping for dry wood, but it does little to warm this place.

I dreamed of the Heartstone. Of its glow deep in the dark, pulsing like a dying heart. We bled for it, all of us. Bent our backs, broke our bodies. They say it fuels the forges of kings, but to us, it was nothing but suffering. I wonder if the others still dig, still rot in the depths of Undertell. Or if they, too, have tried to flee and perished in the dark.

replies.text: This is getting better. Let's read the next page.
Reading is difficult. Killing is easy. I'm out of here.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message:
Day 4?
I lost track of time. The hunger dulls everything. My wound festers, and I am too weak to move. I hear the wretches outside every night now, closer than before. As if they can smell my weakness.

I wrote a letter to you, Elira. It's tucked beneath the heartstone. If anyone finds this journal, please... please bring it to Remgard. Let her know I never stopped trying to return.

I will rest now. Perhaps in dreams, I will walk home at last.

replies.text: Wow. This is awful to read.
What a weak creature this guy was.
This journal is so ancient looking that there's no way this Elira person is in Remgard or even still alive.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: With a deafening noise, the floor collapses and you fall through, along with stones and floorboards, into the basement.
The remains of the ladder are too high for you to reach.
Here is a good place to drop some rocks.

replies.text: I have no rocks to drop.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Plop.

replies.text: Twenty. I'm getting hot. Anyway - drop a rock.
Forty. Keep going! Drop a rock.
Fifty. Things are moving forward. Drop a rock.
Sixty. Looks almost ready. Come on, drop a rock.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Wow, the pile is rising at last.
Now the pile of stones looks high enough for me to reach the ladder.
Maybe I could climb these crates to get to the remains of the ladder somehow?
Could this chest work as an improvised staircase?

replies.text: Let's try to push the chest next to the barrels.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: With a lot of force you push the box forward.
You feel something hard beneath your feet. When you instinctively look down you notice some metal. Do you want to explore it?

replies.text: It's time to get dirty...well, even more dirty.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Kneeling down, you push aside loose dirt and rocks with your fingers. Bit by bit, you uncover a wooden shield braced with metal, its dirty and wet, but otherwise it's in great condition.
As you near the top, a streaking shadow crosses overhead. A hawk, sharp-eyed and swift, releases a piercing screech. The sound jolts you, fear sparks in your chest, and your grip gives way.
As you fall, you watch the hawk fly off out of sight.

You brush aside the branches and find an old chest tucked behind the tree. Inside lies a weathered tome, bound in cracked leather. It's an unknown book on the art of fighting. You open it and begin to read, flipping through dense pages until a chapter catches your eye, "Striking by Rhythm and Force". It speaks of precision and control, of mastering your strikes. As you finish reading, knowledge sharpens your mind and your weapon feels steadier in your grasp. Just then, a hawk screeches overhead and dives. It snatches the book from your hands and vanishes into the sky. But in your grip remains a single page, torn free in the scuffle. Somehow you instantly feel like a better fighter.
You spot a glint of crimson feathers and a golden beak in the distance, unlike any bird you've seen before...
...but it sees you and runs away. Maybe you will see it somewhere else?

replies.text: Huh, it ran away from me? That's never happened to me before.
Maybe it's the sound of my boots that's scaring it off...I should try taking them off and moving quieter.
Oh, I have an idea. Let's leave some corn for it. Yeah, that should work to gain its trust.
Hey, maybe I could leave a red apple. It might help it warm up to me.
How about I set out a green apple? That could be enough to earn its trust.
What if I leave an orchard apple from Deebo's farm behind? That might gain its trust.
I know, I'll drop a rosethorn apple on the ground. Let's see if that gets me on its good side.
What am I doing wrong here?

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: It does not see you!
Just over there on the hill, a creature with obsidian feathers and a gleaming golden beak watches from afar...
...but it sees you and runs away. Maybe you will see it somewhere else?
You spot a glint of crimson feathers and a golden beak in the distance, unlike any bird you've seen before...
...but it sees you and runs away. Maybe you will see it somewhere else?
There's a glimpse of something rare ahead, dark feathers and a vivid red crest catching the light as it turns its head...
...but it sees you and runs away. Maybe you will see it somewhere else?
You see a rare bird in the distance, its form striking against the wild - red-crested, golden-beaked, almost like a story come to life...
...but it sees you and runs away. Maybe you will see it somewhere else?
You've just killed the Rubycrest strider bird, but for an unexplainable reason, you feel as if you've done the wrong thing.
Leave! You are not welcome here.
Oh, a visitor? Welcome! Come, come. Sit down.

replies.text: No, thanks, I have to go.
Why are you up here alone?

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: ...wait a second. Hold that thought. [while leaning in...] Please come closer. [He sniffs your hands]
You killed my friend!

replies.text: Well, he probably deserived it. Whoever this person is.
Me? Nah. Not me. [Lie] I've never killed anybody.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Yes, yes you most certainly killed him. His scent is all over your hands.
You killed my best friend! You killed the only thing I have to talk to up here on these hills.

replies.text: Who did I kill? You are the only person up here that I've encountered.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: You killed the unique and exotic bird that calls these hills "home". My best friend! So I am now asking you to leave. [pointing his finger towards the door.]

replies.text: I will stay. You are not the boss of me.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Just a man with a brush and a view. I spend my days painting what others overlook.

replies.text: Well, I'm just an explorer with a weapon.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Peace and perspective. Down there, it's noise and trade. Up here, I see everything more clearly.
What are they?

replies.text: I found this broken bell and a music box. [Show Vaelric.]

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: I see. Interesting, but not very helpful. Go explore the Galmore encampment east of the graveyard and report back to me when you find something helpful.

Interesting, but not helpful. Go back and search for something useful. It makes sense if you search close by to where you found this other item. And don't keep running back to me every time you find something so mundane.
You notice that one of the graves looks to have been dug-up in the not-so-distant past.
You notice that one of the graves looks to have been dug-up in the not-so-distant past.
Clearly more agitated than usual, pacing and muttering.
[Voice trembling but defensive.]
Leta pauses, clutching her head as if in pain. Her voice shifting, darker and more guttural.

replies.text: Leta, talk to me. What's going on?

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: You wonder if Vaelric knows anything about this.
But you really don't know what to think about it.
Yes...
Undertell; the pits of the lost souls. Travel south to the devastated wastelands of Galmore Mountain and follow the tracks from there.
What is it?

replies.text: I'm looking for some place called "Undertell", do you know where it is?
I'm looking for my brother. His name is Andor and he looks a lot like me.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: With a terrified expression on his face, Myrelis slowly raises his arm and points you to the southwest.
Over there, but it looks like it's blocked.

replies.text: How do I get past those barricades?

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: No, I'm sorry, but you are the first human that I've seen in...geez, I can't even remember how long.
You are to leave now. [pointing his finger towards the door.]
There's sorrow in you...maybe even regret. Perhaps you're not the monster I feared. Very well. You may stay, but only because I sense "warmth" in your heart and we won't speak of the bird again.

As you cross the bridge, it begins to sway side to side which instills an element of dread in you as you fear toppling over the railing into that water will most certainly pull you over the cliff's edge and down into the abyss.
There's a really strong stink of a decomposing animal emanating out from under the trees.

replies.text: I guess one of the many aroughcuns on this mountain will enjoy that later.
Oh, that is nasty. I need to escape this stink now.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Yes?

replies.text: You mentioned leeches earlier. What did you mean by that?

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: This gold will really help me rebuild my life. Now I just need to decide where to do that.
Feygard? Why would I ever want to live there?

replies.text: Well, I've heard such wonderful things about that glorious city. There's so many opportunities for almost anyone.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Feygard? I don't know, maybe. But thank you for your suggestion.
Nor City? Why would I ever want to live there?

replies.text: I'm really not sure why except that I've met so many Shadow folk that rave about that place.

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Nor City? I don't know, maybe. But thank you for your suggestion.
That gold you're holding... it belonged to my family. Stolen from us not long ago, taken by hands no better than yours.
She takes a cautious step forward.
You can do right and give it back. Or you can learn what happens to those who carry what's not theirs.

replies.text: If it's truly yours, then take it. [Hand over the recently looted gold.]
Oh, you mean that gold that now belongs to me? It's now mine.
[Lie] Oh, you mean the 500 gold pieces that I found back there? [Pointing west.]

conversationlist_mt_galmore2.message: Thank you very much!
Egrinda lunges at you.
Liar!
You don't have what I require in order to make them.
