Do not challenge her. Do not delay near her rock. Sail past, and accept the loss she takes.
[she meets your eyes] Scylla is not cruel. She is simply hungry.
And you might meet Charybdis.

replies.text: Yes, we have met her indeed.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: She is no creature of claw or tooth. She is hunger in the lake.
Three times each day, the waters descend into her throat. Three times they rise again.
Ships caught too near are pulled under - not smashed, but taken.
She hesitates.
Where they go, I cannot say. Some say downward. Some say elsewhere.
I have never known a sailor who returned the same.
[quietly] Or returned at all.
Sounds promising.
You cannot avoid Scylla. Charybdis or the cyclops are your choice.
With Charybdis - I wouldn't trust her, you may lose everything.
The cyclops - well, they don't like me. And the feeling is mutual.
You survived me. That suggests you prefer thought over force. You will need that.
The lake ahead does not hate you. It does not love you either.
It simply waits.
We should leave now.
The door to the cave is securely locked.
The mirror blurs. It obviously rejects you.
Baaah.
Baaah.

replies.text: You look strong enough to carry me. I hang down beneath you, and you pull me outwards.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: The sheep carries you willingly.
Serve yourself, take all you like!

replies.text: I will take some fresh toasted bread.
Let's enjoy a whole bunch of sweet grapes.
I will sip a tiny glass of that ruby wine.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: I love to see you improving! You may refresh yourself as long as you wish.

replies.text: I think I'll take some more...
Great! It is a wonderful place here!

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: You don't want to leave this paradise island.

replies.text: I don't want to leave this paradise island.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: Take as much as you need.
You may leave whenever you wish.
But if you face storms or monsters tomorrow, you might prefer to do so at your strongest.
[points to the table] One grape is a courtesy. A meal is preparation.
Oh. A traveler.
[examines you carefully] You look capable. But tired.

replies.text: I rarely get time to rest.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: I host those who pass through. You are free to come and go as you please.
Kalypso picks a single grape from the plate.
These grow only here. The soil is... unusual.
Try one. If you dislike it, I shall be offended for exactly three seconds.
It is not enchanted wine. Not a vow. Not chain that binds you.
It's just fruit.

replies.text: I might have a closer look at it.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: [slightly amused] You may inspect it if that makes you feel heroic.
[watches intensely] Ah. You feel it, don't you?
As a token of my friendship, I give you this tiny green key.
Keep it safe. You'll know when you can use it.
The island rewards those who survive long enough to reach it.
[Her eyes flashing] Muscles awakened. Breath deepens. Old fatigue loosens its grip.
[Honest admiration] It suits you.
Now have a look at yourself how you have evolved!
You felt it.
[She does not smile] The island does not stop your feet.
It stops your wanting.
You can walk to the shore. You can touch the ship. You can even set a hand on the oar.
[softly] But your body does not wish to leave.
No. You make your own choices.
The fruit strengthens what is already there.
Muscle. Breath. Certainty.
Kalypso looks at you carefully.
And it quiets the part of you that is always preparing to suffer again.
Tell me... Did you feel threatened?
I did not bind you. I did not cast a spell of obedience.
People think I imprison sailors.
I do not.
They simply discover they are tired of striving.
[A faint, almost sad smile.] Strength without struggle is very comfortable.
You wait.
[Calmly] The island's gift fades. It is not permanent.
When you feel hunger again, when you feel lack again...
You will walk onto that ship without resistance.
$playername - you are free. You always were.
Hello, child. Sit down, you may keep me company.

replies.text: I have beeswax with me now.
We have a problem sir. There's a rocky reef that the captain doesn't want to sail past. He's afraid of some singing creatures.
I have found all the new parts for your map.
I have found some of the new parts for your map.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: Oh, really? We have sirens here in the lake? Fascinating!
Of course! Everyone with a bit of education knows about them.
However, no one has yet returned alive to report what they sing - if that's what they do.

replies.text: Then my trip is already over.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: No, of course not. Just put something into your ears. Wax should work. Do you have beeswax with you?
You can get the best beeswax directly from a beekeeper. I know one: Leofric, I would trust him.

replies.text: Leofric? Where can I find him?
Oh, that guy. I remember him.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: Beeswax? From Leofric I hope. Good, give it to me. I can create earplugs for you.
When he isn't out and about, he's at his bee meadow behind the Foaming Flask - in case you know it, kid.

replies.text: A rather crowded and noisy place.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: You need one piece of wax for each pair of earplugs. So, four in total - for yourself, and for the crew.
With practiced movements, Thyrope made several pairs of earplugs.
Here, take these earplugs. The wax was perfect for them, they'll work well.

replies.text: Thank you. I'm going to go and try them out right away.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: Good, good. Then off you go - the ship is waiting!
I am Thyrope Splathershed, the famous scholar and cartographer.

replies.text: Splathershed? Haven't I heard that name before?

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: A map maker.

replies.text: Then you must travel a lot. Have you seen my brother Andor?

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: You probably know my brother, who wrote the famous treatise on the history of Dhayavar.

replies.text: Maybe. What are you doing here?
Talking of brothers - have you seen my brother Andor?

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: Probably not. I mainly focus on the environment so I can create the most accurate maps possible.
There's less and less terra incognita... sorry, children don't understand these technical terms - I mean unknown parts of the world. My work is getting more and more difficult.
Here in Remgard, I've struck gold. The great lake here is well known in the coastal regions - but what's in the lake itself?
That's what I want to find out, and then I'll become famous with my map of the great lake.

replies.text: So you want to charter a ship and explore the lake? Sounds exciting.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: What? No, absolutely not!
I'm not allowed to go myself. It would be an immeasurable loss to humanity if something were to happen to me.
But I'm looking for someone to make the trip and tell me about it.
You look like you don't have anything better to do right now anyway. Will you make the trip for me?

replies.text: [muttering] Nothing to do? If you only knew...

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: The ship is ready to depart from the dock, and the passage has already been paid for.

replies.text: Hmm. It sounds exciting. I agree to your proposal.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: So then, Captain Burry will greet you on board!
Ohh, I'm almost dying to have the entire map complete.
Really!! That fast? I am extremely impressed. And delighted!
You talk of how you nearly got stuck at Kalypso on a paradise island.
You explain how you passed by the sirens.
You talk of the captain and his crew being turned into pigs.
You talk of blinded cyclops and sheep.
And how the six-headed monster Scylla had attacked your ship.
And finally, you raved about the gloomy land beneath the lake. What it was like to be swept into the abyss with the ship, and then to resurface again.
Thyrope Splathershed didn't seem entirely sure whether to believe your incredible story.
Thank you so much for these extremely entertaining experiences. Perhaps I'll write a story about them sometime.
As a reward you can use Captain Burry and his ship whenever you want. I will pay for it.

It swirls around you, faster and faster, until everything is black.
You wake up in a daze. The ship survived the maelstrom!
The ship has made it back up again!
The ship has made it back up again!
The ship has made it back up again!
The ship has made it back up again!
The ship has made it back up again!
The ship has made it back up again!
Hey! A round of mead for everyone! We sailed the entire lake!
Come closer, $playername, and learn the truth of every road you have walked and every lie told about it.
We know the names you forgot, the faces you left behind, and the fate waiting at your door.
Stay, and we will sing you the ending of your story.
No man has sailed past us unchanged, for knowledge always takes its price.
Listen, and you will understand why your brother still feels farther away with every mile.
Untie yourself, clever one - wisdom should never be heard from a distance.
What you seek is not safety, but certainty, and we can give you that.
You have outwitted monsters and men, but you have never dared to face the truth we sing.
Hear us, and you will finally know which of your victories were earned, and which were merely spared.
We sing not to trap you, $playername, but to show you what you have been running from.
One day, the knots won't be tied tightly enough. Or the blocked ears won't be closed tightly enough.
We are hungry but patient.
End of journey. This is as far as we can go.

replies.text: Hey, there is still so much to explore.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: See the rocky island over there? This is where the sirens live.
Dreadful creatures. They have lured many a brave crew to the rocks. The ships were wrecked there, and the crew was never seen again.

replies.text: Hmm, then just ignore it and we'll drive by really quickly.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: Absolutely not. I will not sacrifice my ship and crew to the childish wish of a kid.

replies.text: Let me think: If you didn't hear the sirens, everything would be OK, right?

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: Of course. But we can't cover our ears and steer a ship at the same time.

replies.text: Look, I have earplugs here, take them and you can drive through here as often as you like without any problems.
Look, I have earplugs here, take them and you can drive through here as often as you like without any problems.
Remember the earplugs I have given you. Use them to drive through here as often as you like without any problems.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: Sounds like a plan. And you? How do you plan to stop yourself from simply jumping overboard?

replies.text: I'll take earplugs too, of course.
Just tie me to the mast. And whatever you do, don't untie me, no matter how much I beg.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: Sounds like a plan. But we need a total of 4 pairs.

replies.text: Oh. Then let's turn back once more.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: That's what we'll do. We'll be the first to cross the Sirens' Passage alive.
That's what we'll do. We'll be the first to cross the Sirens' Passage alive.

replies.text: And I am very curious to know what the sirens are shouting that lured so many to their doom.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: You have to tell me later.
And I'll keep your pair of earplugs safe for you, just in case.
Hello kid. Finally, a sober tavern patron!

replies.text: Yes, the noise in here is almost unbearable.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: That's why I have produced these earplugs from beeswax. I could sell you some of them.

replies.text: With pleasure. I'd need 4 pairs for me and the crew. Show me what you have for sale.

[sniffs] Hm. The cave smells... strange today.
Oh, a guest! How unusual.
Don't be alarmed. I'm not alarmed by myself either.
[looking in the mirror] I just look dangerous.
[to the sheep] Quiet now. The visitor is looking.
You're in luck, little one. It's not a holiday today.
[grins proudly] But it will be soon.
The door is locked. You can't leave now. Don't be angry. Rules are rules.

This door has no key. Keys always get lost... 
It only opens when I look in this mirror. Clever, clever - just like me.

replies.text: So I can't just kill you to get out again.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: What? How you dare? Me the mightiest of all cyclops! Me Polyphem!
[beats his chest] My relatives will be coming for the next feast.
My hungry brothers.
[leans toward the player] And I'll bring the main course.
[straightens up, smugly] You can stay until then. The sheep are nice. They don't talk much.
You should take a leaf out of their book.
[turns to the mirror, straightens up] Me too, by the way. Nice, I mean. Very nice, in fact.
They say I have an eye for guests.
Who are you, anyway?
Nobody, huh? But that's not important. I just need to know what to call the dish.
Without another word, Polyphem falls onto his bed and immediately begins to snore loudly.
Hmmm? [Polyphem opens his eye for a brief moment.]
Hmmm? [Polyphem opens his eye for a brief moment, but long enough for you.]

replies.text: You pour the harsh soapy water directly into Polyphem's eye.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: It's a good thing sheep are so easy to distinguish from humans.
HA! Are you trying to sneak your way through here acting like a sheep?!

replies.text: Does it really catch the eye?

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: My favorite sheep! Your bleating sounds a bit unusual today. But I recognize you among hundreds by your wool.
Hop, hop, run outside and enjoy the delicious grass.
Baaaaah!

replies.text: Thanks, that worked out perfectly! But just to be on the safe side, carry me all the way to the ship.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: I'd better not go into the cave. No sheep will save me again.
AAAAH - MY EYE!
MY GOOD EYE!
[staggers backward, flailing blindly] That burns!
That's cheating!
[angry] YOU! Little one! WHERE ARE YOU?!
Calm down. Stay calm.
I'll see you again in a minute.
I CAN'T SEE ANYTHING ANYMORE!
[yells outside] BROTHERS! HELP!
[bangs against the cave wall] HELP! I'VE BEEN BLINDED!
[voices from outside, muffled, bored] What's wrong, Polyphem?
NOBODY! NOBODY BLINDED ME!
A stunned pause outside.
... What?
If nobody blinded you, why are you screaming?
BECAUSE IT HURTS!
[desperately] NOBODY WAS DOING IT!
HE'S STANDING HERE! OR WAS STANDING! NOT ANYMORE!
Then cool your eye.
And stop drinking.
Laughter outside, footsteps receding.
COME BACK!
HE'S DANGEROUS!
[quieter, offended] Very dangerous indeed. But nothing against me, Polyphem!
Coward! Invisible coward!
[sniffs] I can still smell you.
Never mind. You're not getting out of here.
I'll let the sheep out, then I'll find you more easily.
Don't go yet, you haven't thoroughly explored the cave.
Ah, there is Nobody. You think you're particularly clever, don't you?

replies.text: Well, it has worked with your brother.

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: Now let go of the ram and act like a man, kid.

replies.text: Well, you'll see what you get for it. Attack!

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: Our brother has made us a magnificant gift: We get to hunt our own holiday roast...
So let's get to the ship. The ram can carry me there again.
A bucket of water? Surely something can be done with that...
On a whim, you dissolve the soap in the water. That must sting badly if someone gets it in their eye.
This device has a green key hole.
You hear a sharp click and a faint rumbling. The key vanishes.
This device has a golden key hole.
You hear a sharp click and a faint rumbling. The key vanishes.
This device has a stone grey key hole.
You hear a sharp click and a faint rumbling. The key vanishes.
The key vanishes, but nothing else happens.
You can't even blink before Scylla's head darts out and bites.

For a moment, time seems to stand still.
Then all hell breaks loose.
You have managed to defeat another one of Scylla's monstrous heads.
You better had not.
BOOM!
I am not sure... I hope it isn't...
BOOOOOM!

replies.text: Again! Captain Burry - what is this?

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: The Taurophag! We are doomed!
BOOM! BOOOOOM!!

replies.text: Something is ramming us from below! Can nobody help us?

conversationlist_lake_laeroth_2.message: BOOOOM!
The Taurophag is no more. We have survived it!
We cast for names.
The water keeps them.
Wood floats. Memory sinks.
Someone is shouting: "Shallows ahead!"

conversationlist_undertell.message: THIS PERSON IS TRYING TO DESTROY ME!

replies.text: No, no I am not. I am here to help you.

conversationlist_undertell.message: You...you sound like the others did before they lied.

replies.text: I know about the talisman. The folded coin.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Then you know why I can't come down. If it's gone...it will come back.

replies.text: I found it. I have the folded coin.
But I already gave it to you, remember?
Actually, I know about it, but I don't have it yet. Sorry.

conversationlist_undertell.message: You have it? Then throw it to me. Please. Don't come closer.
HELP!
She fumbles, then grips it tightly. Her breathing slows.
Safe...I forgot what that feels like.
Safe...I forgot what that feels like. I cannot stay here anymore.
Back to them. The others who waited. Meet me there. I do not walk alone now.
My name is Syrra. Thank you for bringing it back.
It's unsafe to walk on top of these large rocks.
HELP! SOMEBODY HELP ME!
STAY AWAY FROM ME!
I know. It still follows me. Just not as closely.

replies.text: Fear does not decide where you stand.

conversationlist_undertell.message: No. But it remembers. I will too.
It is.
Yeah, sure, twenty-five thousand and I take a couple of your fingers too?

You want the house for yourself? Now that is interesting. Most people shy away from that cursed glow, but I can see ambition in your eyes. Hm. I could let it go for forty thousand gold...but gold alone won't earn my trust. If I sell it to you, I need proof you can be useful to me.
There's a small matter I want handled. Do this, and the price will stay at forty thousand. Refuse, and I'll reconsider whether you're worth the trouble.

replies.text: What do you want from me?

conversationlist_undertell.message: If you want the house, I'll need proof that you can handle business my way. There's a card dealer who runs games in the back of the tavern here in Brimhaven. He operates because I allow it. That means he owes me a regular fee, call it an 'operation tax' if you will.

He's late. Bring me what he owes, and don't let him wiggle out of it. I want every bit of the five thousand gold. When you return with the gold, I'll know you're serious, and the deed will be yours for forty thousand more.

replies.text: I'll be right back. Keep that deed handy.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Sure thing! As soon as I see forty-five thousand gold, you will see the deed to the house. Remember, you have my 'operation tax' gold too.

replies.text: Forty-five thousand?! I don't have that kind of gold.
Here, take the fourty-five thousand and give me the deed and the key.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Ah...so this is for Nocmar? The man who couldn't pay his debt and lost everything. And now you want me to just hand it back? Hah! If he wants redemption, let him pay double what he owed. Fifty thousand gold, no less. You bring me that much, and I'll give you the deed and the key.

replies.text: Fifty thousand gold?! Are you nuts? How about twenty-five housand?
Fifty thousand gold? I don't have it.
Here, take the fifty thousand and give me the deed and the key.

conversationlist_undertell.message: A pleasure doing business with you.
Well, then you better go find it.
Do you hear it now? The world hums with the memory of its first breath. Silence was never the absence of sound...it was waiting.

Kazaul'te varmun iktel urul.
Klatam ur turum Anavrin.
Kazaul'thra mor'gul ven'taar.
Uruk tharum vel Kazaul'ten mor.
Kazaul hamat urul.
Kazaul'the vurmor Anavrin urthaal!

So...the Fifth Master breathes once more.
You have undone silence itself, mortal. The rift shall open again, and through it we will see our dominion restored.
The Kazaul acolyte stands before Anavrin's shrine, its hands trembling as it unrolls the aged parchment. The air grows colder, shadows stretching across the floor.
The acolyte begins to read from the pages, the syllables harsh and alien.
Kulauil hamar urum Kazaul'te...Kazaul hamat urul...Klaatu ur turum Kazaul'te!
The parchment disintegrates in its grasp. The acolyte trembles violently, energy surging around the shrine.
You have done as we asked. The ritual of Five Aspects is complete...and with it, truth returns to the world.
The Shadow that your kind worship is not what you believe. It is no benevolent guardian, no path to balance. It is the echo of our masters...the Kazaul.

replies.text: That cannot be true. The Shadow guides and protects.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Believe what soothes you. Denial is the comfort of the living. But when you walk in its darkness again, listen...and you will hear our voices in its breath.

replies.text: You lie. The Shadow is not Kazaul.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Perhaps. Or perhaps you already know the truth, but your heart fears its shape. Leave now, child of dust. The Fifth is awake, and the world will not remain silent much longer.
Good work, my friend. You have saved Dhayavar.
You shall have your reward. But first you shall know my secret: I was the twelfth shade.

Worry not, fear not - I shall not harm you. When I said that in the confusion of the War, us shades hid, that's not strictly true. An Elytharan mage caught up with me, who was about to be the last to hide. She could have killed us, but I think her energy was nearly spent.

Instead she told me: "Until now, you have sustained fantasies in which you are the adventurers in magic, the pioneers in a new form of magic. Comforting daydreams in which you are always right. But no more. The fantasy is over. I have taken it away. For this is my judgement upon you: that you shall know, from this moment on, exactly how craven and selfish and monstrous you are."
Her spell stripped away my justifications. It made me realize what a monster I was.
Then she said - when your erstwhile colleagues, who hide now, are neutralized, you shall find peace. So $playername, thank you for liberating me.
Wear it if you want to overcome the resistance of the Kha'zaan shades. It should let you get past their safeguards.

You're back so soon?

replies.text: I'm getting thrown out of Undertell.

Wear the ring that the Holy One give you if you want to talk to me.

replies.text: Oh, you now too? Let me put it on now.

As you have truly vanquished the Kha'zaan and resisted their whispers, Elythara grants her favor. Through this ring, her blessing now flows anew.

replies.text: No luck. I'm still getting thrown out of the caverns.

Through devotion, even if the Kha'zaan lost their corporeal forms, they became incorporeal shades. And survived.

During the confusion of the War, this section was overlooked. As the Elytharan mages cleansed Dhayavar, the war reached Undertell and was fought in these passages. Spells and counterspells everywhere. In this confusion, the shades hid here, weakened but alive. And here they remain.

replies.text: Let them be. I will just search for my brother Andor and get out. Tell me what to avoid.

conversationlist_undertell.message: If only it were that simple. These shades gain strength from the life force of the living. As no one has come here, and you are the first, they shall awaken. The longer you stay, the stronger they will grow. Soon enough they will escape these passages and haunt Dhayavar once more.

replies.text: What do I need to do?

conversationlist_undertell.message: You must destroy each shade you encounter in this cavern. There were twelve who hid here. You should find eleven of them still around.
There is not much time to tell you more. The shades grow stronger. Go hunt them! May Elythara bless you.
You are back once more!

replies.text: It is no use. They are just making me disoriented. Maybe I should give up?

conversationlist_undertell.message: Not if you want to save your brother, your family and Dhayavar.
Let me think...
In the town of Sullengard, there is a statue of Elythara. Pray to her for aid.

replies.text: That is the statue of Elythara? So close to Nor City?

conversationlist_undertell.message: Sullengard is a riddle bound in contradiction. Though it stands as the southernmost town sworn to the light of Elythara, it does not bend the knee to Feygard. Its people hold Feygard in quiet contempt, for its levies, its corruptions, its heavy rule, and the favoring of blood over merit. They veil these sentiments behind courteous silence, and so to outsiders they seem neutral. Even the statue bears no name. It is spoken of only as the Holy One.

replies.text: And me praying will not kick a hornet's nest?

conversationlist_undertell.message: No one will notice. Except maybe a few kids.
O Holy One, Preserve Us.
Why did you have to come here?

replies.text: I need clarity. What am I supposed to be doing?

conversationlist_undertell.message: Child, I will tell you later. Not enough time to tell you. Go hunt!
Now, no thanks to you, my soul has become reinfected, and we shall lay Dhayavar to waste, starting with you.

replies.text: Today, you will be removed from this world.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Memory of the self endures first. Pain follows identity. Systems are not remembered, they are endured. You must listen again.
Then you heard structure without belief. A system reveals itself through repetition. You must listen more.
Silence is not absence. It is what remains when speech was never permitted.

Then you have more than one account. That allows comparison, but only if you listen for what does not repeat. Systems reveal themselves at their edges. Return. Do not seek another voice. Seek the limit of speech itself
I asked you to listen, not for stories, but for failure. If Undertell erased the Elytharan deliberately, it would not do so in only one way. Return. Listen for difference.

Undertell!
That book was written carefully. Not to preserve truth, but to survive being questioned.
The Aewatha Kingdom was meticulous in year four hundred and thirty-two. Stone was counted. Labor was measured. Voices were not.

The Elytharan followers sent into those mines did not vanish. They were made unrecordable. If even one of them still remembers themselves, then this book is incomplete. You have already walked Undertell. Return and listen for what the pages avoid.

replies.text: I will return to Undertell and listen.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Of course they do. History records stone and steel, but memory lives in people even after death. You have given voice to what was buried. That is worth more than any written account.
Definitely. Count on me. Glad you could help him, the poor sod.
What is more important than a kidnapping?

replies.text: Please keep these {4850} gold coins for safekeeping. Rain has asked for you until he gets over his hangover, he'll come collect them when he is ready.

conversationlist_undertell.message: W-w-w-well?
W-w-whatever y-y-you say.

replies.text: You need to pay Shannal's descendant.

conversationlist_undertell.message: I have to pay this person? How can you be serious? Look at me, I just recently got of that Feygard prison. I don't have any gold.
All I have is fifty gold, I swear of it.

replies.text: Are you kidding me? Let me call the ghost - she must be nearby...

conversationlist_undertell.message: N-n-no, I found some more in my other pocket. I have 500 gold.
H-h-how about a {1000}?

replies.text: Old sins cast long shadows. Try harder.

conversationlist_undertell.message: You'll bankrupt me! Well, here's 5000. It's all my savings I secreted away before I was arrested and put in a Feygard prison.

replies.text: That should be enough. Stay out of trouble. You're safe for now.

conversationlist_undertell.message: What do you want?

replies.text: To show you this traders' coin.

conversationlist_undertell.message: W-w-w-where did you get t-t-t-that?

replies.text: A ghost near Galmore Mountain asked me to show it to you.

conversationlist_undertell.message: G-g-g-g-almore! I am dead.
Oh well, we're not proud of it. My ancestor was one of those who would force or capture people to work in the mines of Undertell. He would be paid in these coins to get these people.

replies.text: What is that coin? What does it mean?

conversationlist_undertell.message: Can't really say. We're not happy about it. He was the black sheep of the family.

replies.text: Like you're any better. The apple doesn't fall far from the tree.

conversationlist_undertell.message: A ghost asked you to show m-m-me? I'm dead. Since the ghost is here after all these years, it could be looking for revenge. My life for her suffering.

replies.text: Old sins cast long shadows. However, perhaps I could talk to her, ask her to spare you?

conversationlist_undertell.message: W-w-will you? T-t-t-thank you! P-p-p-please help me.
Have you t-t-talked to the ghost y-y-yet? P-p-please hurry.
...Unless you're not here to play. Don't tell me Alkapoan sent you for his damned tax again?

replies.text: Yes. He sent me to collect the operation tax.
You owe Alkapoan. I'm here to take what's his.

conversationlist_undertell.message: [Grumbles] Always the same story. Alkapoan's cut, never mine. Fine, here. Take your five thousand gold and tell him I'm clear...until next month.
Take what's his? Ha! He already bleeds me dry every month. How much is it this time?
Slams the table, six?! That greedy vulture...fine, here. Just get out before I change my mind.
Speak the names of the lost when you can. We were men once, not shadows in stone. That is all a slave could hope for.

replies.text: I will honor your memory by continuing my search.

conversationlist_undertell.message: That weapon...must you hold it where I can see it? Even in death I know its glow.
Wrong? To you it is a finely forged weapon. To us...it was an executioner's tool.
When the Shadow rose, many who came for the Elytharans carried heartsteel. It cut through armor with frightening ease, but that was never what we feared most.
Those struck down by heartsteel often found no peace. Too many never reached Elythara's embrace. Instead, they lingered...as you see us now.

replies.text: So these weapons created the ghosts?

conversationlist_undertell.message: No. The weapon was only a tool. It was those who wielded it, and the darkness they served, that filled our halls with restless souls.

replies.text: I never knew any of this.

conversationlist_undertell.message: I believe you. Had I thought otherwise, I would not have spoken with you. Keep your weapon if you must, but remember what it once meant to my people.
If you want to talk about something else, then please, get it out of my sight.
The pick is light in my hand and heavy in my memory. We were driven into the deep seams with only a lamp and a promise. Many never climbed back.

replies.text: What was it like down there?

conversationlist_undertell.message: Hardship was the only thing we owned. The mountain took the rest. But remembering us is enough. Few living souls do.

replies.text: I will remember that, but I must continue my search.

conversationlist_undertell.message: I will not speak while that glowing stone is in your pack. It stirs old pain. Set it down and return if you want my words.

replies.text: All right. I will set it down.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Sure, you do that.

Dark, cold, and full of smoke. The tunnels shook when the rock groaned. We dug at glowing seams until our hands bled. The overseers said the ore was precious to Nor City, though none of us were told why. We were tools, nothing more.

replies.text: Is there anything I can do to honor you?

conversationlist_undertell.message: My name was Brenor. I came from the lands ruled by Feygard, back when its people still followed Elythara. I was taken during the rise of Garthan I, when those who held to the Light were chained and sent below the mountain. I swung this pick as a slave until the stone claimed my breath.
Oh, sorry. Please don't tell Alkapoan that I hassled you.

replies.text: Now that's the attitude I like to see.

conversationlist_undertell.message: You look down again. The ghost stands where she was before: still, watching.
You say nothing.
You look down below to the first floor and you spot a ghost.
[Talking to yourself...]

replies.text: She ran away? Was it something I said?

conversationlist_undertell.message: The silence is so rewarding.
Then we can speak briefly.

replies.text: May I look at what's here?

conversationlist_undertell.message: You don't shout.
These were stored. Not claimed.
With Anoa fallen and the last of the Kha'zaan shades dissolved into silence, the cavern finally grows still.
The darkness born in the War of Dawn loosens its grip at last, leaving only the echo of what devotion once twisted.
Words trace in my mind like smoke. You carry the scent of heartstone. You did not ask the smith to shape a weapon from it. Why?

replies.text: I chose not to have a weapon forged.
That is none of your concern.

conversationlist_undertell.message: The air trembles as Falkour lowers his gaze to the box. For a long moment he says nothing, then exhales a slow breath that stirs the dust at your feet.

This scent...old fire and fear. I remember this relic. It passed through the hands of a mortal named Varnel, long before you walked this world. He fled these caverns clutching it as though it would save him.

replies.text: Varnel? Then this box is truly ancient. Can you open it?
You knew Varnel? How old are you, Falkour?

conversationlist_undertell.message: I will not open it myself. Some seals are meant to remain unbroken by my kind. But you...perhaps it is your fate to see it undone.

I lend you this fragment of me, not for greed but for truth. Take this claw. Its edge remembers the heat of the first forge. Use it to break the seal, and only the seal. Whatever sleeps inside will not thank you for waking it.

replies.text: Thank you, Falkour. I will be careful and find a safe place in this basement to open the box.

conversationlist_undertell.message: My child, I long ago gave up on counting the days. Hidden away from the sun, I have lost track of the passing years. The world above has changed many times while I slept.

replies.text: Then you must have known much of what came before?

conversationlist_undertell.message: The dragon lowers his head once more, eyes half-closed. A single claw, blackened and gleaming, lies on the stone between you. Its warmth seeps into your hand as you pick it up.
Disturbance wakes very old hunger. I rest because it is less costly to dream than to remember. If I rise, the world will remember dragons. That is not a kindness for either party.

replies.text: I understand. I will not wake you.
I must know more. Wake yourself.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Something vast lies curled against the far wall, scales dark as coal and steam rising from its nostrils. A thought touches your mind like a hand on a bell.
The dragon lowers a claw and nudges a small trinket toward you. It gleams faintly, warm but not burning. Take it, and keep your hands gentle with fire.

replies.text: I will wear it with care.

conversationlist_undertell.message: When the Rift opened, heat buried itself in rock and memory. I came seeking shelter from the hunger of its fires. I slumbered, and the humans rose above me, shaping houses and laws in ignorance. My breath found cracks and fed a small forge. I remain because the place holds what I once escaped. I do not leave what keeps me whole.

replies.text: I will go upstairs and leave you to sleep.

conversationlist_undertell.message: The dragon settles, and the warm hush returns. Its breath is a slow tide through the stone vents. The glow above you hums like a distant hearth. You climb the steps back to the house and the smith who waits there.
Counsel is costly, yet you have already shaped your path in flame. You carry a weapon forged from my breath; what more could I give? Go now, and do not let that gift burn the world anew.
You show restraint where many would choose blade. For that, I offer a token. Take it and wear it as a reminder: heat can be a cure or a curse.
Mortal flame...yet not born of greed. Why do you disturb my rest?
Thought is older than voice. I do not rise for passing curiosity. Speak plainly, child of ash and stone.

replies.text: Nocmar said you heat the forge above. Why do you live here?
I found this ancient box sealed tight. They say only a dragon's claw can open it.
I will not wake you. I only wanted to see.

conversationlist_undertell.message: To wake is to remember. If you insist, I will stir. But remember, not all that sleeps should be coaxed to waking.

replies.text: No. I will leave you be.

conversationlist_undertell.message: You press your palm to the warm scale and whisper whatever small plea your heart can shape. The great form shifts. Steam rolls across the chamber. A low hum grows into a thought that blooms in your mind.
You woke me. You risked the old truth. Why did you do it?

replies.text: To know why you live here.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Your answer tastes of sharp iron. I ask only to mark the heart of your choice. Walk in peace if you can. I will sleep on.
The bell has not rung.
When the bell rings, the bowls are filled.
The fire must be watched. The pots must not boil dry. When the bell rings, the bowls are filled.
Those who work, eat. Those who eat return to work. The bell decides.
When the bell rings, the bowls are filled.
Tell those ingrates over in the other room that their dinner is almost ready!

replies.text: [Lie] Sure, I'll do that right now.
What still needs to be done?

conversationlist_undertell.message: There is another. A girl. She never came back here when the shades fell. Instead, she hides east of here. Probably in a corner somewhere.
Fear does not listen to truth. She made something to keep it away.
A folded coin. Copper. She believed evil could be trapped if it could not breathe.
Lost. Taken. We do not know which. Only that it never came back.
You have not forgotten her, have you?

replies.text: I am still trying to understand what happened to the talisman.

conversationlist_undertell.message: They used to gather our things. Count them. Decide what mattered.
Those above us. Those who studied fear instead of ending it.
If the talisman still exists, it will not be with the dead.
With those who believed fear could be shaped. Go to the Masters.

replies.text: Don't worry, I will take care of this for you guys.

conversationlist_undertell.message: What are you doing here? Go find that talisman and bring it to her.
She came back. We did not think she would.

replies.text: I want to speak to her.

conversationlist_undertell.message: She is here because she chose to be. Not because fear left her.

replies.text: Then let me hear it from her.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Do not mistake silence for weakness.

replies.text: You do not have to hide anymore.

conversationlist_undertell.message: It is so wonderful to finally be free of the evil that surrounded those shades...thank you Elythara!

replies.text: What?! It was thanks to me. You guys are hopeless.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Yes! Freed from the rule of those Kha'zaan shades.

replies.text: But that was not Elythara. That was me.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Listen you, we've been hiding for Elythara knows how long, and the first thing you say to us is a lie?

replies.text: But it was me, I swear to Elythara it was me.

conversationlist_undertell.message: If that is true, then maybe you could help us help someone else?
Oh thank you Elythara! We are freed at last.
Is it that mead I ordered from the tavern?

replies.text: No, it's not mead. That's the last thing that you need.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Well, then I don't want it. Go get me some more mead from the lovely barkeeper, Bela.

replies.text: No. I have a potion that will make you recover. Shannal's ghost has asked that you drink it. Now, here, drink it.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Shannal? That name sounds familiar to me, yet distant to me.
While leaning his head back, he downs the potion in one gulp...amazing.
Now I remember; it was horrible. [weeping]

replies.text: There...there...Shannal's ghost told me to tell you she's at peace.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Thank you! To have passed her life at that place, kidnapped against her will, away from her husband and kids...
Well, let me get on with life...I seem to have made a mess of myself.

replies.text: Worry not, as restitution, Shannal made the kidnapper's descendant, Benbyr pay up. Here's {5000} gold. Keep it and yourself safe.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Thank you! Please ask Bela to keep them safe till Rain, oh by the way, that's my name, gets over this hangover. I need new clothes. So I will take 150 gold and visit the merchant. Please give Bela the remaining {4850} gold.
Let me meet the merchant and then return. Please go meet Bela.
Among the dust and bindings, something dull catches the light. It is copper. Folded. Out of place.
It rests untouched, as if waiting.
You grab the coin off the shelf.
You notice some fresh footprints in the dirt.

replies.text: They are of no interest to me. Time to go back to my plans.
I think I should follow them.

conversationlist_undertell.message: "The Ritual of Five Aspects"? No, I can't say that I have. The name sounds ominous though. You're welcome to look through the shelves if you wish. Just be careful with the older scrolls - they crumble if you breathe too hard on them.

replies.text: Thank you. I'll take a look around.

conversationlist_undertell.message: A locked box? No, I've never noticed one. I've been in charge of these archives for years, but I suppose some things manage to hide from even the most watchful eyes. I'm afraid I don't have a key for anything like that.

replies.text: Do you know who might have the key?
That's all right. I'll figure something out.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Hmm...the church keeps spare keys in the rectory upstairs, I think. You might ask Skylenar - he oversees most of what's stored down here. But please, don't break anything. Those boxes could be older than Remgard itself.

replies.text: I'll ask him. Thank you, Gwendolyn.

conversationlist_undertell.message: This heartstone radiates unbearable heat, glowing faintly with the breath of the Rift itself. The surface scorches at the slightest touch, making it impossible to lift or carry.

replies.text: [thinking aloud] Maybe Unnmir knows what I should do next?
OK, it's time to see if Unnmir is right! [place the block of Galmore ice on the stone]
I have a great idea! Maybe this block of ice that I found on Galmore Mountain can be used to cool the heartstone?

conversationlist_undertell.message: Before you rests a massive, glowing stone, pulsing faintly with an inner light. The shape and markings leave little doubt: this is the heartstone you've been seeking.

You set the block of Galmore ice onto the blazing heartstone. At once, a violent hiss erupts, filling the chamber with steam. The ice cracks and splinters, melting faster than your eyes can follow until nothing remains but a shallow puddle on the stone floor. Where the ice once lay, the heartstone has cooled enough for you to grip it safely. You lift it from its resting place, its weight heavy with ancient power, its heat now steady but bearable. At last, the prize is yours.
Where the scorching hot heartstone once lay, now lies only the melted remains of the once unmeltable Galmore Mountain ice block.
If you ever leave while I am talking to you again, I will end your life. Understood?

[While pointing its finger in your direction.]
You! How did you get past our army?
We are "masters", not "bosses". And yes, there are five of us.
Well, currently there are only four of us masters. We are not complete.

replies.text: "Complete"? What is that supposed to mean?

conversationlist_undertell.message: Oh, a real live human here? I don't believe it.
She reaches out and pinches your arm to confirm that you are in fact human.
No, I'm sorry, but you don't need to rest here. You need to experience this place more before you decide whether or not you want to get cozy with a dark pillow.

replies.text: What is that supposed to mean?

conversationlist_undertell.message: For your protection, you can not rest in our beds...right now anyway.

replies.text: So I can later? If so, when is 'later'?

conversationlist_undertell.message: When you have a better understanding of this place.
The Kha'zaan are no more, thanks to you. So yes, you are free to sleep in any of the desirable beds.
What brings you to me now?

replies.text: I would really like to rest here now.

conversationlist_undertell.message: I am. Born Lethgar, died Lethgar, and it seems I am doomed to remain so long after any of it mattered.

replies.text: I have seen a statue near Brightport that bears the Lethgar name. Do you know of it?

conversationlist_undertell.message: Near Brightport? Child, my people never reached that far north. We were here, beneath this mountain. We built, we dug, we died. The northern lands were not ours to know.

replies.text: Then why would a statue carry your people's name up there?

conversationlist_undertell.message: I cannot say with any certainty.

But the Kazaul were never above reshaping the truth to suit their purposes. They renamed places, rewrote histories, left their marks upon things that were never theirs. A statue bearing our name in a land we never walked...that is not honor. That is confusion, and confusion was always their sharpest tool.

replies.text: You think the Kazaul put it there to mislead people?

conversationlist_undertell.message: I think the Kazaul are ancient, patient, and very skilled at making the living doubt what stands before them. A name here, a stone there. Given enough time, even a carefully placed lie begins to look like history.
Good. You should be troubled. It means you have not yet stopped thinking for yourself. Now, was there something else you needed?

replies.text: I would really like to rest here now.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Ah...so some of his scales remain. Then it's true - not all the old stories were lies.

Long before the Rift tore this place apart, a great serpent of flame slept beneath the stone. Some said his breath warmed the forges. Others feared he kept the mountain alive when it should have died.

replies.text: Did you ever see him yourself?
Maybe those scales are just from a monster, not a dragon.

conversationlist_undertell.message: No. By the time I was born, he was already legend. We mined the heat, not the truth. But sometimes...the walls breathed, and the stones glowed like coals in a hearth. That was enough for me.

replies.text: Then maybe the legend was real.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Heh...maybe. But the Kazaul feared that heat. They sealed off the deepest tunnels where the warmth was strongest. Even they left it undisturbed - and that tells you something, doesn't it?
If he still lives, child, best let him sleep. Some fires burn long after they should have gone out.
The Heartstone? Don't speak that name down here.

replies.text: Why? What's so dangerous about it?

conversationlist_undertell.message: We dug near its glow once. The air turned to ash, and our skin blistered from the inside. When we struck it, the light screamed...and then the tunnels fell quiet forever.

replies.text: That sounds like a story meant to scare miners.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Not cursed. Hungry. It drinks the warmth of living things. Leave it buried, or it will remember the taste of us.
We thought that too. Then the ground split, and the glow swallowed our camp. Don't go looking for it, child.
Oh, Shannal! She's my girlfriend, you know?
Well...I want her to be. I love that woman.
No way! Even after so many many years, I'm still terrified to tell her.

replies.text: Wimp. Girls don't bite, well some do I guess. Good luck with that.

conversationlist_undertell.message: What? A live human, down here? How? Why?

replies.text: I found these ash covered dragon scales. Was this place once home to a dragon?
I'm here for the Heartstone, of course!

conversationlist_undertell.message: Child, I can't even remember my own name. Go into the other room over there and talk to Durnan.
A human, here?

replies.text: Shannal let me in after I performed so really hard work for her.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Why are you here?

replies.text: I am wondering why you guys are safe here?
Do you remember anyone named Varnel?

conversationlist_undertell.message: Huh?

replies.text: What I mean is, why do the liches not attack you guys?

conversationlist_undertell.message: Oh, that's because they are incapable of climbing stairs.

replies.text: Oh, I never thought of that.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Names are comforts. They make old things feel small.
It was placed where power would grow teeth and learn to walk.
Some tools were made for rule. Others were made to be watched.

replies.text: So this crystal is a tool?

conversationlist_undertell.message: We no longer shape the world so openly. But what was shaped does not forget the hand that shaped it.

replies.text: Then what should I do with it?

conversationlist_undertell.message: Keep it close. Power that is not understood still teaches obedience.
A child's charm. Folded copper. Fear pretending to be faith.
Yes. And fear is the purest lens for understanding devotion. We examined it. Measured what clung to it.
That belief leaves an imprint. Not divine. Not benign. Something old listens when it is named.
Names are doors. Some were spoken long before your kind learned prayer. The Kazaul understood this well.

replies.text: You are saying the Shadow answers to them.

conversationlist_undertell.message: I am saying echoes do not choose who repeats them.
Sealed. Labeled. Forgotten. As most inconvenient things are.

replies.text: You want me to retrieve it.

conversationlist_undertell.message: I want it removed from circulation. Belief is dangerous when it spreads without instruction.
In the lower records. Where discarded faith is kept for study, not mercy.

[The Master's hollow eyes flare briefly with dim blue fire.]
You hold the Ritual of Five Aspects, mortal. But its meaning lies beyond your grasp. Only Thalen, our brother of Knowledge, can speak the words. Seek him where the thoughts of the dead still linger.

replies.text: Thalen? What will he do with it?

conversationlist_undertell.message: He will guide your unlearned hands. He alone can draw the pattern that binds the Five. Without him, the ritual is only ink on lost parchment.
[With a terrified expression on his face] Oh those? Yeah, you don't want to go past those. Past them is the entrance to Undertell.

replies.text: Oh, that's how to get to Undertell?! How do I get past those barricades?

conversationlist_undertell.message: To enter Undertell, you need to talk to my friend Shannal, she has just come to spend a day at the beach. Shannal is the guardian ghost who controls passage to Undertell. Only she can remove (and put back) the barriers you see now.

replies.text: You, Shannal, maybe other ghosts, you all sure can affect the world of the living. Why does Shannal control the passage to Undertell?

conversationlist_undertell.message: She has seen horrors, as have the rest of us. It moved something inside her. When she came back as a ghost, that change gave her the ability to barricade the entrance, which she has. Go see her.
The Fifth breathes again. The world will tremble...as it once did.
A slow rumble of laughter escapes the Master's skeletal chest.
You reek of intrusion, mortal. The stench of the living offends this place.

replies.text: I mean no harm. Who...what are you?

conversationlist_undertell.message: I am Morvath, the Kazaul master of wrath.
The cavern trembles with wrath. A heavy voice fills your mind.
You've not been to Brimhaven and had to deal with him?
Oh, then you must do so first as I need you to understand the man before you can accomplish what it is that I need from you.
A parrying weapon it is. This will hinder your attacker's weapon.
It is done. The weapon cools beneath my hand. Take it, and guard it well. There will never be another like it.

replies.text: Thank you. I will guard it.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Wait! Come over and talk with me before you rudely enter my basement without asking first.

replies.text: Oh, right. Where are my manners?

conversationlist_undertell.message: Meet me at the white house south of town. The lock will no longer bar your entry. I must prepare the forge and make certain the place is safe.

Below this floor lies more than stone and ash. A dragon slumbers beneath, bound by the magic of this place since long before my time. Its breath seeps upward through cracks in the rock, feeding the forge with endless heat.

Even when no fire burns, the stones themselves glow with its warmth. The light you see spilling from under the door isn't flame - it's the dragon's breath, alive and eternal. I sealed the forge years ago when Geomyr banned heartsteel, but the glow never faded. It's as if the creature dreams in embers.

replies.text: That explains the glow under the door?
A dragon? You've been living above a dragon?

conversationlist_undertell.message: Aye. The forge's light is fed by its breath, not by any flame of mine.
Aye. Respect it and it respects us. Disturb it and you wake things that cannot be bargained with. That is why I will work here and not in my shop.
Now, you brought one cooled heartstone. We can forge only one item from it.
There you are. The forge has been lit. Truth be told, it never truly dies, not while the thing below sleeps. Come, sit by the anvil if you can steady your hands.
Heartsteel answers to shape and intent. Tell me which form you demand and I will pour the heartstone's essence into that blade or head. Choose wisely; only one may be made from this stone.

replies.text: Where would I find a dragon in this age?

conversationlist_undertell.message: It was before my time, but the records say it came from one of my predecessors, the first priest to serve under the banner of the Shadow here. He noted that it was delivered to him by travelers claiming to have found it among the ruins to the west.

replies.text: Ruins to the west, perhaps where Varnel perished.

You carefully sift through the remains...

You step back toward the table, aware now of how deliberately the crown was positioned and decide to return it.
You step back toward the table, aware now of how deliberately the crown was positioned and decide to return it.
You return the crown to its place at the center of the table. The room settles into its intended stillness.
There's nothing left to do here without the crown.
Resting alone upon a stone table, lies a crown. It is not shelved, nor sealed away, but left exposed, as if meant to be examined again and again.
As you lift the crown from the table, the space around it feels suddenly incomplete, as though the room was arranged with this absence in mind.
Much to your dismay, the chest  is empty.
A ghostly miner leans heavily on a spectral pickaxe, using it as a cane. His faded eyes glimmer faintly in the warm air of the tunnels.
Durnan...once of the Lethgar. This pick carried me through life, now it props up what's left of me.

replies.text: Do you remember anyone named Varnel?
I have to go now, but it was nice talking to you.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Varnel...the scribe. He was no miner, yet they made him dig beside us. Always scribbling between swings. Said he wrote words to keep them from the Masters.

replies.text: Do you know where he went?

conversationlist_undertell.message: East, through the lower caverns. He spoke of a town where the sun still touched the Sutdover River. Said he would hide among its people until the voices of the Masters faded from his dreams.
If you find what he carried...bury it deep, far from here. The chains broke too late for us. Now...let me rest.
A little dazed and a lot confused, you pick yourself up off of the ground only to find that you are no longer in Undertell.
The shade did not try to kill you. It simply removed you.

replies.text: [talking to yourself] I guess I should talk to Anoa?

conversationlist_undertell.message: A lot annoyed, you pick yourself and your stuff off of the ground and accept the trip to Undertell is needed once again.
The shades do not fight. They just keep sending you away.

replies.text: [talking to yourself] Anoa better know the answer!

conversationlist_undertell.message: A little annoyed, you pick yourself up off of the ground only to find that you are once again not in Undertell.
Once again, displacement occured.

replies.text: [talking to yourself] I guess I should talk to Anoa? Maybe he will be more helpful than before?

conversationlist_undertell.message: You've come back to visit me?

replies.text: Yes and I am really hoping that you can help me! I found the heartstone, but it burns to the touch. I cannot carry it.
I don't want to hold you from your busy day. I will leave now.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Too hot, you say? Hah, that makes sense. The heartstone has been sitting near that cursed rift for centuries, soaking up its heat. No man alive could carry it as it is. But there is a way. Back when I still walked the high trails of Galmore, I heard of a rare ice found only near the mountain's peak...

They called it "Galmore Ice". Unlike any common frost, it does not melt in your hand or in the lowlands. Only the hottest fire, or something born of the Rift itself, can turn it to water. If you can get your hands on a block of it, place it upon the heartstone. The ice will cool the stone, and in melting, make it safe enough to carry.
Climbing to that height is no small task, and the beasts there guard it jealously. But if you truly want to see heartsteel reforged, you'll need to brave the peak. No one else can do this but you.

replies.text: Great. Thanks. That helps a lot.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Unnmir leans back, shaking his head.
And?

replies.text: And he had this book. [show the Undertell history book] I was hoping for your insight.

conversationlist_undertell.message: If that book matters, someone in Fallhaven should know why.
Someone with a lot of books, I presume.

replies.text: OK, you don't know then. Thanks anyway.

conversationlist_undertell.message: A broad, luminous stone sits half-embedded in the cavern floor. Warm light swirls beneath its surface, shifting like embers stirred by an unseen breeze.
Its size and presence leave little doubt - this must be what you came for.
Before you lays a stone strikingly similiar to the one you already have, but this one is unrefined and can't be moved.
As you lean down to place the stone, a sharp crack echoes through the cavern behind you...
You flinch and the heartstone slips from your hands and shatters across the ground.
Where the luminous stone once laid, now lays only the stone's ground impression.
I felt the pulse the moment it stirred. Death is restless again. I welcome the silence no more.
Vaelzahr's voice is a rasping whisper.
Mortality remembers pain. Even now, your blood knows me.
The walls pulse faintly, as if the stone itself had veins. A deep, rasping voice speaks within your chest.
You arrive carrying an echo that is not yours.
Your kind drags history behind it, even when it thinks it walks alone.

replies.text: You are being vague on purpose

conversationlist_undertell.message: You carry what your kind calls an Oegyth crystal.

replies.text: So you know what it is?

conversationlist_undertell.message: This spot is just as good as any other to unlock this box.
After placing the claw in the keyhole, the box lights up red and crumbles in your hand. Revealing an ancient parcment in your hands.

The air thickens with heat as you descend the narrow stone steps. Each breath feels heavier than the last, carrying the faint taste of smoke and iron. At the bottom lies a vast, shadowed chamber, lit only by the dull orange pulse of fire leaking through cracks in the stone floor.
Something enormous stirs at the edge of sight - scales blackened by soot, breath slow and deep. The warmth here doesn't come from any forge...it comes from him.
A voice echoes inside your mind, as soft as the crackle of a distant flame.
Oh, a human child, here? How did that come about?

replies.text: Shannal let me through. Can I ask you, why do you look different than the others here?

conversationlist_undertell.message: Oh no. Just as I feared.
Like I feared. He was up to no good.
Saki seemed kind, even gentle. But there were inconsistencies in his stories. I assumed they came from the loss of memory that follows death. I was wrong.
Saki was no follower of Elythara. He sought to absorb the spirits of the Elytharan mages and draw power from them. I fear he serves the Kazaul, and he must be stopped.

replies.text: By we, do you mean me?

conversationlist_undertell.message: Unfortunately, yes.
Saki is trying to flee Undertell. Find him, defeat him, and recover the soul pearls and anything else he carries. Bring them back here.

replies.text: Looks like no one can be trusted.

conversationlist_undertell.message: In the end, trust is still required. Without it, we would already be lost.
It is not ordinary ore. Heartstone drinks the breath of the Rift and holds it. They wanted it.
Long ago, the first King of Nor City, Garthan of House Houdart, sent men into Galmore to pry at the mountain. They prized what they pulled from the mountain, though few ever speak plainly of why.

replies.text: What did they want it for?
Thank you. That is enough for now.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Power and profit are plain reasons. Old families in Nor City desired advantage. That is what men call progress and what others call cost. Remember this when you carry the stone.
This is what happened when he died [point to the man at the table]. That is what happened when they died [pointing east]. It's all very personal.
Oh, sorry, child. I am not knowledgeable about such things.
You carry questions like coins. Ask them, child.

replies.text: What is this heartstone everyone speaks of?
I found a book about Undertell. Do you know it?
I found these coins [showing Ysrine the rare coins] here in Undertell. Are you familiar with them?

conversationlist_undertell.message: Good - you're back...
but unfortunately you've come empty handed. How did you manage to drop them on the way back?

replies.text: Don't be so judgemental. They are really heavy, so I didn't want to carry them around with me.

conversationlist_undertell.message: and you have brought the Soul pearls.

replies.text: What do I do with the Soul pearls?

conversationlist_undertell.message: Go get them and bring them back here!

Besides keeping them away from those Kazaul Masters? I do not know yet. Powerful they are - they could perhaps bring Elythara back, help her re-establish her Dominion on Dhayavar.
Those Pearls might be the key to bring Elythara back, and balance out the power of the five Masters. Let the wisdom of your travels guide you.
This is no time to be fooling around. Please get those pearls back.
Thank you! It's because of you that we are rid of the remnants of the Kha'zaan. On that note, there's someone here to meet you.
Here, on my left.
Then you walk a quieter road than most.
Written histories come easily to stone and steel. They are less kind to breath, fear, and hunger.

replies.text: It feels like something is missing.
A book collector from Fallhaven asked me to listen to the ghosts of Undertell.

conversationlist_undertell.message: What is measured can be counted. What is endured must be remembered. Undertell has little love for the latter.

replies.text: You think the book leaves things out?

conversationlist_undertell.message: Those who suffered here were tools, not witnesses. Tools are used. Witnesses are avoided.

replies.text: I should keep that in mind.

conversationlist_undertell.message: The dead are accustomed to being spoken for. Few think to listen instead. Undertell remembers those who do.
You have spoken with one of them, haven't you? Their words cling to you. Be careful what promises you keep down here.

replies.text: They spoke of balance. I am not sure what they meant.
I did. Do you know what they want?
I wanted to talk about something else. The Kha'zaan to be specific.
I wanted to talk about something else. The Kha'zaan to be specific.
I found a book about Undertell. Do you know it?
Actually, I want to talk about Saki.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Balance can mean many things. For them, it once meant chains and silence. Listen closely, but never forget they speak for themselves, not for you.

replies.text: I will keep that in mind.

conversationlist_undertell.message: No one truly knows what the Masters want anymore. Even they may have forgotten. Just remember this: "truth and deceit sound much the same when spoken by the dead".

replies.text: You sound like you don't trust them.

conversationlist_undertell.message: Trust is for the living. Down here, it's better to doubt everything, even me.
Mortality's coil burns anew. The flame remembers what it once devoured.
The embers within Zaroth's hollow ribs flicker violently.
Flame does not merely destroy. It remembers what it consumes. Tell me, traveler, do you fear what endures through fire?

replies.text: I fear nothing born of heat or ash.

conversationlist_undertell.message: The chamber flickers with living fire, casting shadows that dance across Zaroth's scorched form. His eyes burn like twin embers as he studies you.
Yes, yes you are and a foolhardy one at that.
Carrying the very same weapon Geomyr banned?

strings.skill_longdescription_armor_prof_shield: Increase damage resistance by %1$,d per skill level while having a shield or parrying weapon equipped.
strings.skill_longdescription_armor_prof_unarmor: While fighting without having any piece of armor equipped, gain %1$,d block chance per skill level. Items made of cloth are not considered as being armor.
strings.skill_longdescription_armor_prof_light: For every skill level, increases the block chance of every piece of light armor being worn by %1$,d %% of their original block chances. Light armors include leather, light metal and hide armors.
strings.skill_longdescription_armor_prof_heavy: For every skill level, increases the block chance of every piece of heavy armor being worn by %1$,d %% of their original block chances. Pieces of heavy armor have their movement penalties reduced by %2$,d %% per skill level, their attack speed penalties reduced by %3$,d %% per skill level, and their item use cost penalties reduced by %4$,d %% per skill level. Heavy armors include metal armors, chain mail and plate mail.
strings.skill_longdescription_fightstyle_dualwie:
Gives benefits when fighting with two weapons at the same time, one in the main hand and one in the off-hand.

Without this skill, only %1$,d %% of a weapon's qualities may be used when equipped in the off-hand. This includes attack chance, critical skill, damage potential and block chance. Without this skill, attack cost (AP cost) of making an attack is the sum of the attack cost of the main weapon and that of the weapon used in the off-hand. The lower of both damage modifiers will be used.

With one level of this skill, %2$,d %% of the off-hand's weapon's qualities may be used, and the attack cost is the highest attack cost of both weapons plus %3$,d %% of the lowest attack cost of both weapons. The average of both damage modifiers will be used.

With two levels of this skill, %4$,d %% of the off-hand's weapon's qualities may be used, and the attack cost equals the highest of the attack costs of the two equipped weapons. The highest damage modifier will be used.
strings.skill_longdescription_fightstyle_2hand:
Gives benefits when using weapons that require both hands to wield, such as two-handed swords, greataxes or giant hammers.

Every skill level increases damage potential of two-handed weapons with %1$,d %% of the original damage potential.
strings.skill_longdescription_fightstyle_weapon_:
Gives benefits when fighting with a weapon in the main hand and having a shield or parrying weapon equipped in the off-hand.

Every skill level increases the attack chance of weapons in the main hand with %1$,d %% of their original attack chances, and the block chance of shields or parrying weapons by %2$,d %% of their original block chances.
strings.skill_longdescription_fightstyle_unarmed:
While fighting without having any piece of armor equipped and without using a weapon or shield, gain %1$,d attack chance, %2$,d block chance, %3$,d damage resistance and increase the maximum damage by %4$,d per skill level. The skill also gives a critical multiplier of 1 plus 0.%5$,d per level.

Items made of cloth are not considered as being armor.
strings.skill_longdescription_specialization_dua: Increases the attack chance of both wielded weapons by an additional %1$,d %% of their original attack chances, in addition to the benefits given by the weapon style skill. The block chances of both wielded weapons are also increased by %2$,d %% of their original block chances.
strings.skill_longdescription_specialization_2ha: Increases damage potential of two-handed weapons by an additional %1$,d %% of the original damage potential, in addition to the benefits given by the weapon style skill. The attack chances of two-handed weapons are also increased by %2$,d %% of their original attack chances.
strings.skill_longdescription_specialization_wea: Increases both attack chances and damage potential of weapons in the main hand. The attack chance is increased by %1$,d %% of the original attack chance, and the damage potential is increased by %2$,d %% of the original damage potential.
strings.skill_longdescription_weapon_prof_pole: For each skill level, increases attack chance when using pole weapons by %1$,d %% of the item's base attack chance, increases block chance by %2$,d %% of the item's base block chance, and increases critical skill by %3$,d %% of the item's base critical skill.
strings.preferences_ui_show_quickslots_when_tool: Show quickslots when toolbox is opened
Makes the quickslot buttons be displayed as soon as the toolbox is opened
strings.startscreen_incompatible_savegames: This is a development version of Andor's Trail. Savegames produced by this version are incompatible with the release version.
strings.startscreen_non_release_version: This is a prerelease version of Andor's Trail. Savegames produced by this version might not be compatible with the release version.
strings.preferences_ui_use_localized_resources: Use translation of interface and content, where available. (requires restart)
strings.change_locale_requires_restart: Changing locale requires restart. Andor's Trail has been closed.
strings.change_theme_requires_restart: Changing UI theme requires restart. Andor's Trail has been closed.
strings.storage_permissions_mandatory: Access to storage is mandatory for Andor's Trail to handle saved games and worldmap. Closing Andor's Trail.
strings.skill_longdescription_spore_immunity: Permanently prevents monster attacks from inflicting the "Spore poisoning" status effect.
strings.preferences_movement_dpad_transparency: If the virtual d-pad is enabled, this setting determines how transparent it should be.
strings.loadsave_export_downloads_info:
Savegames will be placed in system %1$s folder under the '%2$s' subfolder.

A file manager app may be used to copy the files to an external device or cloud storage.
strings.preferences_export_to_downloads_summary: If enabled, a different method will be used to export savegames directly to the system Downloads folder. This may be required on some devices.

preferences_display_loot: Show loot dialog box when finding items
Show notification only when finding items
preferences_display_overwrite_savegame_e: Only show when overwriting a different playername
